Where deeds are recorded

The City's Department of Records is the recorder of deeds for Philadelphia County. It sits in City Hall, and the main line is (215) 686-2262. One office takes deeds, mortgages and other real estate documents for every neighborhood, because the city and county share the same borders.

Individuals file by mail or at the counter. Counter service needs an appointment, booked by email to appointments.records@phila.gov, and recording hours are weekdays from 8 a.m. until 3:30 p.m. Mailed documents go to City Hall, Room 111, 1400 John F. Kennedy Blvd., Philadelphia, PA 19107, along with a stamped, self-addressed envelope so the original can come back. Anyone dropping off three or more documents leaves them to be picked up later.

Title companies and businesses usually record electronically through Simplifile, CSC eRecording or ePN, and those filings are paid by ACH.

What a deed needs before it is accepted

Documents that miss the office's formatting and content rules are rejected, so a title company or lawyer normally prepares the deed. The Department advises against drafting one yourself and recommends title insurance.

  • White 8.5 by 11 inch paper, typed in 10 point black ink, one side only.
  • A 3 inch top margin on page one with the "Prepared by" and "Return to" details at the left, and 1 inch margins elsewhere.
  • A date, the typed names of every party, and signatures and a notary acknowledgment that match those names.
  • For a Philadelphia property, a metes and bounds description and the street address.
  • A signed, certified grantee address on deeds, mortgages and assignments.
  • The full consideration, with numbers that match the written amount.
  • The Philadelphia Real Estate Transfer Tax Certificate in duplicate and the Pennsylvania Realty Transfer Tax Statement of Value, plus the tax unless the transfer is exempt.

Recording fees

A standard deed costs $278.75 on the current schedule, and a few special cases carry lower fees. These are the charges homeowners run into most.

Department of Records fees for common documents
DocumentFee
Deed$278.75
Deed, deceased spouse or partner$43.75
Deed, miscellaneous$263.75
Mortgage$248.75
Assignment of mortgage$246.75
Release of mortgage or satisfaction$231.75
Power of attorney$96.50

Payment can be cash, a money order, a business or certified check, or Visa, Mastercard, Discover or American Express. Cards add a 3.5 percent convenience fee, and personal checks are refused. Taxes and fees need separate checks: the state tax payable to the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, and the City tax and recording fees payable to the City of Philadelphia. A surviving spouse named on the deed can have part of the fee waived, and military discharge papers are recorded and copied free.

Philadelphia realty transfer tax

The total rate is 4.578 percent of the sale price: 3.578 percent for the City plus 1 percent for the Commonwealth. The City portion rose from 3.278 percent on July 1, 2025, and the City says the increase pays for affordable housing programs.

The tax is owed when the deed is presented for recording, and the City allows up to 30 days to pay after the property is acquired. Buyer and seller usually divide it at closing, yet the City can collect the whole amount from either one, so buyers want it paid at settlement. Misstating the transaction or never recording it can bring a penalty of up to 50 percent of the tax.

When no price exists, as with a gift or foreclosure, the tax runs on a computed value: the assessed value times the state's Common Level Ratio, then times the rate. Most transfers among spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings are exempt, with documents required for each claim.

Do inherited or estate-sold homes pay transfer tax?

It depends on how title moves. A transfer under a will can be exempt, but tax is due if mortgages, liens or debts on the home are still unpaid at the time of transfer. A home bought from an estate is not exempt. If a will leaves a property to several heirs and one buys out the others, tax is owed on that purchase.

  • Heirs who keep the property usually record a deed from the estate and show the family relationship.
  • Heirs who sell record the deed to the buyer, and that sale carries the full transfer tax.
  • If title is still in a deceased owner's name, ask the title company which estate papers it needs before it will insure the sale.

How to pay the transfer tax

There are three ways to pay, and the title company usually picks the first or second.

  • Online through the Philadelphia Tax Center, by logging in or using the Letter ID printed at the top of the bill.
  • In person, when the deed is filed with the Department of Records.
  • By mail, with two copies of the City certificate, one copy of the state Statement of Value form, and three certified checks: one for the recording fee, one for the City tax and one for the Commonwealth tax.

The tax reaches more than sales. Deeds, leases of 30 years or longer, easements, life estates, entity transfers and transfers of 75 percent or more of a real estate company all trigger it.

Older land records

The Department also runs the City Archives. Copies of deeds from 1683 to 1955 cost $2 a page, mortgages from 1748 to 1963 are also $2 a page, and a search of deeds, mortgages and other land records is $20 an hour with a $20 minimum. A plot plan copy is $10, and a certified copy is $2 per document. These records come in handy when an old gap in ownership needs tracing before a sale.

Where recording fits in a Philadelphia sale

Recording comes last in the closing sequence, and the title company usually files it. The seller signs the deed, the title company or buyer assembles the transfer tax certificates, pays the tax and fee, and files the package with the Department of Records.

Ahead of that, the title search looks at property tax, water and sewer balances, since each can sit as a lien. A seller with tax or lien problems can still close if the payoff is arranged in advance. A cash buyer working through a title company can handle the transfer tax split and the recording as part of one closing.

A seller's preparation list

Most of the work lands on the title company, but a seller can save time by doing a few things early.

  1. Confirm who will file: the title company by electronic recording, or you by mail or with an appointment at City Hall.
  2. If you are filing by mail, prepare the stamped, self-addressed envelope for the original and send the package to Room 111.
  3. Ask the title company how the transfer tax will be split and whether any exemption applies.
  4. Make sure checks are separate: the Commonwealth tax on one, and the City tax and recording fees on another. Personal checks are refused.
  5. Clear up any tax, water or sewer balance before the closing date, or have the payoff arranged in advance.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Which office files my Philadelphia deed?

The Department of Records in City Hall, Room 111, either by mail or in person with an appointment. Businesses can also record electronically through a third party vendor.

What fee applies to a standard Philadelphia deed?

The deed fee is $278.75, plus the realty transfer tax unless the transfer is exempt. A deed for a deceased spouse or partner is $43.75. Check the current fee schedule before you send payment.

What is the realty transfer tax rate in Philadelphia?

It is 4.578 percent, made up of 3.578 percent for the City and 1 percent for the state. It falls due at recording, and the City allows up to 30 days to pay.

Can I record a deed without a lawyer?

It is possible, but the Department advises against preparing a deed yourself. Use a lawyer, title company or other professional, and consider title insurance.

Does the Department of Records take personal checks?

No. It accepts cash, money orders, business or certified checks, and cards with a 3.5 percent fee. Taxes and fees go on separate checks.

Where to record a deed

In Allegheny County the Division of Real Estate does the recorder’s work. It is in Room 101 of the County Office Building, 542 Forbes Avenue, Pittsburgh, and it also collects the state and local transfer taxes.

The counter is open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Phone 412-350-4636 and choose Option 2. Most documents can be eRecorded online, so a title company in another city can submit a deed without anyone walking into Room 101.

Most sellers never visit the counter. The title agent prepares the deed, records it, and sends the tax and fee payments the division requires.

Recording fees

A deed costs $200.00 to record, and so does a mortgage, under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. Large documents add charges only when they pass 30 parcels or 30 indexed names.

Allegheny County recording fees effective January 1, 2026
Document typeStandard fee
Deed and deed related documents$200.00
Mortgage and mortgage related documents$200.00
Power of attorney$50.00
Notary public bond and commission$80.00
Financial statement$175.00
Military service dischargeNo fee

Each parcel past 30 on a deed adds $10.00, and each indexed name past 30 adds $5.00. Deed related documents include leases, rights of way, declarations of trust, oil and gas documents and sewage permits, all at the same $200.00.

Transfer tax rates

The tax runs from 2% to 5% of the price depending on where the house is, and 1% of that goes to the state. The rest goes to the municipality and the school district that cover the property.

The division collects every layer at recording, with one check for transfer tax and a second check for the recording fee. The county’s own examples show the spread:

  • A house in Shaler Township pays 1% to the state, 0.5% to the township and 0.5% to Shaler Area School District, for 2% in total.
  • A house in the City of Pittsburgh pays 1% to the state, 3% to the city and 1% to Pittsburgh School District, for 5% in total.

On a real sale that gap is large, so ask the closing agent for the exact municipal and school rates before the settlement statement is final.

When no price appears on the deed, or when an exemption applies, a Statement of Value on Pennsylvania form REV-183 is required. Certain family transfers can skip the form if the deed carries a sentence explaining the relationship. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, at 717-783-8104, handles exemption questions.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Allegheny County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deed formatting rules

Type the deed in black ink on white or manila sheets, 8 1/2 by 11 inches or 8 1/2 by 14 inches, in a font of at least 10 points. Continuous paper is rejected.

  • Leave a one inch margin at the top of the first page for the certification stamp.
  • Print a name and a full address with zip code in the Record and Mail to area, outside that top margin.
  • Handwriting is limited to signatures, acknowledgments and a few listed exceptions.
  • Keep out tape, glue, staples, correction fluid and highlighting.
  • Double-sided pages are fine, though each side that carries text counts as a separate page for the fee.

The Certificate of Residence has its own formatting rule, and the county publishes content requirements for each document type separately.

Paying recording fees

In person, the counter takes cash, a business check, a money order or a cashier’s check. Personal checks, debit cards and credit cards are refused.

Firms that record often can open a draw down account in the office during business hours, which saves a trip with a check each time. Online payment is available for eRecorded filings, and the county posts a separate sheet for copies and their fees.

If you see an unfamiliar deed or mortgage filed against your property, the county has a web form for reporting suspected deed or mortgage fraud.

Common level ratio and your deed

The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue issues a new Common Level Ratio factor for each county every year, effective July 1, and the Division of Real Estate links to it from its transfer tax page. It sits beside the Statement of Value, so a filer working on a gift or low-price deed sees both together.

The county’s appeal board uses 49.3% as the ratio for the 2027 tax year. A figure near 49% tells you that county assessments, frozen to a 2012 base year, run well below current market prices. Ask the closing agent which figure belongs on the Statement of Value before you sign the deed.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Allegheny County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Housing in Allegheny County

The county covers 745 square miles, and the Allegheny and Monongahela rivers meet at Downtown Pittsburgh to form the Ohio. With 130 municipalities, it has more local governments than any other county in Pennsylvania, and neighboring municipalities can carry different transfer tax rates.

Population is 1,225,035 as of July 2025, with 614,484 housing units. About 65.2% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $227,600. Roughly 35% of units are renter occupied, which matters when you own a duplex or a house with tenants in place.

Checklist before the deed is recorded

  1. Confirm the municipality and school district, since those two set most of the transfer tax.
  2. Review the deed against the formatting rules above so the division does not reject it.
  3. Decide who pays transfer tax. Grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable for it, so settle the split in writing.
  4. Choose eRecording or hand delivery, and for hand delivery plan on a business check, cashier’s check, money order or cash.

Buyers of rental houses have a second step. Under Act 29 of 2026, a new owner of non-owner-occupied real estate must send contact details to the county’s chief assessor within 30 days of purchase, and a knowingly false filing can bring a fine of up to $500. If you are handing a tenant-occupied house to an investor, you can mention that duty to the buyer.

What a cash sale changes at the counter

Nothing about the recording changes when the buyer pays cash. The deed still needs correct formatting, a transfer tax check and a fee check. What goes away is the lender’s paperwork, so your closing may move faster. If you still have a mortgage, ask your title agent to confirm the payoff and the recording of the release so the public record is clean afterward.

Frequently asked questions

What is the standard recording fee for a deed in Allegheny County?

It is $200.00 for a deed and for a mortgage under the fee sheet effective January 1, 2026. Parcels beyond 30 add $10.00 each and indexed names beyond 30 add $5.00 each.

Does Allegheny County take personal checks or cards at the recording counter?

No. The Division of Real Estate does not accept personal checks, debit cards or credit cards. It takes cash, business checks, money orders, cashier's checks and draw down accounts, and online payment exists for eRecorded filings.

Why is the transfer tax so different between Pittsburgh and the suburbs?

The 1% state share is constant, while the municipal and school district shares change by location. Shaler Township totals 2% and the City of Pittsburgh totals 5%.

Can a deed be recorded without visiting Room 101?

Yes, most documents can be eRecorded online. For hand delivery, the address is 542 Forbes Avenue, Room 101, and the counter keeps weekday hours.

Does a military discharge cost anything to record in Allegheny County?

No. Military service discharge papers, street or alley vacations and ordinances are listed with no recording fee.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326

Selling in Montgomery County?

Where Montgomery County records a deed

Deeds for Montgomery County go to the Recorder of Deeds on the third floor of One Montgomery Plaza, 425 Swede Street in Norristown, Suite 303. Posted hours are weekdays from half past eight until four o'clock, and quick questions can be texted to 267-355-3404.

The office handles deeds, mortgages, powers of attorney, notary commissions, subdivision and highway plans, and military discharge papers.

For a seller the visit happens last. Papers get signed at the closing table, they travel to Norristown, and the recording date marks the moment the buyer shows up as owner in the public record. That is why your closing agent keeps asking you for a parcel number.

Recording charges

A deed starts at $87.75 under the schedule dated November 24, 2025. The price assumes no more than four names, four pages and a single parcel, and every extra is billed on top.

Montgomery County recording charges, schedule effective November 24, 2025
Charge typeAmount
Deed or mortgage, starting price$87.75
Additional page past the fourth$4.00
Additional name past the fourth$1.00
Additional parcel$15.50
Relocation deed$175.50
Satisfaction of a mortgage$81.75
Document rejection$10.00
Returned check$30.00

A few smaller charges apply too:

  • Statement of Value forms cost $1.50 for the pair of originals the office wants. A relocation deed needs four originals, at $3.00.
  • Mail a lone document with no return envelope and it costs $2; a bundle costs $10.
  • Cards add a 2.65% convenience charge.
  • Where land sits in two or more taxing authorities, the first unique parcel ID in each one carries a $5.50 fee.

How transfer tax is collected

The recorder collects it during recording, at a combined 2 percent. One point goes to the state, and under the state's rule the seller and the buyer answer for it jointly.

Bring two separate checks when a deed is recorded: one for the recording fee and one for the realty transfer tax. Payee names the county will honor include "Montco Recorder of Deeds" and "Montgomery County ROD," and each check should print the account holder's address.

Form REV-183, the Statement of Value, rides along whenever the tax is not simply paid on a stated price. Land spread over two or more municipalities calls for a split of value in the deed, so each local tax collector gets the right piece. The fee page also posts a Common Level Ratio Factor, 3.25 as of July 1, 2025 and 3.36 as of July 1, 2026. Ask the office how it applies to a deed that carries no sale price.

Some transfers owe nothing, such as particular gifts inside a family or inherited property. Whether a given family deed qualifies is a question for the closing attorney or the recorder's staff.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Montgomery County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Why a deed goes to the Board of Assessments first

Every document, on paper or electronic, must be registered by the Board of Assessments before it is recorded. The board sits directly across the hall from the recorder on the third floor of One Montgomery Plaza.

Every document also needs a Parcel Identification Number, a 12-digit number in this county. If a parcel number appears anywhere on a document, it has to be registered unless the document says in so many words that the number is for reference only. Questions about parcel mapping belong with the Board of Assessments, not the recorder.

Older advice about registering a deed with the township before recording no longer holds, because pre-registration was rescinded on December 9, 2008. Some municipalities still want the deed registered after it is recorded, and the municipality may charge for that. Whoever submits the deed handles it.

Can a deed be filed online?

Yes, within limits. The county has taken electronic recordings since fall 2006 and works with Simplifile, the eRecording Partners Network and CSC. Documents usually come back the same day or the next.

Some items must go on paper, so your closing agent should plan for that:

  • Deeds that contain a trust must be mailed or delivered, because an electronically recorded document becomes public automatically.
  • Mortgages in default, plans and post-construction stormwater documents cannot be submitted electronically.
  • Documents with more than 10 parcels, packages of more than 10 documents and packages above 100 pages are turned away.
  • Scans must be at least 300 DPI, black and white, as TIFF images.

If an electronic filing is rejected and you think the rejection was wrong, call 610-278-3289 the same day so staff can decide whether the rejection fee comes back.

Errors that get a deed returned

Most returns come from small mismatches. The office follows the standards set by the Pennsylvania recorders' association and adds its own.

  • The document must be an original, not a copy.
  • The acknowledgment date cannot be earlier than the document date, and it needs county, state, names, titles, the notary's signature, seal and commission expiration.
  • The number written out must match the numeral on a deed or mortgage.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments need a certified grantee or mortgagee address, signed.
  • Blanket documents are refused.
  • Paper submissions need a stamped, self-addressed envelope big enough for the documents.

Each rejection costs $10, so a package that fails twice costs more than one that is checked before it leaves the closing office.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Montgomery County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

The Montgomery County market

Montgomery County is a suburb of Philadelphia, with Norristown as the seat and Lower Merion Township as the biggest municipality. The 2025 federal estimate is 877,643 residents, and roughly 71 percent of homes are lived in by their owners. Prices run high: the typical owned home is valued at $436,700 and the typical household earns $113,915 on the latest five-year survey. The local share of transfer tax follows the municipality the house sits in, and school district names such as Lower Merion, North Penn, Abington and Norristown Area matter when you compare tax bills.

What to put in the closing folder

Bring the paperwork that the recorder will otherwise bounce. A few items cause most of the delay.

  • The 12-digit parcel number, checked against the Board of Assessments.
  • Two original Statement of Value forms, fully filled in.
  • Two checks, one for the recording fee and one for transfer tax, each with the account holder's address.
  • A prepaid return envelope if the deed comes back by mail.
  • A plan for any trust deed, since those cannot be filed electronically.

Your title company normally handles all of this. It still helps to ask who is paying the recording fee and the buyer's half of the tax, because the sales contract can shift those costs from the default.

Frequently asked questions

What is the price of recording a Montgomery County deed?

The base fee is $87.75 for up to four names, four pages and one parcel, plus $1 per extra name, $4 per extra page and $15.50 per extra parcel. Transfer tax and a $1.50 Statement of Value fee are separate.

Does Montgomery County take one check or two for a deed?

Two. One check covers the recording fee and a second covers the realty transfer tax, both payable to the Recorder of Deeds, each showing the account holder's address.

Who owes the transfer tax on a Montgomery County sale?

State law makes seller and buyer jointly responsible. The sales contract normally sets who really pays, and the combined rate collected at the Norristown counter is 2 percent.

Why can't a trust deed go through e-recording in Montgomery County?

Electronic recordings become public at once, so deeds with a trust must be recorded by mail or in person. Mortgages in default and plans are also excluded.

What if my deed has no parcel number yet?

Contact the Montgomery County Board of Assessments, which is across the hall from the recorder in Norristown. Every document must carry a registered 12-digit parcel number before it can be recorded.

Office location and hours

The Recorder of Deeds sits at 55 East Court Street, 6th floor, Doylestown. Call 215-348-6209. Counter hours are weekdays, 7:45 a.m. to 4:15 p.m., yet anything you want recorded has to be in by 4 p.m. A package that lands after noon may roll to the next workday.

Real estate records go back to 1684, when William Penn founded the county. Beyond deeds and mortgages, the office handles as many as 25 other types of paper, among them subdivision plans, UCC filings, mausoleum and sewer permits and notary commissions. Records are preserved on microfiche, microfilm and PDF/A, and bound books are no longer produced.

The county assessment board works hand in hand with the Recorder. Its deed registry staff review each document and attach tax parcel labels before recording, so a deed with a wrong parcel number or an outdated owner name can get stuck at that desk.

Recording fees

The fee schedule assumes one parcel, four names and four pages. Each page past four adds $4, each name past four adds $1, and each parcel past the first adds $10. For the base price of a deed or mortgage, use the recording fee calculator linked on the county's site, built by the state recorders association. The Statement of Value form isn't counted as a fee page.

Bucks County extra recording charges, effective January 2026
ChargeAmount
Each page after the fourth$4
Each name after the fourth$1
Each parcel after the first$10
Official search per name or item for a court order$5
Special handling per document$25
Rejected document returned$10
Paper copy of a receipt$0.50
Credit card service fee3.0%

Make checks and money orders payable to the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds. Calculators leave out certified copies, and staff confirm the final total when the document is recorded. Call 215-348-6209 to verify an amount before you mail anything.

Transfer tax for sellers

The rate is 2%, shared equally by the state and the local taxing bodies, and the Recorder collects it when you file. It applies to the value of the interest conveyed, which can differ from the sale price. State and local rules are silent on who pays, so most purchase agreements split it between buyer and seller. If the amount paid falls short, the new owner is the one who owes the difference.

Since January 2026 the office refuses personal checks for transfer tax. It takes cash in the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card. Title agents usually deal with this at settlement, so ask your closer which method will be used.

  • Some transfers are exempt, including conveyances between spouses, from parents to children, across three generations, and among siblings.
  • A one-time transfer between former spouses is allowed.
  • If an investigator finds a higher value, the state can bill extra tax and interest and mails the determination to you directly.
  • State revenue officials put their share at 1% of the value, collected along with any local tax by the county recorder.

Statement of Value (REV-183)

You need the state's REV-183 Statement of Value whenever transfer tax isn't paid or the true value is missing from the deed, as with a $1 consideration. The form either sets the value or gives the reason for an exemption. Bucks accepts only the June 2019 version, and a paper copy must come in duplicate.

The form relies on the Common Level Ratio Factor, which the county posts for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. State investigators may later test whether the stated value or exemption holds up. If it falls short, the state issues a determination, collects the extra tax and interest, and sends a receipt to the Recorder for recording.

When a deed is e-recorded, attachments such as a trust agreement, mortgage or assignment add a $1 per page copy fee. The office prints them for the Department of Revenue and then removes them from the public record. Sending those pages on paper avoids the charge.

How to submit a deed

Three routes work: e-record through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, carry the paper deed to the counter, or mail it. A mailed package needs the right checks payable to the Recorder and a stamped envelope addressed to yourself. Deeds, mortgages, general powers of attorney, satisfactions and copy requests go straight to the Recorder's office.

Book and page numbers ended on July 1, 2012, so every recorded document carries only an instrument number. Paper receipts ended that year too. Receipts now come by email, which requires the Submitter Information Form on file with the office.

  • The Fraud Alert System is free and tells an owner when something is recorded against the property.
  • A free email copy of your own deed is available on request.
  • Military discharge papers (DD-214) are recorded free.
  • An in-office notary is available.

Before you file a sale

Bucks covers 622 square miles between the Delaware River and Montgomery County, with Doylestown as the seat and Bensalem as the largest township. The 2020 population was 646,538. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 is $445,700, and 77.8% of households own their homes.

At that price, a 2% transfer tax is a real line item, so agree early on who bears it. Check that the municipality named on the deed matches the tax bill, since the local half of the tax depends on it. Ownership questions can go to the assessment board at 215-348-6219, though its public site can lag behind recordings.

Give your closing agent the parcel number, every owner name and the school district well ahead of settlement. The county has 54 townships and boroughs, and a short checklist of those three details can head off a rejected filing and the $10 return charge.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bucks County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

A seller's filing checklist

Gather the signed deed, the Statement of Value if tax is unpaid or the value is missing, and checks or a card for the fee. Confirm the parcel count and the number of names and pages so the charge is right the first time. Decide how the transfer tax will be paid, remembering that personal checks are refused. Choose e-recording, counter or mail, and meet the 4 p.m. cutoff, with noon as the safer mark. If you mail it, include a stamped return envelope and, if you want a receipt by email, the Submitter Information Form.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds office hours?

Counter service runs weekdays, 7:45 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. Documents to be recorded have to be submitted by 4 p.m. A package received after noon may wait for the next workday.

Can I pay Bucks County transfer tax with a personal check?

No. Since January 2026 the Recorder of Deeds refuses personal checks for realty transfer tax. Accepted methods are cash in the office, a cashier's check, a money order or a credit card, and cards carry a 3.0% service fee.

What is the fee for each extra page on a Bucks County deed?

Each page after the fourth costs $4. Names after the fourth cost $1 each and parcels after the first cost $10 each. The REV-183 Statement of Value isn't counted as a fee page.

Does Bucks County require a Statement of Value?

Yes, when transfer tax isn't paid or the deed lacks the true value, for example a $1 consideration. Use the June 2019 version of REV-183, in duplicate if submitted on paper. The state may later send a determination if the stated value looks low.

How far back do Bucks County deed records go?

The Recorder of Deeds holds records from 1684 to the present, kept on microfiche, microfilm and PDF/A. Documents recorded since July 1, 2012 carry an instrument number only.

Where to record a deed

Delaware County deeds are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds in the Government Center, Room 108, 201 W. Front Street, Media, PA 19063. Real property records go back to 1789, the year the county was created from part of Chester County. The phone is 610-891-4152.

The counter is open from 8:30am to 4:30pm, but documents are taken for recording only from 8:30am to 3:30pm. If your closing runs late in the day, ask the title company how the deed will get in before the cutoff, since e-recording and hand delivery follow the same window.

One office handles every deed, but each deed also touches a municipality. The recorder collects the local share of transfer tax for the township, borough or city where the house sits, so the municipality named on the deed shapes your final bill.

Recording fees

Recording a four-page deed costs $117.25 under the fee schedule dated December 1, 2025. The $38.00 base fee covers up to four pages, four names and ten folio numbers, and county and state add-on charges make up the rest.

Delaware County recording fees for a four-page document
Document typeTotal fee
Deed$117.25
Mortgage$115.25
Satisfaction, release or assignment$84.25
Agreement, power of attorney or general miscellaneous$43.00
Certification (4 pages)$7.00

The deed total breaks down as follows.

  • Base fee: $38.00
  • County Affordable Housing charge: $18.00
  • Judicial computer, access to justice and criminal justice add-on: $41.25, which rose by $1.00 on December 1, 2025
  • County Improvement Fund: $5.00
  • Demolition of Blighted Properties charge: $15.00

Extra pages on a deed are $4.00 each, and every name after the fourth or folio after the tenth adds $1.00. Military discharge papers are recorded free.

Transfer tax by municipality

Most Delaware County sales carry 2% in realty transfer tax: 1% to the state and 1% to the local taxing bodies. A few places charge more, so the municipality printed on your deed decides the rate.

  • Radnor Township: local 1.5%
  • Upper Darby Township: local 1.5%
  • Chester City: local 1.5%
  • Upper Providence Township: local 2%
  • Everywhere else in the county: local 1%

Contracts often split the tax between buyer and seller, so read the agreement of sale before assuming who writes the check. A seller in a 1.5% township pays noticeably more than one across the line in a 1% township, so check the municipality before you price an offer.

When a deed covers land in more than one municipality, it has to show what share of the value belongs to each taxing body, using the Pennsylvania Statement of Value.

Checks and paperwork

For an in-person recording the office asks for three separate checks. Each has its own payee, and a single combined check gets the package returned.

  • One check for the recording fee, made out to Recorder of Deeds
  • One check for state transfer tax, made out to Recorder of Deeds, Agent
  • One check for local transfer tax, also made out to Recorder of Deeds, Agent

Every page needs a 1-inch top margin so the office can stamp recording data electronically without covering text. All documents are also subject to Solicitor approval before recording, so build that into the closing timeline.

E-recording submitters can flag incorrect fees until 11:30am on the next business day after a month ends. The office does not run title searches, so title work stays with the title company or an attorney.

Common Level Ratio

The recorder's 2026-27 Common Level Ratio factor is 1.83. It applies to any document dated July 1, 2026 or later.

The ratio changes every fiscal year, so a deed dated before July 1, 2026 uses the earlier factor. If your document needs the factor at all, ask the office which one fits the date on your deed.

Searching records and ordering copies

Records from 1799 to the present can be viewed online through the county's public access site, and copies cost less there than at the counter. Online copies are $0.50 per page; counter copies are $1.00 per page. Electronic certified copies are $12.50 through the public access site, while paper certifications are $7.00 for four pages plus $1.00 for each added page.

  • Property Alert: a free service that emails you when a document is recorded against your Property ID number
  • Return envelope: add $1.00 to a mailed request if you do not enclose one
  • Microfiche copies: $1.00 per page

Homeowners worried about deed fraud can sign up for Property Alert before listing. It costs nothing and shows quickly if someone records a document against the parcel.

Delaware County housing

The county's estimated population was 580,937 in July 2025, with 230,160 housing units. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $332,200, owner-occupancy is 69.6%, median gross rent is $1,372 and median household income is $89,546. The county issued 217 building permits for 2025.

At that price level, transfer tax is a real number in a sale here, so work out your municipality's rate before you pick a net-proceeds figure.

What the recorder will not do

The office records, indexes and reproduces documents. It does not search title, and it does not tell you which transfer tax rate your contract should assume. Those questions belong to your title company, attorney or the municipality involved.

Mistakes are expensive in time more than money. A deed returned for a missing margin, a wrong payee or a bad notary block has to be fixed and brought back inside the recording window, which closes at 3:30pm. If that slips past the cutoff, recording can slide to the next business day, and the buyer may be waiting on keys or funds.

Questions about a particular deed are best asked before the closing date. Phone 610-891-4152 and have the municipality, the parcel's Property ID number and the page count ready.

Checklist before closing

Ask your title company who will bring the deed and whether it will be e-recorded or delivered by hand before the 3:30pm cutoff. Confirm the municipality on the deed and the local rate that goes with it. Make sure three checks are ready, with the right payees, and that each page of the deed has its top margin.

If the sale is to a cash buyer, the recording steps are the same. The deed, the fee and the transfer tax still go to Room 108, and the new owner appears in the records once the office has indexed the document.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What is the cost to record a deed in Delaware County?

A four-page deed costs $117.25 under the December 1, 2025 schedule. Extra pages are $4.00 each, and names after four or folio numbers after ten add $1.00 each.

What are the transfer tax rates in Delaware County?

The standard rate is 1% state plus 1% local. Radnor, Upper Darby and Chester City charge 1.5% locally, and Upper Providence charges 2% locally.

What hours does the Delaware County Recorder of Deeds accept recordings?

Recording hours are 8:30am to 3:30pm, although the office stays open to 4:30pm. It is in Room 108 of the Government Center in Media.

Do I need separate checks to record a deed in Delaware County?

Yes. The office asks for one check for the recording fee, one for state transfer tax and one for local transfer tax. Tax checks go to Recorder of Deeds, Agent.

Can I look up Delaware County deeds online?

Yes. Records from 1799 to the present are available online, with copies at $0.50 per page. Copies bought in the office are $1.00 per page.

What the recorder's office does in a sale

In West Chester, this office takes in the deed that passes a house to its new owner, gathers the realty transfer tax owed, and holds the lasting land record. A deed that hasn't been recorded leaves the old owner on the public record, and a buyer's lender or a later purchaser may balk at that.

The office is the custodian of all land records and transfer indexes, going back to 1688. It also records mortgages, satisfactions, powers of attorney, subdivision plans and notary commissions. Tax money it collects goes on to the Commonwealth, the county's 73 municipalities and its 14 school districts. Nobody at the counter will draft a deed, hunt for liens or advise you legally. A title company or attorney does that work.

Location and filing times

The office is at 313 W. Market Street, Suite 3302, West Chester. Call 610-344-6330. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but recording documents must be handed in by 4 p.m.

  • Same-day recording runs 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.
  • Same-day recording of large exhibits such as maps and subdivision plans stops at 3:00 p.m.
  • The search library stays open until 4:15 p.m.
  • Fees are due at the moment of recording, and the office won't record an unofficial copy of a document already on record.

Any paper filing should carry a self-addressed stamped envelope. Leave it out and the county supplies postage and bills you $2.00.

Recording fees

A standard deed costs $94.75 to record under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. That base covers one UPI, up to four pages, one notation fee and four names. A mortgage and a deed of correction carry the same base.

Chester County recording fees, effective December 1, 2025
DocumentBase fee
Deed$94.75
Re-recorded deed or mortgage$96.75
Deed in blank or relocation deed$183.50
Satisfaction, assignment, release, easement$81.75
Power of attorney$20.50
Miscellaneous document$40.50

Extras stack on top. A UPI costs $20.00 per number, a document that misses the PRIA formatting standards carries a $25.00 non-compliance fee, and each exhibit adds $5.00. The base fee already contains a $41.25 judicial administration charge set by the Department of Revenue.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Chester County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax and who pays

The rate is 1% of the consideration or computed value, whichever is higher, with higher rates in three places: Malvern and Tredyffrin at 1.5%, and Coatesville at 2.5%. Ask the recorder for the combined state and local figure that applies to your deed.

State law makes grantor and grantee jointly liable for the tax, and certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy are exempt. Who covers the bill in a sale is a matter for the sales agreement.

  • Pay transfer tax with separate checks, one for the municipality and one for the state, made out to the Chester County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Only business checks, cashier's checks and money orders are taken for tax. Cash and credit cards are refused for tax.
  • Recording fees go on a third check or other accepted payment.

Why deeds get rejected

Payment errors and gaps on page one cause most returns. The recorder takes cash in person for recording fees only, and personal, estate and trustee checks are always refused. Checks older than 180 days are returned, no more than ten documents may share one check, and a returned check triggers a $25 bank fee on top of the $10.00 rejection fee for returned documents.

  • Type a valid UPI on the first page. A computer-printed label on page one is acceptable.
  • Give the grantee's exact mailing address and certify it with a signature, as 16 P.S. Section 9781 requires.
  • Attach a Statement of Value when the deed doesn't show the full value, unless a family exemption applies. The Common Level Ratio factor, updated each July 1, belongs on that form.
  • For land in more than one municipality, show the local tax split in dollars on the deed.
  • Match every name across the caption, signature and notary acknowledgment, including Sr., Jr. and III.

Checks before the deed goes in

Begin with the chain of title. Any mortgage you paid off ought to have a recorded satisfaction, and filing a missing one costs the $81.75 base fee in that category. A house inherited through an estate leans harder on the Statement of Value and the family-transfer rules, so get your title company looking at those early.

Check the grantee's mailing address with the buyer too. Future tax bills follow the address on the deed, and the county asks that it be exact, current, legible and scannable. A deed sent in with a tax check from a personal or estate account will be turned away, so arrange transfer tax funds as a cashier's check or money order ahead of time.

  • If the seller's copy of the vesting deed is lost, order one from the recording office. Staff-made certified copies run $0.50 per page plus $5.00 for certification.
  • Ask the title company whether the property sits in Malvern, Tredyffrin or Coatesville, where higher tax rates apply.
  • Confirm the deed shows the correct UPI and not the tax parcel number, since the two are formatted differently.

Can a deed be e-recorded?

Yes. Simplifile and CSC eRecording both carry electronic filings to the Chester County office, and most title companies send closing packages that way. For a deed that owes tax, the consideration and the state and municipal tax amounts must appear on the first page.

Each package is limited to ten documents, and one document can list no more than ten UPI numbers. Deeds of correction, re-recorded deeds and Statements of Value with exhibits attached can't be e-recorded and go in on paper. Resubmitting a document costs a $10 return fee each time, and a document recorded in error isn't refunded.

Chester County housing context

Chester County sits in the Philadelphia metropolitan area, with West Chester as the seat and Coatesville as its only city. About 557,116 residents live across roughly 751 square miles, with 217,440 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home value is $485,600, median household income is $127,208 and median gross rent is $1,763. Owners occupy 75.1% of homes. Transfer tax can differ sharply from one township to the next.

Frequently asked questions

How long does it take to record a deed in Chester County?

Same-day recording is offered until 4:00 p.m. on business days, and e-recorded packages through Simplifile or CSC are the usual route for closings. Large plans must arrive by 3:00 p.m. for same-day handling.

Can I pay the Chester County transfer tax by credit card?

No. Transfer tax must be paid by business check, cashier's check or money order made out to the Chester County Recorder of Deeds. Credit cards may be used only for recording fees and copy requests, with a 3.5% in-person fee.

Do I need a Statement of Value to record a deed in Chester County?

Yes, when the deed doesn't show the full and complete value of the property, unless a family exemption applies. It is a Department of Revenue form and is recorded with the deed, so its pages count toward the recording fee.

Can the Recorder of Deeds correct a mistake in a recorded deed?

Not by editing it. A deed of correction costs $94.75 and needs a written explanation on page one, the book and page of the deed being fixed, a new acknowledgment and a Statement of Value. Deeds of correction can't be e-recorded.

Is the transfer tax the same everywhere in Chester County?

No. The base rate is 1% of consideration or computed value, but Malvern and Tredyffrin charge 1.5% and Coatesville charges 2.5%. Check the municipality where the house sits before you price a sale.

Where to record a deed in Lancaster County

Send or carry deeds to the Recorder of Deeds, 150 North Queen Street, Suite 315, Lancaster, PA 17603. The office is open from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays, and recording itself concludes at 4:30 p.m.

Payments aren't taken over the phone. Since October 1, 2025, staff no longer print trusts or other supporting papers as a courtesy. Send those pages already printed, or attach them to an electronic filing, to avoid a 25 cent per page printing charge.

For a seller, this office comes at the very end. The deed is signed and acknowledged at closing, then recorded here, and the county's public search shows the new owner afterward.

Recording fees

The posted base fee for a deed or mortgage of up to four pages is $71.25. Every page after the fourth adds $2.00, and the office doesn't issue refunds.

Lancaster County base recording fees, up to four pages
Document typeBase fee
Deed or mortgage$71.25
Assignment, release, satisfaction, installment sale agreement, easement$59.75
Agreement, termination, modification, subordination$58.75
Power of attorney or deputation (miscellaneous)$18.50

Copies, per page$0.25

The JCP fee rose from $40.25 to $41.25 under Act 45 of 2025. Call the office for the exact total on your package.

A military discharge, the DD-214, is recorded free.

Payment methods

For recording, the counter accepts cash, certified checks, corporate checks, money orders and credit cards. Personal checks are refused for amounts over $75 and are never taken for transfer tax. Blank checks aren't accepted either.

  • Card payments carry a 2.5% charge on transactions over $50, and $1 on smaller ones.
  • A returned check costs $25.00.
  • There are no refunds, so the amount has to be right the first time.
  • Mailed or couriered packages need a self-addressed stamped envelope of the right size and with enough postage.

When a document type has no listed fee, the Recorder sets one. If your deed has attachments or several parcels, ask before sending money.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lancaster County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Deed formatting and content rules

No cover page is needed, and staples are not allowed. Use white paper, 8.5 by 11, with type of 10 point or larger.

  • The notary acknowledgment date can't come before the date on the document, and the acknowledgment needs the state, county, date, the person appearing, the notary's signature and the notary's expiration date. The seal itself is optional for Pennsylvania notaries.
  • The tax parcel ID, with its district code, must appear on every deed.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments need a signed, certified address with a zip code for the buyer or lender. On a deed a P.O. box isn't allowed as that address, though the deed may say tax bills should go to a box.
  • Land in more than one municipality must state the percentage split of local transfer tax, in whole numbers.
  • Written amounts must match numbers, and no Social Security or bank account numbers should appear.
  • A transaction is limited to 10 documents, and blanket assignments or releases are rejected.

A corrective or confirmatory deed must come with a Statement of Value, an explanation, and a full copy of the deed it fixes.

Realty transfer tax

You pay the tax to the Recorder when the deed is recorded. Pennsylvania takes 1 percent of the transferred value and treats buyer and seller as equally liable. Local taxes are collected at the same counter and divided between municipalities and school districts.

Some transfers are exempt: certain family transfers, transfers to governments, and property passing by will or intestacy. If the full tax isn't paid, attach a completed Statement of Value. The county counts that form as one page of the four-page base, and easements need one too.

If a deed names the wrong property location, the submitter bears the cost. The right municipality, school district and state must still be paid, and the submitter claims back anything sent to the wrong place.

Other documents the recorder files

The office handles mortgages, satisfactions, assignments, powers of attorney, leases, Uniform Commercial Code filings, notary commissions and military discharges. Several of these touch a house sale, so know the charges ahead of time.

  • A notary commission and bond costs $32.00, and registering the notary's signature adds $4.75.
  • Subdivision, stormwater and state highway plans start at $15.00 for the first page and add $2.00 per page. Condominium plans start at $30.00.
  • Plans must be at least 18 by 24 inches and no larger than 24 by 36, and both Mylar and paper are accepted.
  • A UCC-1 or UCC-3 filing costs $100.00 each.
  • Notaries can register their signature at the Recorder's office, which saves a trip to the Prothonotary's office in a separate building.

A seller paying off a mortgage should ask the lender when the satisfaction piece will be filed. At the posted $59.75 base, it is a separate recording with its own book and page reference back to the original mortgage.

Checklist before the deed leaves for the courthouse

Go through this list with the title agent.

  • Parcel ID and district code on the deed, matching the county record.
  • A certified buyer address that isn't a P.O. box.
  • Dollar figures that agree in words and numbers.
  • A completed Statement of Value if the transfer is taxed in part or exempt.
  • Payment in an accepted form: no personal check over $75 and none at all for transfer tax.
  • No staples and no cover sheet.

If the deed is going by mail, put the package together a few days early and enclose the return envelope. The office's public records search lets you confirm afterward that the deed appears under the buyer's name.

After the deed is submitted

Once the package reaches the counter before 4:30 p.m., staff check it against the rules above, collect the fee and the transfer tax, and record it. If something is off, such as a stapled page, a P.O. box as the buyer's certified address or a personal check, the deed doesn't go on the record until it is fixed.

Fees aren't refunded, so a rejected package that needed a new payment form means a second trip or a second mailing. The sellers who avoid this are the ones whose title agent ran the checklist before sending anything. When the deed is recorded, the county's public search should show the new owner under the buyer's name.

A house that needs work can sell to a cash buyer without lender paperwork, but the recording side of the closing doesn't change.

Lancaster County housing snapshot

Lancaster County had 563,159 residents and 223,178 housing units in July 2025. Owners live in 69.8% of homes for 2020 to 2024, at a median value of $301,100. Median gross rent is $1,357.

Frequently asked questions

What is the base fee for a deed at the Lancaster County Recorder of Deeds?

The posted base fee is $71.25 for a deed or mortgage of up to four pages, plus $2.00 for each added page. The JCP fee rose to $41.25 under Act 45 of 2025, so confirm the total with the office.

Can I pay Lancaster County transfer tax with a personal check?

No. Personal checks are never accepted for transfer tax, and they are refused for any amount over $75. Use cash, a certified or corporate check, a money order or a credit card, with the card fee added.

Does a Lancaster County deed need a cover page?

No. Cover pages are no longer required, and staples must not be used. Use white 8.5 by 11 paper and type of at least 10 point.

Can I use a P.O. box as the buyer's address on a Lancaster County deed?

Not as the certified address, which must be a street address with a zip code. The deed may say that tax bills should be mailed to a P.O. box.

What time does the Lancaster County recorder stop recording?

Recording concludes at 4:30 p.m., though the office stays open until 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. Documents that come in after 4:30 p.m. wait for the next business day.

What does the York County Recorder of Deeds do?

The Recorder of Deeds records and keeps every real estate document in York County, Pennsylvania. It also records military discharge papers and notary bonds and commissions. The recorder is an elected position with a four-year term.

The office takes documents by mail, in person and through approved e-recording vendors. A seller whose title company uses e-recording never has to mail the deed. A seller who does mail it should send a check or cash for the exact fee, because the office does not take e-checks at its counter.

Indexing follows set rules. Every name variation on a document (a former name, a trading name, an also-known-as) is indexed, and the office may cross-index documents such as affidavits and rights of way so that each person or entity appears as both grantor and grantee. Where Mortgage Electronic Registration Systems acts as nominee for a lender, only that name is indexed, not the lender behind it. A title searcher reading a York County chain of title should expect those conventions.

Another service worth knowing about is the Records Alert program, which tells a homeowner when any document is recorded against their property. The county posted a notice that anyone who enrolled before May 1, 2026 has to create a new subscription in the current system, since earlier sign-ups no longer work.

What are the recording charges at the York County Recorder?

Recording a deed runs $86.25, the same as a mortgage or quitclaim deed. The sum is good for four pages and four names. Beyond that, each extra page is $2 and each extra name is $0.50. A separate $20 is charged for every parcel identification number the document mentions, a rule in place since January 1, 2025.

The county also notes that its Access to Justice fee changed to $41.25 on November 14, 2025, so use the county's fee calculator (choose York) or the printable worksheet rather than adding figures from memory.

York County recording base fees
DocumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage or quitclaim deed$86.25
Deed of dedication$71.25
Release of mortgage, easement, lease or assignment of mortgage$59.75
Affidavit, power of attorney or plain release$18.50
Statement of Value (transfer tax form)$2
Military discharge (DD-214)Free

The counter takes cash, business checks and personal checks, and the requirements sheet also lists money orders payable to the Recorder of Deeds. Bounced checks incur a $50 charge. A surplus below $10 is kept, but a check exceeding the fee by more than $10 is returned for correction.

Which details must a York County deed contain?

The recorder's requirements sheet lists the points that most often cause a rejected deed. Check each before the closing agent sends it in:

  • The document must concern real estate, carry original signatures, and be properly notarized, in English or with an English translation.
  • A Uniform Parcel Identifier must appear on the document, with the property location (not a street address) beneath it at the top left. The county assessment office at 717-771-3253 or 717-771-4656 can supply it.
  • The grantor's name has to match the name on the prior deed exactly, so John Allen Smith cannot become John A. Smith.
  • The deed needs a precise address, because the assessment office uses it to mail tax bills.
  • The municipality, whether township, borough or city, belongs above the legal description.
  • The date on the deed must be the same as or earlier than the acknowledgment date.

When land lies in several municipalities, the deed must state the percentage split for local transfer tax. A family transfer where no tax is paid should say so in a typed statement on the deed. The Common Level Ratio factor is chosen by the date the document was signed and notarized, and the recorder's office at 717-771-9608 can supply factors for earlier years.

What realty transfer tax applies to a York County sale?

The state's own levy is 1 percent of the value of the real estate conveyed. Per the Department of Revenue, recorders bring it in along with any local transfer tax and pass the Commonwealth's share along.

A local portion rides on top, and it varies with the borough or township and the school district, which is the reason a deed has to name each municipality. Get the exact local percentage for your parcel from the recorder or the closing agent before you estimate what you will net. The state holds buyer and seller jointly liable, while the sales contract decides who actually pays.

Exempt transfers listed by the state include some among relatives, those to government bodies, burial-site deeds and property that passes by will or intestacy. Whenever the price paid is below full market value, a Statement of Value must accompany the deed, and an easement needs one too unless it belongs to a public utility.

How do I find or copy a deed in York County?

Documents recorded in York County are public records, except military discharges. You can search free on the public computers in the Recorder's office during open hours, and printing costs $0.50 a page. Certified copies add $1.50 per document.

To search from home you need the deed book and page. Look up the owner's name in the county's real estate assessment database and the record book and page appear under the owner record. Documents can then be retrieved online through the Landex public records link on the county site. For anything recorded before 1944, the county points researchers to the IQS site, where searching as a guest is free and printing is $0.80 a page.

What is York County like beyond the courthouse?

Created in 1749 out of Lancaster County, York County stretches 911 square miles along the Susquehanna River, ending at the Mason-Dixon line in the south. The 72 local governments consist of one city, 36 boroughs and 35 townships. York city holds the county seat, and in the 2010 count Hanover came second among communities by population.

Fertile farmland sits alongside factories here. Snack and food makers, a Harley-Davidson plant, the York International HVAC brand and York Barbell are all linked to the county. The 2025 federal estimate puts the population at 473,197, which is 3.7 percent higher than in 2020.

  • Housing units: 193,394 as of 2025.
  • Owners live in 76.3 percent of occupied homes (2020 to 2024).
  • Homes owners live in have a midpoint value of $248,600.
  • Midpoint household income of $84,829.
  • Monthly gross rent at the midpoint: $1,193.

On a $248,600 sale the state's 1 percent comes to $2,486 before any local share is added. Anyone selling an inherited house should also read up on Pennsylvania inheritance tax before listing.

Frequently asked questions

Does York County accept e-recording?

Yes. York County takes recordings by mail, in person and through e-recording partners approved by the county. The recorder's counter does not accept e-checks, so fees paid in the office must be by cash, check or money order.

What does the York County recorder charge to file a deed?

The base fee is $86.25 for a deed, mortgage or quitclaim deed. It covers four pages and four names, and each parcel number on the document adds $20. Use the county's fee calculator to include every add-on.

Do I need a parcel identifier to record a deed in York County?

Yes. A Uniform Parcel Identifier is required on all documents before they are recorded. The assessment office can provide it. The property's location, not just its mailing address, goes beneath the UPI at the top of the deed.

Can I stop someone from recording a document against my York County property?

The Records Alert service is meant to let a homeowner know before any document is recorded against their property. Anyone who signed up before May 1, 2026 must enroll again in the new system.

Is there a free way to look up a York County deed?

Yes. Public computers in the Recorder's office offer free searching during open hours, with $0.50 per printed page. Remote access runs through the county's Landex link, and the IQS site covers records before 1944 at $0.80 a page.

Where to record a deed in Berks County

The Recorder of Deeds is on the third floor of the Berks County Services Center, 633 Court Street, Reading, PA 19601. Counter hours are 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, and the phone is 610-478-3380. Documents can also arrive by e-recording, by mail or over the counter.

The office does more than file deeds. It collects state and local real estate transfer taxes, affordable housing fees, judicial fees and redeterminations, records subdivision and land development plans, highway maps and real estate UCC liens, and swears in notaries. Every document recorded since the county was founded in 1752 is available as an image and index on its online search site, with original handwritten and typed books kept for 1752 to 1953.

Owners can use the Property Alert tool, a fraud protection service that tells you when something is recorded against your address.

Recording fees

A deed, agreement, easement, lease or order of court carries a base fee of $88.00 for up to four pages, and every added page is $4.00. The fee schedule took effect on November 14, 2025, and a Statement of Value counts as an extra page when fees are figured. The base fee includes one tax parcel, and each additional parcel is $15.00.

Berks County recording fees effective November 14, 2025

There is an extra charge to index more than 15 names on one document. Statements of Value that arrive through e-recording are charged a $0.50 per page copy fee for printing and mailing to the Department of Revenue.

Transfer tax rates and payment

The rate depends on where the house sits. The fee schedule lists 5% in the City of Reading and 2% in all other Berks municipalities. That is charged before any recording fee.

How you pay matters here. The office no longer accepts cash or personal checks for transfer tax. Overpayments of $10 or less are forfeited, and checks 180 days old or older are refused. Checks are made payable to Berks County Recorder of Deeds.

  • Ask your closing agent whether the title company will pay by company check or wire.
  • Confirm which municipality and school district appear on the deed, especially for Wyomissing Borough, where deeds must name Wyomissing or Wilson School District.
  • Read the purchase agreement to see who pays the tax, since the split is a negotiated term.

The Statement of Value

A Statement of Value is required on every deed that leaves out the full and complete value of the property, unless a family exemption applies, in which case the exemption has to be stated in the deed. It must also accompany easements and rights of way. The form is completed in duplicate under Department of Revenue rules, and it is the Pennsylvania REV-183.

The form uses the Common Level Ratio, which changes each July 1. For documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027 the Berks County factor is 3.12. Since the office treats the form as an additional page, include it when you estimate fees so the check comes out exact.

Why documents get rejected

Berks County is specific about format. Documents should be on white 8.5 by 11 inch paper at 20 pound weight, in a font no smaller than 10 point, with a one inch margin at the top and one inch margins on the sides and bottom. Legal size paper is no longer accepted, and light copies will not be scanned legibly, so use dark print and black ink.

  • A Property Identification Number (UPI) is required on every document that references real estate, and the grantee’s mailing address must be exact, current and legible.
  • The written amount on a deed must match the numerical amount.
  • The acknowledgment needs the state and county, date, signers, notary signature and a clear stamp with an expiration date.
  • Do not include Social Security numbers or bank or loan numbers, since the Recorder may redact or reject the document.
  • The submitter’s name and company must be typed in the Return To area, with a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

Documents received by 3:30 p.m. are generally recorded that same day and held until the next day before being returned. A document written in a foreign language has to be recorded with an English translation sworn or affirmed by the translator.

Berks County housing

Reading is the county seat, and the Schuylkill River runs through the county, about 50 miles northwest of Philadelphia. Population is 440,072 for 2025, up 2.6% from 2020, with 172,559 housing units and 163,236 households. The owner-occupied rate is 71.3%, the median value of an owner-occupied home is $257,300, and median gross rent is $1,181.

Getting the recorded document back

The submitter decides where the recorded document goes, because the office requires a postage-paid, addressed envelope with each one. Title companies and attorneys often address it to themselves and forward it, and others address it to the new owner. If a copy never shows, check with the closing agent first, then request a copy from the Recorder.

Certified copies ordered online are $10.00 per document, regular copies from the website are 50 cents a page, and copies made in the office, other than your own home’s deed, are also 50 cents a page. Credit card payments add a processor fee that is not a county charge. After a mortgage payoff, the lender has 60 days to file the satisfaction, and Pennsylvania lenders do not hold deeds, so no new deed will arrive.

Changing names and selling for cash

To add or remove a name on a deed, a new deed has to be prepared and recorded. An attorney can often prepare and file it, and the office line is 610-478-3380. For a cash sale, the recording rules do not change: the deed still needs the right paper, a Statement of Value if the price is not stated, the UPI and a transfer tax payment the office will accept. What disappears is the lender, so the title company can usually send the deed in right after signing. Ask for the recorded copy and keep it.

Frequently asked questions

What is the base fee to record a deed in Berks County?

The base fee is $88.00 for up to four pages and one tax parcel. Every extra page is $4.00 and each extra parcel is $15.00, under the schedule effective November 14, 2025.

What is the Berks County transfer tax on a home sale?

It is 5% in the City of Reading and 2% in every other Berks municipality. The office no longer takes cash or personal checks for it.

How do I add or remove a name on my Berks County deed?

A new deed has to be prepared and recorded. An attorney can often file it too, and the office phone is 610-478-3380.

What is the Berks County Common Level Ratio for 2026 to 2027?

The factor is 3.12 for documents accepted from July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. It changes every July 1 and goes on the Statement of Value.

Does the Berks County Recorder record military discharge papers?

Yes, recording a DD-214 and the military ID card are free. Bring the original discharge papers if you have not recorded them before.

Where to file a deed

Deeds for Lehigh County property are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds Division, Room 122 of the Lehigh County Courthouse, 455 W. Hamilton Street, Allentown, PA 18101. The phone number is 610-782-3162. Counter service runs Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:30. Parcel identification, called GIS PIN certification, stops earlier, at 3:45 in the afternoon, so bring a deed that needs a new PIN in the morning or early afternoon.

The office closes on major holidays and on any day the President Judge of the Court of Common Pleas directs. Your closing agent normally files the deed and payoff papers for you. The fees below still matter, because each one appears as a line on your settlement statement.

Deed recording fees

A deed of any type costs $81.25 to record under the fee schedule effective January 1, 2026. That covers up to four pages, four names and one PIN certification. Anything beyond those limits is billed separately.

Lehigh County recording fees, effective January 1, 2026
DocumentFee
Deed, all types$81.25
Mortgage$81.25
Satisfaction piece$71.75
Release of mortgage$71.75
Assignment of mortgage$71.75
Deed of dedication$69.75
Easement or right-of-way$69.75

Extras are small but add up on a complicated parcel:

  • Each page over four costs $2.00, and each name over four costs $0.50.
  • Each additional PIN costs $10.00, so a deed that covers several parcels costs more.
  • Each electronic notation costs $2.00.
  • A rejected document costs $10.00 each time, and a returned check costs $20.00.
  • Mailing documents back costs $3.00 each unless you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

An overpayment of $10.00 or less is forfeited, and the office does not refund fees for a document sent twice by mistake. Check the amount before you send it.

Electronic recording

Yes. The office accepts electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC and ePN. Those platforms calculate fees and taxes as you submit, so fewer documents get rejected, and electronic filings are usually recorded the same day. If one is rejected, you can correct it and send it back right away.

Maps and plans, including subdivision plats, can be recorded electronically through the same three vendors. The division keeps no paper copy of a map that was recorded electronically.

Certified copies cannot be bought online. They are made at the recorder's counter for $1.50 per document on top of the copy charge. Plain copies are $0.50 per page in person and $1.00 per page by mail.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lehigh County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Searching old deeds

The division holds records back to 1812. All of it is public except military discharge papers (DD-214), which the office records for free and keeps private. Staff are not authorized to do your search or research for you, so you search on your own. There are four ways to do it:

  • LANDEX Webstore: free searching, with a fee to view or print a document, aimed at occasional users.
  • LANDEX Remote: pay as you go at $0.15 a minute and $0.10 for each page loaded, built for heavy users, with an Index Book tab covering 1812 to 1983.
  • Lehigh County Online Records Access: needs an account and a yearly fee arranged through the county Fiscal Office.
  • In person: the public review area downstairs in the courthouse, open Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 4:00.

If you inherited a house with a thin paper trail, the index books can turn up an old deed or an unreleased mortgage before a buyer's title search does.

Transfer tax when a house sells

Pennsylvania charges 1 percent of the property's value on a transfer. You pay it at the recorder's counter on the day of filing, in the same payment as the recording fee. The state revenue department's page holds seller and buyer jointly responsible. Your school district and municipality may tack on a local share, and the rate depends on where the parcel sits. A city can charge differently than a township. Ask the recorder for the full combined rate on your parcel before you pick a list price.

Certain family transfers, transfers under a will or by intestacy, and transfers to government bodies are exempt. You explain a claimed exemption on the state's REV-183 Statement of Value.

Other filings that can land on a house record

A sale is not the only event that touches a parcel. Farmland owners record Act 319 preferential assessment filings at $33.00 with no extra charge for added pages or names, and covenant filings under Act 515 carry the same $33.00. An Agricultural Security Area ordinance costs $28.50. Easements and rights-of-way cost $69.75. A lease over 30 years costs $59.75. Financing statements under the Uniform Commercial Code cost $110.00 flat.

Release paperwork matters most to sellers. A paid-off mortgage keeps showing on the record until the lender files a satisfaction piece ($71.75) or release of mortgage ($71.75). If the house came to you by inheritance, search for loans that were paid years ago and never released. A notary commission and bond cost $33.50 in the same office.

Plans and maps follow a different scale. A subdivision, survey or stormwater plan costs $35.00 for page one and $25.00 for every page after it, and a condominium plan costs $40.00 and $25.00. Highway, mining and railroad maps cost $15.00 and $3.00. You would see them if you divide a lot before selling.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lehigh County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Steps from signed deed to recorded deed

A typical sale moves through the office in a few steps. Your title company or attorney drafts the deed and holds it to the four page, four name and one PIN limits. It is then sent through an e-recording vendor or walked to the Room 122 counter. The tax and the fee are collected in one payment. A deed that needs a new parcel number gets its GIS PIN certification first, which explains the earlier afternoon cutoff.

After acceptance the deed becomes part of the public record. Ask the closing agent for the recording details, and if a lender is being paid off, make sure its satisfaction piece is filed as well. Anyone filing by mail should include a return envelope with postage so the mailing charge is not added.

Selling in Lehigh County

Lehigh County is in the Lehigh Valley, and Allentown is the county seat. The 2020 count was 374,557 people, of whom 125,845 lived in Allentown, and the 2025 estimate is 384,383. Housing runs from the oldest buildings in the county, such as Shelter House in Emmaus, built in 1734, to newer construction. Older homes can bring title questions like old easements or a lien that was never released, and the recording office's records can help answer them.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Lehigh County recording fee for a deed?

A deed costs $81.25 under the schedule effective January 1, 2026. That covers four pages, four names and one PIN certification, with extra pages at $2.00 and extra names at $0.50.

Where is the Lehigh County Recorder of Deeds?

The office is in Room 122 of the courthouse at 455 W. Hamilton Street in Allentown. It is open weekdays from 8:00 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the number is 610-782-3162.

Can I get a certified copy of a Lehigh County deed online?

No, they are made only at the office. Each certified copy adds $1.50 per document to the usual charge of $0.50 per page in person.

How far back do Lehigh County records go?

Records begin in 1812. LANDEX covers index, deed, mortgage, map and miscellaneous records from that year to today.

Are Lehigh County deeds recorded the same day?

Electronic filings through Simplifile, CSC or ePN are usually recorded the same day. Paper filings depend on the queue, and a rejected paper filing costs $10.00.

Where deeds get recorded

The Recorder of Deeds works from Room L116 of the county government center at 669 Washington Street in Easton. Phone 610-829-6210. Staff are at the counter until half past four, but a recording that needs a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m.

The office records, images and stores deeds, mortgages and other real estate papers filed in the county. Each document gets a volume and page reference, then it is imaged for viewing and copying. The office also collects the fees and taxes on property transfers and passes them along.

Sellers meet this office at the very end of a sale. The title company gets the deed signed, carries it to Easton, and the recording puts the buyer's name on the public record. Most deeds need a parcel certification, so a courier who arrives at 4:15 may be told to come back tomorrow.

Recording fees

Filing a deed costs $76.25 on the schedule that began December 1, 2025. That price assumes four pages and four names at most, with parcel certification added on top.

Recording fees, effective December 1, 2025
DocumentFee
Parcel certification (each parcel)$10.00
Deed$76.25
