Mortgage satisfaction, assignment or release$61.75
Extra page after the fourth$2.00
Extra name after the fourth$0.50
Installment sales agreement$59.75
Notary bond and commission$38.50

An easement or right of way costs $59.75, and a power of attorney used to sell real estate costs $18.50 plus parcel certification. A Statement of Value costs $2 and counts toward the page total, certifications cost $2.50, and copies are fifty cents a page.

How a closing agent pays the recorder

Make payment out to "Recorder of Deeds." Personal checks are refused. Business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash all work, and a single check can cover five documents at most.

The exact amount has to accompany each document, and the office turns away overpayments. Packages built on a rough guess run into that rule, so build the number line by line from the schedule.

  • Count the pages first, then add $2 for every page past four.
  • Add $10 for each parcel on documents marked with an asterisk on the schedule.
  • Count names past four at $0.50 each.
  • Add the separate transfer tax payment if the deed is taxable.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Northampton County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Paper rules the Easton office enforces

The fee schedule opens with house rules, and they decide whether a deed is recorded or returned.

  • Parcel numbers must appear on every document that relates to real estate. The county's public parcel search is at ncpub.org.
  • Pages should be letter size, 8.5 by 11 inches. A paper that cannot comply, with 8.5 by 14 as the only allowed exception, pays a $10 penalty.
  • Blanket assignments, releases and satisfaction pieces are refused.
  • Anything coming back by mail needs a return envelope with the right postage already on it.

Not every filing is a deed. If a sale involves a new lot line or survey, the county charges $35 for the first page of a subdivision, site or survey plan and $30 for each added page. State highway plans cost $15 for the first page and $3 after that, and a lease for 30 years or longer costs $59.75. Full-size map copies up to 36 by 48 inches are $25.

Every document is microfilmed and open to public inspection, so whatever gets filed in Easton becomes searchable by anyone. Page count drives the fee. A deed with a long legal description and an attached exhibit can pass four pages quickly, so check before you assume the base price.

Transfer tax on a sale

On a taxable deed the recorder takes the state's 1 percent along with whatever local transfer tax the municipality and school district impose. State rules hold the grantor and the grantee jointly responsible.

The state exempts some deeds, among them certain family transfers, deeds to a government body and inherited property. If you believe your deed fits, tell the title agent early. For the local share, call the recorder's office and give the municipality where the house stands, because the figure can differ from one borough or township to the next.

Who actually pays is a matter for the sales contract, so read that clause before closing.

Which municipalities use this office

All of them. Two cities, Bethlehem and Easton, sit among many boroughs and townships, yet every deed for land inside the county line is recorded in the same Easton office. Part of Bethlehem lies in Lehigh County, a different county with its own recorder, so confirm which side your house is on before planning the closing.

Local transfer tax and school district bills follow the municipality, so a sale in Hellertown can price out differently from one in Palmer Township. Other boroughs in the county include Northampton, Wilson, Nazareth, Bangor, Pen Argyl and Wind Gap.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Northampton County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens after the deed is recorded

Once the clerk accepts the paper and the fee, the deed is stamped with its volume and page reference and imaged. From that point it is a public record. Your title company usually tracks this step and confirms it to you, and the buyer's lender, if there is one, waits on it before funds are released.

If a deed comes back, the cause is nearly always a missing parcel number, a wrong fee, a page that is the wrong size or an envelope without postage. Fix the item and send it again. Nothing about the sale is lost, but the recording date moves, so tell the buyer's side what happened. As the seller you should bring ID to the signing, the parcel number and the tax certification, so the package leaves the table complete.

Before closing day

Most delays are paper problems, not legal ones. Work through this list a few days ahead.

  • Confirm the parcel number on the deed matches the county's parcel search.
  • Count pages and names to get the exact fee, with no overpayment.
  • Ask whether the title company will deliver by 4:00 p.m., since parcel-certified recordings close early.
  • Pull the tax certification and any unpaid tax before the closing date.
  • Ask the title agent how the Statement of Value is being counted in the page total.
  • Collect a return envelope with correct postage if the deed is coming back by mail.

Open mortgage balances get released through a satisfaction piece, which costs $61.75 to record. Ask the lender how long it takes to file one so the buyer's title is clean. A cash sale skips the lender's recording package, which leaves fewer documents to count and price.

Local housing snapshot

The county has an estimated 324,411 residents as of 2025, with Easton as the seat and Bethlehem as the biggest city. The latest five-year survey shows a $308,600 median home, $89,184 median household income and owners in 71.1 percent of occupied units. Housing costs sit well below Montgomery County to the south.

What will it cost to file a deed in Easton?

Plan on $76.25 for a deed of four pages and four names. Add $10 per certified parcel, $2 for each extra page and 50 cents for each extra name.

Can I pay the recorder with a personal check?

No. The office takes business checks, certified checks, money orders and cash, and caps a check at five documents.

Can I overpay the recording fee?

No. The office wants the exact fee with each document and refuses overpayments, so work out the total before the package goes out.

When does the recorder stop taking documents?

The counter stays open until 4:30 p.m., but anything needing a parcel certification must be in by 4:00 p.m. A later deed waits for the next business day.

Who pays the transfer tax on a sale?

State law makes both sides jointly responsible for the 1 percent state tax. The contract decides who actually pays, so check that clause.

Where to record and office hours

Luzerne County deeds are recorded in Wilkes-Barre. The public counter of the Recorder of Deeds is in the Courthouse Annex at 153 N. River Street. Mail goes to 200 N. River Street, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711, and the phone is 570-825-1641. The counter is open Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., except holidays, and the last filings are taken at 4:20 p.m.

A second counter in Hazleton is open only Tuesdays and Thursdays, 10:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. It takes no cash, only money orders, cashier's checks, personal or business checks, and credit cards, and you wait there while staff finish the documents. Electronic recording can be submitted at any hour.

The Assessors' Office is in the same annex. Every deed needs a certified parcel number before it can be recorded, so the two stops go together.

Deed recording fees

Under the schedule effective November 17, 2025, the base charge for a deed or a mortgage is $72.75. That covers up to four pages, four names and one PIN. Since July 1, 2026 the county also adds $15.00 to deeds, exempt deeds and mortgages to fund a demolition program for blighted buildings. Ask the office for the exact total on your document.

Luzerne County recording fees, base amounts effective November 17, 2025
DocumentBase fee
Deed$72.75
Mortgage$72.75
Satisfaction$64.75
Release of mortgage$64.75
Assignment of mortgage$64.75
Deed easement or right of way$64.75
Timber conveyance$33.50
Power of attorney$23.50

Smaller charges to watch for:

  • Each page over four costs $2.00, and each name over four costs $0.50.
  • Each PIN after the first costs $0.50 at the Recorder. The Assessor's Office bills its own fee to certify each PIN, so call 570-825-1525 for that amount.
  • A rejected document costs $10.00 by mail and $5.00 when sent electronically.
  • A returned check costs $35.00.
  • One check can cover at most 10 documents, and an overpayment is not refunded. The office either sends the check back for a corrected one or keeps the extra.

Transfer tax by municipality

The state charges 1 percent, and the county schedule gives the combined rate by municipality. The total is 2 percent everywhere except three places: Wilkes-Barre and Pittston at 3.5 percent and Kingston Borough at 2.5 percent. Hazleton's total is 2 percent. The county has 76 municipalities, so confirm which borough, city or township your house is in before you work out what you will net.

Both the person selling and the person buying are liable to the state for the tax. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue exempts certain family transfers, transfers by will or intestacy, and transfers to government units. A deed claiming an exemption should say why, for example parent and child. A non-family exemption needs a Statement of Value.

If a property sits in two municipalities, the deed has to state what percentage lies in each, because the local portion is split between them.

What a recordable deed needs

Every deed, mortgage and assignment must carry a PIN certified by the Assessor's Office and a signed, certified address for the grantee or mortgagee. Have the Assessor certify the number in the top margin, and leave a blank 2 1/2 inch margin at the bottom of at least two pages for the recording stamps.

  • Statement of Value (REV-183): one original and one copy, completed with the school district, assessed value and common level ratio, then signed and dated by someone connected to the transaction. It counts as a page, and attached exhibits cost $2.00 a page too.
  • Numbering: when several documents make up one transaction, number them in the order they should be recorded. If they arrive in the wrong order, the presenter pays for re-recording.
  • Self-addressed stamped envelopes for returning documents and receipts.
  • No non-standard financing forms, and no blanket assignments or blanket releases, which are refused.

Common level ratios effective July 1 of 2024, 2025 and 2026 are posted with the office's related documents. Use the one in effect on the date of transfer.

Searching land records

There are three online routes. Landex Remote is a prepaid account that draws down as you view records, with images from 1968 to the present and indexing from December 1980. Landex Webstore lets you search the indices free and charges for each document you view or print. IQS Infodex, at searchiqs.com/paluze, is free for older deeds from 1786 to 1967 and also holds grantor and grantee indices from 1786 to August 1, 1993.

Certified copies are made only at the office. A plain copy by mail costs $5.00 for the first page and $2.00 for each added page. Staff do not run title searches for individuals or give legal or tax advice, so title work stays with an attorney or title company.

Record Alert for owners

Landex also offers a free Record Alert service. It watches up to five PINs or names and emails you when a document is recorded against them. It cannot stop a filing, since the office must record any properly executed document that comes with payment, but it gives an owner early warning of a fraudulent deed. Sellers who still own other parcels, or who inherited property, can sign up while the title is in transition.

From closing table to the record

Most sellers never visit the counter, because the title company or attorney handles the filing. The order of events is the same either way. The Assessor's Office certifies the PIN on the deed, the Statement of Value and the signed grantee address are put with it, and the package goes to the Recorder with one payment covering the recording fee, the county charge and the transfer tax. Electronic submission avoids the trip and the wait at either counter, and a rejected electronic filing costs less than a rejected paper one.

If you do file yourself, check each item in the list above first, bring a check made out correctly, and include the stamped return envelopes. A missed margin or a wrong page order sends the deed back and costs you the rejection fee plus another round.

Before you sell in Luzerne County

Luzerne County is a home rule county with 76 municipalities, and Wilkes-Barre, Hazleton, Kingston, Nanticoke and Pittston are its largest places. The 2020 census counted 325,594 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 332,126. Your address decides the transfer tax and the yearly tax, so check the municipality and school district on your tax bill before you quote a net figure to a buyer.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the base fee to record a deed in Luzerne County?

The base fee is $72.75 on the schedule effective November 17, 2025, with $15.00 added from July 1, 2026 for the county demolition fund. The office can confirm the current total.

What is the realty transfer tax rate in Luzerne County?

The county lists a 2 percent total in most municipalities. Wilkes-Barre and Pittston are 3.5 percent, and Kingston Borough is 2.5 percent.

Can I pay for Luzerne County recording with cash?

The Hazleton counter takes no cash, only checks, money orders, cashier's checks and cards. Ask the Wilkes-Barre counter before you bring cash there.

Does Luzerne County require a Statement of Value?

One is required when a deed claims a non-family exemption. File one original and one copy, completed, signed and dated.

How can I find an old Luzerne County deed?

Search Landex for records from 1968 forward, or the free IQS Infodex site for deeds from 1786 to 1967. Certified copies must be requested at the office in person.

Office location and recording hours

You'll find the Recorder at 123 Wyoming Avenue, Suite 218, Scranton. Call 570-963-6775. The office keeps 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. hours, though recording submissions end at 3:45 p.m.

A signed deed can reach the office three ways: carried in, dropped in the box in the main lobby of the Government Center, or sent by U.S. Mail. Title companies often skip all three and file electronically through Simplifile, CSC or ePN, the vendors the county lists on its Recorder of Deeds page.

Besides recording and indexing property documents, the Recorder collects realty transfer tax on behalf of the state, the municipality and the school district. A seller reaches this office at the very end, once the deed has been signed and notarized.

What a deed must contain

Lackawanna's written recording requirements have tracked national PRIA document standards since September 1, 2024. A closing package that comes back usually lacks one of the items below.

  • Letter-size paper (legal size is tolerated), 12-point type or larger, and a one-inch margin on every page.
  • Original signatures in dark ink. Handwriting isn't allowed anywhere else on the page, and highlighter marks aren't allowed at all.
  • The full legal description, naming municipality, county and state, along with the county tax parcel number. The Assessment Office certifies each parcel number before the deed is recorded, and mailed packages are forwarded there first.
  • An acknowledgment taken by a notary or other authorized officer, with the date, the signer's name, the notary's signature and the commission expiration date.
  • The buyer's signed Certificate of Residence, with an exact address.
  • Written dollar amounts that match the numbers, since consideration is checked against the transfer tax paid.

Re-recording won't repair a deed. A Corrective Deed is the only fix, and it must carry a Statement of Value, an explanation, and a full copy of the deed being corrected.

Paying the recorder

Bring a check for the exact amount. Credit cards aren't taken, overages aren't refunded, and every check should have the submitter's address printed on it.

Payment rules from the recording requirements sheet, revised August 2024
SituationRule
Transfer tax and recording feeOne check can cover both
Documents per checkUp to 4 in one land transaction
Checks per transaction batchUp to 3
Overpayment of $5.00 or lessForfeited
Overpayment above $5.00Document is returned
Returned check$20.00 fee

Payee is the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. The office refuses a check whose memo line points to some other land document, and it may ask for ID to confirm the address printed on a check.

Base amounts vary with the number of pages, names and parcels. Use the fee calculator on the county's Recorder page, or phone the office, before you write the check.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lackawanna County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Realty transfer tax on a sale

The tax is taken at the counter when the deed is recorded. The state's share is 1 percent of the value, and both buyer and seller answer to the Department of Revenue for it. The municipality and school district add their own local portions.

Certain transfers are exempt, such as some between relatives and property passing under a will or by intestacy. Even so, the exemption has to be spelled out in the deed or on a fully completed Statement of Value.

  • Land in several municipalities: the deed lists each one's percentage and dollar amount in whole numbers, supported by a Statement of Value.
  • Wrong location on the deed: the submitter owes the correct tax to the correct municipality and must chase the refund from the one paid in error.
  • Easements: these need a Statement of Value too, and it counts toward the page total.

Recent fee changes

The combined court and AOPC portion of the surcharge on every recording is now $41.25, up from $40.25. It followed a state budget change signed on November 12, 2025, and the Recorder began collecting the higher amount on November 17, 2025. Packages mailed in with the old amount were sent back to be redone.

Since January 1, 2026, attachments on e-recorded documents, such as a Corrective Deed or Deed of Trust, cost an extra $0.50 per page, because the office must print them for the Department of Revenue. Documents brought in, dropped off or mailed don't pick up that per-page charge.

If your closing package was prepared from an older checklist, ask the office for the current total before sending a check.

The Lackawanna County reassessment and your sale

The county finished its first full reassessment in nearly 60 years in 2025, moving values off 1968 levels to current market values. A 2022 resident lawsuit led a court to order it. The Assessment Office says the county millage rate fell from 89.98 to 5.79 mills to keep the change revenue-neutral.

The county describes the result as roughly a third of owners paying more, a third paying less and a third about the same. A quarterly payment option was introduced for property tax bills. Pull the current assessment record before you list, since an old tax bill no longer tells a buyer much.

Assessment appeals open again on April 1, 2027, and the next Clean & Green application window starts March 1, 2027. The county also posts a form under Act 29 of 2026 for owners of rentals, LLCs, trusts and other entity-held property bought on or after September 18, 2026.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lackawanna County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Lackawanna County housing snapshot

The July 2025 estimate shows 216,502 residents and 100,686 housing units. For 2020 to 2024, 65.4% of homes are owner-occupied, with a median value of $201,800. Renters pay a median of $1,007.

Scranton is the county seat and Carbondale is the other city. If you price a vacant house in winter, plan for snow-season showings and heating costs.

What to bring to a Lackawanna County closing

Gather these items first and the counter clerk has little reason to turn you away.

  • The original deed, inked and acknowledged, with a legible notary stamp and no typing or handwriting added on top of it.
  • The parcel number and legal description.
  • The buyer's signed Certificate of Residence.
  • A completed Statement of Value if any tax is excused or the price is not shown on the deed.
  • One check for the exact total, printed with your return address.
  • A self-addressed stamped envelope if you want the recorded original mailed back.

Get it to the counter by 3:45 p.m. on a business day, or let the title company file it electronically.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Lackawanna County recorder take credit cards?

No. Plan on a check for the exact total, payable to the Lackawanna County Recorder of Deeds. One check may cover recording and transfer tax together.

What is the last time of day to record a deed in Scranton?

3:45 p.m. The counter opens at 9:00 a.m. and the office closes at 4:00 p.m. Anything delivered after 3:45 is handled the next business day.

Is a tax parcel number required on a Lackawanna County deed?

Yes. Any document tied to real estate carries the county tax parcel number, which the Assessment Office certifies before recording. Mailed packages are routed to that office first.

How do I correct an error in a deed that is already recorded?

Record a Corrective Deed. Re-recording the original doesn't work. Attach a Statement of Value, a reason for the change, and a full copy of the deed you are fixing.

Who owes the state's 1 percent realty transfer tax on a sale?

The Department of Revenue treats buyer and seller as jointly liable. Your sales contract decides who actually pays. The Recorder collects the tax with the deed and distributes it to the state, municipality and school district.

Where the recorder's office is

The Recorder of Deeds is in the Dauphin County Courthouse, Room 102, 101 Market Street, Harrisburg. The counter is staffed weekdays from eight until half past four, and the phone is (717) 780-6560.

Anything filed against Dauphin County land goes through this counter or its online equivalent: deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements, plans and powers of attorney. The office records, reproduces and indexes documents the law allows to be recorded. Title advice is outside its role.

If you sell through a title company, you will rarely deal with the office yourself. The settlement agent prepares the deed, adds the fees and transfer tax, and sends it in.

Recording fees

A deed and a mortgage each carry an $87.75 fee on the schedule revised December 1, 2025. Any document that needs a Unified Parcel Identifier adds $20.00 for each identifier.

Dauphin County recording fees by document

A page past the fourth costs $2.00, and a name past the ninth costs fifty cents. Simple instruments such as affidavits, agreements, releases and notices run $18.50.

The Commonwealth sets these fees through the General Assembly, and they can change. A fee calculator on the office web page works out the total for a given document.

Transfer tax split

A 2% levy applies to what is paid for the property. One point goes to the Department of Revenue, with a half point apiece for the township or borough and the school district.

Both parties to a deed share liability for the state's portion, and the recorder forwards it. The purchase agreement is where buyer and seller decide who pays.

  • Conveyances between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and brothers and sisters are exempt, and other exemptions exist in special cases.
  • A deed for nominal consideration, such as $1, between tax exempt parties carries $0 of transfer tax and does not need separate checks.
  • State law also exempts property passed by will or by intestate succession, burial site deeds and certain transfers to governments.

Have the settlement agent confirm the final tax figure before closing, since it depends on the price.

Steps for a seller

For most sales the path looks like this. At closing you sign the deed in front of a notary. The settlement agent then works out the recording fee, adds $20.00 for each parcel identifier, calculates the transfer tax from the price and writes the checks. The package goes to Room 102, and the recorded original returns to the agent in a day or two.

If you are selling on your own, call (717) 780-6560 first, confirm the total for your page and name count, and bring a check made out to the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds. Keep the receipt. A cash sale changes nothing here, because the same deed, fees and tax apply whether or not a lender is involved.

After recording, ask the agent for a copy of the deed. You can also search the online index later to see that the new owner's name now appears.

Paying fees and getting the original back

Cash and checks are the accepted payment methods, and checks name the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds. Mailed packages need a stamped return envelope with your address and the correct amount.

The original usually comes back to whoever presented it within a day or two, though busy periods, holidays and staffing can stretch that. If two weeks pass with nothing in hand, ask the firm that filed it.

Large closings often go through a title company, so ask which firm will submit the deed and how it will pay.

Record search and history

The first recorded registry dates to 1785. The office website holds deeds and miscellaneous documents from 1785 forward and mortgages from 1979 forward, and the deed indexes and a mortgage index are online under the Alpha Index.

Each document is scanned, and the original is held until at least two people have checked and proofed the indexes and records. Images are backed up to hard drive and microfilmed to meet Pennsylvania Historical Museum Commission requirements. The microfilm is stored off-site in an underground facility so records can be rebuilt after a courthouse disaster.

Nearly everything recorded is public. The exception is a military discharge paper, DD214. Search access requires accepting the office's disclaimer, which states that the official records are the ones held in the office.

Notaries, plans and burial plots

New notaries start here. Bring identification, the completed notary bond and payment. The office records the bond and commission and administers the oath, and the notary then walks to the Prothonotary to register a signature. No appointment is needed, and the filing fee is $33.50.

The office also takes plans at $20.50 for the first page and $5.00 for each page after, and files Uniform Commercial Code statements at $100.00. Certified copies cost $2.00 plus the per page copy charge. Microfilm copies are $0.75 and photocopies are $0.50 a page.

Burial plots confuse people. A cemetery lot deed usually grants permission to use the ground while the cemetery keeps title, and those papers are held by the cemetery company or association rather than the county.

Questions that come up before a sale

A few questions repeat at the counter.

  • A change of ownership needs a new deed prepared and recorded. Merely stating a change does nothing.
  • After a mortgage is paid, the lender typically sends a satisfaction to the office. The owner does not get a new deed.
  • If a spouse dies and the couple held title as tenants by the entirety, the survivor generally explains the death in the next deed or mortgage. Other forms of title, such as tenants in common, may need different handling, so ask an attorney.
  • A deed for a lot usually covers buildings erected on it, now or later.
  • A deed gives a legal description of boundaries, but a surveyor places markers on the ground.

Anyone can write their own deed, though an attorney is the safer choice so the recording criteria are met and the right fee is enclosed.

Dauphin County housing

The county had an estimated 293,351 people in July 2025, up from 286,401 in the 2020 count, and 129,660 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home value is $236,400, and owners occupy 63.1% of homes. Median gross rent is $1,217, median household income is $76,242, and 329 building permits were issued in 2025.

What will a Dauphin County deed cost to record?

The deed fee is $87.75 on the December 1, 2025 revision, with $20.00 added for each Unified Parcel Identifier and $2.00 for every page after the fourth. Transfer tax is figured separately from the sale price.

What transfer tax rate applies in Dauphin County?

The rate is 2% of the value conveyed, divided as 1% for the state and a half percent each for the municipality and school district. Some transfers between close relatives are exempt.

Does the Recorder of Deeds accept cards?

Cash and checks are the listed payment methods for recording fees. Make checks payable to Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds, and phone (717) 780-6560 before relying on any other method.

When does a recorded deed come back to me?

Usually within one to two days, though volume, holidays and staffing can add time. After two weeks without your papers, contact whoever submitted them.

Can I search Dauphin County deeds online?

Yes. The office website has deeds and miscellaneous documents from 1785 and mortgages from 1979, searchable after you accept a disclaimer. Military discharge papers are the one category closed to the public.

Where to take a Cumberland County deed

Recording happens at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Historic Courthouse, One Courthouse Square, Carlisle. Every deed, mortgage and related paper for land in the county's boroughs and townships is indexed there.

The counter is open weekdays, with an occasional remote day, and shuts at four in the afternoon. Visitors are asked to book an appointment, and notaries and anyone filing a subdivision plan must have one. Call 717.240.6370 or email recorder@cumberlandcountypa.gov to set a time.

Most sellers never make the trip. The closing agent drafts the deed, collects the money and submits the package for you.

Recording fees

A deed costs $104.75 to record under the price list dated November 17, 2025. That figure includes the $20 parcel identifier charge where one is needed, and each parcel after the first adds another $20.

Cumberland County recording fees by document
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$104.75
Mortgage$104.75
Satisfaction piece$78.25
Assignment of mortgage$78.25
Agreement of sale$78.25
Power of attorney with a parcel number$37.00
Notary public$34.00
Subdivision plan$47.00

Each page past the fourth adds $2.00, and each name past the fourth adds fifty cents. A Statement of Value is $1.00 extra.

Deed and mortgage prices went up on that date because of a one dollar increase in the Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025. The state sets most amounts, while the parcel identifier fee comes from a county ordinance.

Transfer tax on a Cumberland County sale

The Recorder collects the tax at the counter when a taxable deed comes in. The total burden is 2% of the price: one point goes to the Commonwealth, and the other point is split equally between the municipality and the school district. Funds move to those bodies at month end, and the county keeps 1% of the state share and 2% of the local share as a commission.

  • State law makes the grantor and grantee jointly responsible for the tax, so the sale contract is where you decide who pays.
  • Some family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy are exempt. Staff cannot rule on exemptions, so ask a lawyer or the Revenue Department.
  • A Statement of Value, form REV-183, goes with the deed when an exemption is claimed, when the real consideration differs from the figure on the face of the deed, or when the deed is over 30 days old.

Ask your closing agent for the combined tax figure before you sign, since it comes out of your proceeds unless the contract says otherwise.

Paper and electronic filing

Electronic recording is available through three vendors: ePN, CSC and Simplifile. Attorneys and title companies file most documents this way.

Paper still works. A mailed deed needs original signatures and notary stamps, because a photocopy cannot be recorded. If the check or card amount is wrong, the package comes back unfiled, unless the overage is $10 or less, in which case the office keeps the difference and records the paper.

Make checks payable to Recorder of Deeds. Cards are processed through Value Payment Systems with a 2.25% charge, a $2.50 minimum, and 3% on business cards. Cash refunds are not given.

Deed books and searching records

The office has kept a continuous record since 1750, so a title search can reach deeds from the colonial period. The books came through the courthouse fire of 1845 unharmed and were hidden away during the Confederate invasion of 1863.

Until 1929 every instrument was copied by hand into canvas bound volumes. Typed books followed, with separate indexes for deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers until December 1993, when the index was computerized. Paper books ended in 2001, and the old volumes moved from the courthouse to the County Archives in November 2017.

Landex lets anyone search back to 1750 around the clock, and public computers in the office do the same job. Searches run by name rather than address. To find out who owns a parcel, ask the Tax Assessment Office or use the county's GIS Property Mapper.

Liens, title and what staff can do

Clear every lien before closing. The Recorder only holds mortgages and secured transactions, while judgment liens, municipal liens and state tax liens are filed with the Prothonotary, so a title search should cover both offices.

  • A lender records a satisfaction piece when a mortgage is paid off. The homeowner does not receive a new deed.
  • Staff are not bonded and may not search title or advise on law. Hire a title searcher, an abstract company or an attorney.
  • Plans from the early 1900s onward may be on file, and a deed's property description often cites a plan book and page.
  • A veteran can record a DD214, and a certified copy is free if the original is lost. Discharge papers are closed to public view.

If your property reaches the Tax Claim Bureau's online upset sale, the 2026 sale terms add transfer tax and recording fees on top of the winning bid. That tax is the assessed value, times the Common Level Ratio Factor, times 2%.

No redemption period exists once an upset sale closes. An owner may still file objections or exceptions with the local court up to thirty days after the court's confirmation nisi of the consolidated return. If you owe back taxes, call the Tax Claim Bureau at 717-240-6367 before any listing goes live.

Cumberland County housing and taxes

The county's estimated population was 277,270 in July 2025, up 6.9% from the 2020 base, spread over 545.48 square miles. There are 114,465 housing units. Owners live in 71.3% of occupied homes, and the median owner-occupied value is $277,600 for 2020 to 2024. A typical household brings in $87,494, and typical gross rent is $1,249. Permits for 745 buildings were issued in 2025.

The 2026 county rate is 2.875 mills, with municipal and school rates added. Totals on the county's sheet run from about 15.95 mills in Hampden Township to about 27.27 mills in Newville Borough, so where the house sits makes a large difference in the yearly bill. Buyers notice that, and it can affect what they will pay.

Seller checklist

A few things make a Cumberland County closing go smoothly. Ask the closing agent whether the deed will be e-recorded or mailed, since only a paper package needs original signatures delivered. Confirm the final fee total against the November 17, 2025 price list, including extra parcels, pages and names.

If anyone in the transaction needs the counter, such as a notary or a plan filer, book that appointment first. Pay off and release any mortgage so the lender records its satisfaction piece, and check with the Prothonotary for judgment or municipal liens. A cash sale skips the lender's mortgage, but the deed, tax payment and recording steps are unchanged.

Frequently asked questions

What does Cumberland charge for a deed recording?

A deed is $104.75 on the price list dated November 17, 2025, with the $20 parcel identifier fee included where required. Pages past four are $2.00 each and names past four are fifty cents each. Transfer tax is paid on top.

Which party owes the transfer tax on a Cumberland County sale?

Under state law both do: grantor and grantee answer jointly. Who actually pays is a matter for the sale contract. The tax totals 2% and is collected when the deed is recorded.

Will the Recorder of Deeds research my title?

No. Staff may not conduct title searches or give legal advice, though they can show you how to use the public terminals. Records are indexed by name, so a searcher looks up owners rather than addresses.

Does paying off a mortgage produce a new deed?

No. The lender files a satisfaction piece to show the loan is paid, and the original deed remains your proof of ownership. A copy of the deed can be bought through Landex or requested by email from the office.

Can documents be filed by mail or electronically?

Yes, with conditions. A mailed package needs original signatures, notary stamps and the exact fee. Electronic filing must come through ePN, CSC or Simplifile. Plans and notary filings need an appointment.

How does the Westmoreland County recorder process a deed?

A cashier checks it, a barcode goes on every page, it is scanned, and the details are keyed into the index. The Recorder of Deeds in Greensburg describes those four steps on its own pages, and the whole routine is built for speed.

At the first step the cashier confirms that the paper is an original, properly signed, dated and acknowledged before a notary whose seal, signature and commission expiration date appear. Fees and transfer taxes are collected at that moment. Then a 15-digit number is assigned, and a sticker on each page shows the page count, the amount paid and the date and time of recording. After scanning, the document goes back to the person who filed it, in person or by mail. Data entry staff finish the index from the legal description, and a second team double-checks it.

The county says Westmoreland is one of only two counties in Pennsylvania where deeds are recorded and returned right away, with no wait of a day or two. That is useful to a seller, because the new owner's name reaches the public record on closing day. County offices keep normal hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, and they close on the county holiday calendar.

The same office also runs a Veterans' Identification Discount Card program for veterans living in the county, announced on its main page, and it publishes a free guide to searching records by name, instrument number, document category, municipality, subdivision or lot. Searches by tax map number or UPI also work, though only where the original document listed one.

What does the Westmoreland County recorder charge?

A deed or a mortgage costs $110.25 to record. Every listed document includes four names, four pages, one tax map number and one UPI, and the office asks for exact payment with anything sent in.

Westmoreland County recording fees, from the county fee schedule
Document or itemFee

Easement or right of way$82.25

Extra name$0.50
Extra page$2.00
Extra UPI$20.00

Questions about any charge go to 724-830-3518 or ROD@westmorelandcountypa.gov. Payment can be cash, money order, cashier's or certified check, or a personal check with ID. Debit and credit cards are not accepted. When you send several documents, the office will not take one check for more than five, so each document after the fifth needs its own.

What is the 10-digit PIN and why do Westmoreland deeds need one?

It is the parcel identifier number, and Westmoreland County requires it on every document it records. The county describes it as a 10-digit number, and the first digits point to the district, the map page and the lot, which the Tax Claim Bureau explains in its tax sale notes.

Getting the PIN right matters more than most sellers expect. A deed with a missing or wrong number is one of the quickest ways to have a closing package returned. If you cannot find the number on a tax bill, ask the Tax Assessment Office at 40 North Pennsylvania Avenue, Suite 440, Greensburg, or search the county's online record index. The index lets you search by name, by instrument number, or, for older records, by book and page for anything recorded before November 13, 2000.

Tax map numbers were not required until 2009, so documents from before then may not appear in a search by map number.

How do you e-record a deed in Westmoreland County?

Open an account with SimpliFile or CSC and upload the scanned original. Each vendor sets its own sign-up steps, and the county recommends reading them first.

Documents sent that way are first routed to the county's UPI and GIS Tax Mapping department for review, then forwarded to the recorder once certified. Nearly every document type can go this way, with one exception: anything that includes an attachment to the Statement of Value must come by mail or in person. The county explains the reason. An e-recorded attachment would add to the page count, and the office cannot alter the page count, so you would pay for pages that cost nothing when handed over the counter.

  • Stamped, self-addressed envelopes are required for mailed recordings and requests.
  • Include a phone number with your paperwork.
  • Plans must have original signatures, and the 18 by 24 inch plan fee is $49.00 for the first page and $20.00 for each page after that.

What transfer tax paperwork goes with a Westmoreland County deed?

Either the tax itself or a Statement of Value. Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state realty transfer tax, and the Department of Revenue says both buyer and seller are jointly liable. The county's recorder collects it, often alongside a local share.

The county's fee schedule says every deed has to state the true consideration or come with two copies of an Affidavit of Value. Any claimed exemption, whether full or partial, must be backed by that affidavit filed in duplicate, with street addresses, consideration, assessed value, fair market value, mortgages recorded and an explanation of why the transaction is or is not taxable. The affidavit must cite the regulation that supports the exemption.

  • Family transfers are the usual exemption, and the recording rules say the exemption must be clearly stated in the deed.
  • A deed with taxes in more than one municipality must say how the transfer taxes are divided.
  • The county publishes a Realty Transfer Tax Rates sheet; ask the office for it, since the rates differ by municipality.

What is Westmoreland County like for a house sale?

It is a Pittsburgh-area county of 1,036 square miles with 349,324 residents in the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate. 169,961 housing units, 154,979 households and a 78.4 percent owner-occupancy rate for 2020 to 2024.

The median value of an owner-occupied home is $203,500, median gross rent is $879, and median household income is $74,109. Owners with a mortgage have median monthly costs of $1,452. Population has slipped 1.5 percent since the 2020 census, from 354,663.

Greensburg is the county seat, and the county's other cities are Arnold, Jeannette, Latrobe, Lower Burrell, Monessen and New Kensington. Coal, coke, steel and glass built the county after the Civil War, and Volkswagen ran a plant near New Stanton from 1978 to 1988. The county's Land Bank and Development Authority work on vacant, abandoned and tax-delinquent properties, a reminder that older neighborhoods vary a great deal. Nineteen school districts serve the county, among them Greensburg-Salem, Hempfield Area, Norwin, Franklin Regional, Greater Latrobe and Penn-Trafford. Greensburg's January average is 28.7 degrees and its July average 71.8, so a house sees real winters.

Does the Westmoreland County recorder take credit cards?

No. The payment policy lists cash, money orders, cashier's or certified checks and personal checks, and it states that debit and credit cards are not accepted. In person, a personal check needs a valid photo ID and the signer must be present.

Can I e-record every document in Westmoreland County?

Almost all of them. The one exception is a document with an attachment to the Statement of Value, which must be mailed or brought in. Use SimpliFile or CSC for everything else.

What happens if I send several documents in one envelope?

The office accepts one check for no more than five documents. Enclose a separate check for each document beyond the first five, plus a stamped, self-addressed return envelope.

Is a PIN required on a Westmoreland County deed?

Yes. Westmoreland County requires a 10-digit parcel identifier number on all documents, in addition to the usual acknowledgment and notary details. Ask the Tax Assessment Office if you cannot find it.

Where does a Washington County, PA deed get recorded?

The office dates from 1781, the year the county was cut out of Westmoreland County. By its own account it records deeds, mortgages, subdivision plans and other papers the state treats as permanent, collects the fees and taxes attached to them, and sends the receipts on to the state, the county, the municipalities and the school districts. Everything is indexed, verified and scanned the same business day.

A Washington County sale ends at this counter. The deed is signed at closing and then recorded here, which is the moment the buyer's name enters the public record. CJEA surcharge after the fiscal code changeUp from $2.50 to $3.50, a $1 increase

The county explains that the printed schedule lags behind the $1 CJEA increase, so a recent schedule on the site may show a figure $1 lower than what the counter collects. If the total is unclear, the office asks you to call 724-228-6806 rather than guess.

Two small details catch people out. The PIN charge applies per parcel number, so a sale that combines several parcels costs more than a single-lot sale. And the extra-page charge adds up on long documents, such as a deed that carries a full legal description and several exhibits.

Who pays realty transfer tax on a Washington County sale?

Both do, in the eyes of the state. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue sets the commonwealth tax at 1 percent of the value transferred and makes grantor and grantee jointly and severally liable, so the state can pursue either party for the whole amount.

County recorders collect that share and usually a local share too, then pass the money along. Washington County's page lists the state, county, municipalities and school districts as the recipients, which means the local rate follows the municipality. Get the combined rate from the recorder or your closing agent before you settle on a net price.

  • Exempt transfers include some between relatives, some to government bodies, and property passing under a will or by intestacy.
  • An exemption claim normally needs paperwork, so ask the office which form goes with the deed.
  • Who bears the cost is a term of the sale contract, not something the recorder decides.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Washington County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What formatting rules can get a Washington County document rejected?

Page size and type size are the two that the county stresses on its recorder page. The office no longer accepts legal-size pages electronically, and it sets minimum fonts: 12 point on letter-size pages and 14 point on legal-size pages.

Subdivision plans follow their own rules. They are filed on paper or mylar, and they need signatures from the Washington County Planning Commission, the local planning commission where one applies, the board of supervisors or borough council, and the owners of the land being divided. The plan also carries an engineer's seal, and it has to be recorded within 90 days of the local governing body's approval.

  • Check page size before you scan a deed for e-recording.
  • Confirm the type size on a long exhibit, since small print is a common reason for a bounce.
  • For a plan, count the 90 days from the local approval, not from the date you finish the drawings.

What is Washington County like for a house sale?

It is a large, mostly owner-occupied county south of Pittsburgh. QuickFacts credits it with 210,802 residents in 2025 on 857 square miles of land, plus 99,340 housing units and 88,505 households in the 2020 to 2024 survey.

About 76.1 percent of households own where they live. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $228,500, rent runs a median $949, and the typical household earns $78,958. People with a mortgage pay a median $1,618 a month in housing costs.

Washington is the county seat and Monongahela the only other city. Canonsburg and Charleroi are two of the larger boroughs, and Peters Township is the biggest municipality. Washington & Jefferson College is in the city of Washington, coal mining continues at the Enlow Fork mine, and the Southpointe business park spreads over more than 800 acres. About 37.8 inches of snow fall in a typical year, mostly from November to April, so buyers touring an older house will look hard at the roof and the furnace.

Which school districts and towns shape buyer demand in Washington County?

Canon-McMillan, Peters Township, Charleroi, Burgettstown Area and Chartiers-Houston are among the districts that draw different groups of buyers. The county is split into many small districts, so neighbors on opposite sides of a boundary can pay different school taxes.

For that reason, a listing in Washington County sells better when it names the district. Peters Township is the largest municipality, and Charleroi is a river borough named after the Belgian city, because Belgian glassmakers settled the Monongahela area in the late 1800s. The countywide median home value of $228,500 hides a lot of variation, so look at recent sales inside the specific district.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Washington County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What if the house has unpaid taxes before the deed is recorded?

Two county offices share the work. The Treasurer collects county taxes at 95 W. Beau St., Suite 130, 724-228-6780, with the counter open 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. The Tax Revenue Department, in Suite 525 at 724-228-6850, handles both assessments and delinquent claims.

Since October 6, 2025 the Treasurer has refused personal checks for delinquent taxes. Certified checks, money orders, cash and cards are accepted. Paying online adds a charge: 2.50 percent with a $2.00 minimum on cards, or $1.50 for an electronic check.

When back taxes are attached to the house you plan to sell, request a written balance from Tax Revenue ahead of closing so your closing agent can settle it from the proceeds. Washington County also has a Board of Assessment Appeals, and Tax Revenue can describe the filing steps.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Washington County recorder stop accepting deeds?

Recording ends at 4:00 p.m., half an hour before the office closes. The address is 95 W. Beau St., Suite 520, Washington. A deed that shows up after 4:00 p.m. is held for the next business day.

Can I record a legal-size deed electronically in Washington County?

No. The county says it no longer accepts legal-size pages electronically. Letter-size pages need at least 12 point type and legal-size pages need at least 14 point, so bring a paper original if the document is on legal paper.

Does a Washington County deed fee cover extra pages and names?

The base fee covers four pages, four indexed names and one PIN. Each page beyond four costs $2.00, each extra name $0.50 and each extra PIN $10.00, and the county added $1 to its CJEA surcharge, so confirm the total by phone at 724-228-6806.

How can I look up recorded deeds in Washington County, PA?

Use Landex online, which holds deeds from 1781 to the present, or use the public computers inside the Recorder of Deeds office. Landex support is 1-800-370-2836, option 4, according to the county page.

Who owes the transfer tax when a Washington County house sells?

Both sides are liable. Pennsylvania charges 1 percent of the value transferred and holds buyer and seller jointly responsible, and a local tax normally rides along. The sale contract decides who pays in practice; the recorder can confirm the local rate.

Where to record a deed in Erie County

Erie County deeds are recorded by the Recorder of Deeds, a division of the Erie County Clerk of Records. The office is in Room 121 of Erie County Courthouse I, 140 W. Sixth Street, Erie, PA 16501. Call 814-451-6246, fax 814-451-6213, or write to recorder@eriecountypa.gov.

The office reviews, records and indexes every document that touches Erie County real estate, then makes those records open to the public and to title professionals. Between 100 and 400 documents arrive each day. A deed with a missing page or the wrong fee can sit in a pile of returns, which delays the new owner's name appearing in the record.

The recorder also collects money for others: the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, the Department of State, and the municipalities and school districts in the county. The office is not funded by county tax dollars, and the county says it brings in more than it spends. Staff can't give legal advice about your deed. Send questions about wording to a lawyer or your title company.

Recording fees

The base fee for an Erie County deed is $87.00 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. Mortgages and a few other conveyance-type papers carry the same base fee, and smaller instruments cost less.

Erie County base recording fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025
InstrumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage, excerpt of adjudication, declaration of acquisition$87.00
Mortgage satisfaction, assignment or release$59.75
Easement, right of way, land contract$59.75
Lease over 30 years$59.75
Lease under 30 years, agreement exempt from transfer tax, all other instruments$18.50

Add-ons apply when a document runs larger than the base covers.

  • Indexed names over four: $0.50 each
  • Pages over four: $2.00 each
  • Additional parcels: $0.50 each
  • Statement of Value: $2.00
  • Copies picked up, emailed or faxed: $0.25 per page
  • Certification: $1.00 per document

Each amount carries an asterisk on the schedule. Ask the office to confirm the final total before anyone cuts a closing check.

Realty transfer tax on a home sale

Yes, Erie County charges it. The office collects Pennsylvania and local realty transfer tax on all realty transfers and passes the money to the Commonwealth and to the municipality or school district. The county points to 72 P.S. Section 8101-C and following, and 61 Pa. Code Section 91.101 and following, as the governing rules.

Some transfers are exempt. The county gives transactions between husband and wife, between parent and child, and between siblings as examples. Don't assume a family sale qualifies. The claim is made on the Statement of Value form, and the recorder reviews what the paper shows.

  • The Statement of Value costs $2.00 to record.
  • The Common Level Ratio changes with the fiscal year, so ask the recorder which factor applies to the date on your document.
  • The local rate depends on the municipality. Ask the office for the rate in your township, borough or city.

Buyer and seller divide the tax the way the sales agreement says. It scales with the sale price, so it is usually a bigger line on the settlement statement than the recording fee itself.

Searching Erie County deeds and ordering copies

The Recorder posts an online index and document images through Infocon, at www.infoconcountyaccess.com. Title companies and other filers can use the office's E-Recording information page.

A fire destroyed the Erie County Courthouse on March 23, 1823, and records made before that date were lost. Anyone tracing a very old chain of title should expect gaps and ask the office what survives.

To record by mail, send the package to Recorder of Deeds, 140 West 6th Street, Room 121, Erie, PA 16501. Enclose the right fees and a Statement of Value if one is needed. Put a return address on the package so the recorded deed finds its way back to you.

Checklist before you send a deed

Most of what slows a recording is avoidable. Before the closing package leaves your hands, run through this list.

  • Count the pages and the indexed names. Pages over four and names over four are billed extra.
  • List every parcel. Additional parcels are $0.50 each.
  • Attach the Statement of Value, and fill in any exemption claim on it.
  • Include one payment that covers the recording fee and the transfer tax. Call 814-451-6246 to confirm the total.
  • Add a return address.

If your title company handles the closing, ask whether it records electronically. That skips the mail and usually gets the deed into the index sooner. Once the deed is recorded, the new owner's name is public record, and the sale is complete as far as the county is concerned.

What happens after closing

The deed is signed at the closing table, then the title company or attorney sends it to the recorder with the fees and the Statement of Value. Staff review it for the items listed above, charge the fees, and index it by name. Only then does the public record show the new owner.

If something is wrong, the office returns the package. A missing page, a wrong fee or an unsigned form means you start the clock again. If you are selling and want to know where your deed stands, call 814-451-6246 and ask. Keep a copy of everything you send, and keep the return address current so the recorded original reaches the right person.

Sellers who plan to hand over the house quickly should talk with the closing agent early about who is sending the deed and how. A package that is mailed, rather than sent electronically, takes longer to arrive and longer to come back.

Other fees on the Erie County schedule

A few items on the schedule come up around a sale. A notary appointment or renewal is $30.50 plus a $3.50 prothonotary fee. A storm water management map, planned community map or condominium plan is $30.00, the same as a subdivision map.

The county also collects low-income housing fees and record management fees along with Erie County recording fees and the Pennsylvania writ tax. State law or local ordinance sets every fee and tax, so the recorder can't negotiate them.

Erie County housing snapshot

Erie County is the northernmost county in Pennsylvania, with Lake Erie along its northern edge. It has two cities, Erie and Corry, plus Millcreek, Harborcreek, Summit and Fairview townships and boroughs such as Edinboro, North East, Girard, Waterford and Union City.

The county has 265,832 residents in the July 2025 estimate, a 1.9% drop from the April 2020 base, and 120,762 housing units. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $177,000.

Frequently asked questions

What is the base fee to record a deed in Erie County?

The base fee is $87.00 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025. Pages over four are $2.00 each and indexed names over four are $0.50 each.

Where do I send a deed for recording in Erie County?

Mail it to Recorder of Deeds, 140 West 6th Street, Room 121, Erie, PA 16501. The office phone is 814-451-6246.

Are family transfers exempt from Erie County transfer tax?

Some are. The county names transfers between husband and wife, parent and child, and siblings as examples. You claim the exemption on the Statement of Value.

How much does a Statement of Value cost in Erie County?

It costs $2.00 on the current schedule. Additional parcels are $0.50 each.

Can I search Erie County deeds online?

Yes. The office offers an online index and images through Infocon at www.infoconcountyaccess.com. Copies picked up or emailed are $0.25 per page.

What the Recorder of Deeds does

Property sales become public record here. Look for the Third Street section, first floor, inside the Beaver County Courthouse at 810 Third Street, Beaver; the phone is 724-770-4560. The counter keeps weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

Recording here began in 1800, and every record has since been digitized. The filing list is long: sheriff deeds, tax claim deeds, satisfactions, assignments, releases, restrictive covenants, leases, installment land contracts, Clean and Green filings and notary bonds, in addition to deeds and mortgages. Pennsylvania realty transfer tax is collected here too, with the local portion sent on to the municipality and school district.

A free Fraud Alert will notify you any time a deed or mortgage is recorded in your name. Since other people in the county may share that name, compare each alert with your own property before you react.

Beaver County housing context

Beaver is the county seat, and Aliquippa is its largest city. An estimated 166,032 people lived here in 2025, in 79,845 housing units. Three quarters of homes (75.0%) are lived in by their owners and typically value $190,900. Estate sales and downsizing moves account for many listings.

Transfer tax on a sale

Expect 2% of the value conveyed. The state keeps 1%, and local governments share the other 1% evenly between municipality and school district. That value may differ from the price you agreed on. Everything is collected when the deed is filed, and no deed is accepted before the tax is paid.

Taxing bodies are indifferent about who writes the check, which leaves it to your purchase agreement. Many contracts split it between buyer and seller, though the buyer is on the hook if the amount is questioned afterward. One check to the Recorder of Deeds can cover the fees and both taxes. Cash or check is all the office takes.

Transfer tax parts and copy charges
ChargeAmount
State realty transfer tax1% of value
Municipal share0.5% of value
School district share0.5% of value
Copy made at the counter$1.00 per page
Copy by mail$5 flat plus $1.00 per page
Certification of a copy$1.50

Deed recording fees changed December 1, 2025, with a new schedule that adds a $1 Criminal Justice Enhancement Account charge under Act 45 of 2025. Ask the office for today’s schedule before you plan your closing costs.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Beaver County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Statement of value and common level ratio

The statement of value is a two-copy state form. It either puts a value on the property or explains why the transfer is exempt. The office wants one when tax is unpaid or when the deed hides the real value, as with $1.00 of stated consideration. Investigators for the state may audit these forms later.

The form calls for the county’s common level ratio, set at 1.34 for documents accepted between July 1, 2026 and June 30, 2027. By 61 Pa. Code 91.02, acceptance is presumed to fall on the execution date written in the deed.

  • Exempt transfers run between spouses, from parent to child, grandparent to grandchild, among siblings, and between stepparent and stepchild.
  • Further exemptions cover particular situations; an attorney or the state Department of Revenue can advise.
  • If the state later decides the value was higher, or an exemption does not hold, the Department of Revenue mails a determination. You pay the added state and local tax plus interest to the state, and the Recorder then disburses the local share.

How to record a deed

Walk it in or mail it. A visit takes roughly 10 to 15 minutes for review, receipt and scanning, and the stamped original comes back by mail within about a week. When a mailed package fails to return after two weeks, contact the Postal Service.

By mail, include a correctly sized check to the Recorder of Deeds and a stamped return envelope with enough postage. Short postage and lost returns are not the office’s responsibility, and cash should never go in the mail. You will probably not do this yourself, since the title company or closing attorney files the deed. Have that person tell you the filing date and forward the recorded copy.

  • Documents that touch more than one municipality need the local tax split clearly stated.
  • Subdivision plans must be 18 by 24 inches or 24 by 36 inches, original on linen or mylar, and no older than 90 days from governing body approval.
  • A military discharge can be recorded through the courthouse basement office that serves former service members, and the Recorder issues certified copies at no charge.

Looking up a deed or mortgage

Beaver County indexes by name, not by street address or tax parcel number. To find a deed or mortgage you need the name of the grantor, grantee, mortgagor or mortgagee and the approximate year. Parcel numbers come from the Assessment Office, so if you only have an address, start there.

Every document in the office is public except military discharge papers, which are impounded. Staff can answer general questions by phone but cannot run searches or give legal advice, so a title searcher or attorney handles anything deeper. To trace ownership backward, read the recital that follows the legal description, usually beginning with the word Being, and follow it through each prior deed toward 1800.

The county records deeds for land only, not buildings. Older deeds sometimes mention when a structure was built, but the Recorder does not keep construction records. Check with the municipality for those.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Beaver County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling with liens or an unreleased mortgage

Confirm that the payoff of your existing mortgage ends with a recorded satisfaction piece. The lender starts that step and may send you the forms. If it fails to file, you can bring or mail the original satisfaction piece to the Recorder with the fee and a stamped return envelope.

Before you list, pull your own name from the index and read what is recorded against it. Open mortgages, old easements and agreements show up there, and clearing a missing satisfaction is quicker before an offer than during the closing window.

  • Gather the last recorded deed and its recital.
  • Ask the Assessment Office for the parcel number.
  • Ask your lender for the recorded satisfaction on any paid-off loan.
  • Agree in writing who pays the 2% transfer tax.

Cash sales and the recording step

When a buyer pays cash, the deed is recorded the same way and the same 2% tax applies. The difference is that no lender stands behind the closing, so there is no loan approval to wait on and no lender checklist to meet. Put the tax split in the contract, ask the closing agent for the filing date, and keep the recorded copy with your sale papers. If you suspect someone filed something against your property, use the Fraud Alert and check the index by name.

Frequently asked questions

Who pays the realty transfer tax when a house sells in Beaver County?

The contract decides, and the county offices do not mind which side pays as long as the full amount is collected at recording. On most agreements the buyer and seller split it, but the new owner is responsible if the amount is questioned later.

What hours is the Beaver County Recorder of Deeds open?

The office is open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, at 810 Third Street in Beaver. The phone number is 724-770-4560, and the office is on the first floor of the courthouse in the Third Street section.

Can I pay the recording fee and transfer tax with one check?

Yes. Recording fees plus the state and local taxes can all be on one check made payable to the Recorder of Deeds. The office accepts only cash or check, and you should not mail cash.

Does the Recorder search by address in Beaver County?

No. The indexes are by the names of grantor, grantee, mortgagor and mortgagee, grouped by year. Parcel numbers and addresses are handled by the Assessment Office.

How long does Beaver County take to return a recorded deed?

A walk-in filing is reviewed, receipted and scanned in about 10 to 15 minutes, and the recorded original is mailed back within about a week. If a mailed filing has not come back after two weeks, contact the Postal Service.

Where deeds are recorded

Butler County deeds are filed at the Recorder of Deeds office in the Government Center, Floor L, 124 West Diamond Street, Butler, PA 16001. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003, and the phone is 724-284-5340. The county's Recorder pages include an online deed search and the current fee schedule.

The county also posts a cover date showing how far recordings have been verified. If that date is earlier than the day you recorded, an index search won't show your deed yet, so look at it before you tell a buyer the record is clean. Subdivision plan books are online starting at Plan Book 315, page 27.

Recording fees

A deed, a mortgage or a re-recorded deed carries a base fee of $87.75 for four names, four pages and one parcel. That rate took effect November 19, 2025. Extras are modest: $1 for each name past four, $2 for each page past four and $0.50 for each parcel past the first.

Butler County base recording fees
DocumentBase fee
Deed, mortgage or re-recording of a deed$87.75
Re-recording of a mortgage$89.75

Mortgage documents pay $2 for each notation past the first. A land contract or article of agreement must carry a Certificate of Residence. Notary commissions and bonds cost $33.50, payable in cash, money order or business check only.

Copy and search charges

Mail requests for record books or instrument numbers run $1 per page, and a certificate and seal of office is $1.50. When you supply the book and page, the service fee is $2 per document. Without them it is $4 per document. Plan book copies by mail cost $2 per page, and an Act 287 search is $2 per township.

  • Maps and plans: $45 covers page one, then $40 for each page after.
  • Highway plans: $15 covers page one, then $3 for every page after.
  • GRID setup: $7 per name.

If a title company wants a copy of an old easement or plat, order by instrument number when you can, since the lower service fee applies once the book and page are known.

Transfer tax on a sale

Pennsylvania charges a 1% state realty transfer tax on the value of real estate conveyed by deed, and the county recorder collects any local tax alongside it. The state holds grantor and grantee jointly liable. Before you price the sale, ask the Butler County Recorder of Deeds for the combined rate in your municipality and school district.

Certain transfers are exempt, such as some family conveyances, transfers to government units, and property passed by will or intestacy. A deed built on an exemption needs the state's Statement of Value to explain it. The county also posts a Common Level Ratio Factor for each July 1 to June 30 period, so check its page for the current one.

Tax sales and what they mean for a seller

The Tax Claim Bureau holds its Upset Sale on the second Monday of each September, for properties two years behind on taxes. A winning bidder takes on past due taxes, liens and mortgages. Properties that don't sell go to a Judicial Sale. Bidding there opens at costs plus deed recording and transfer fees, and the property sells free and clear if every party was properly notified.

Whatever remains unsold goes onto the Repository List. A bidder fills out a bid form, and the Bureau takes the highest bid to the three taxing districts for approval.

The Bureau shares the 124 West Diamond Street address and the P.O. Box 1208 mailing address. Call 724-284-5326, Monday through Friday, from half past eight to 4 p.m. If you're behind on taxes, call before the September sale.

Which place name goes on a deed?

Use the legal municipality, often a township, rather than the mailing-address village. Butler is the only city in the county. Communities such as Renfrew, Lyndora, Herman, Sarver, Cabot, Boyers and Forestville have their own post offices and zip codes but sit entirely inside townships. A deed naming the village can send the recorder, the assessor and the school district to the wrong place.

  • Pull the municipality and school district from the latest tax bill, not from a listing.
  • Match every owner name to the prior deed, since each name past four adds $1.
  • Count pages before you sign, because each page past four adds $2.

A parcel near a boundary belongs to one county only. Confirm the county of record before you send a package.

Butler County housing context

Butler County covers 795 square miles north of Pittsburgh. The city of Butler is the seat and Cranberry Township is the largest township. The 2020 census counted 193,763 residents, and the 2025 estimate is 200,169. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 is $294,200, and 76.9% of homes are owner-occupied. The county issued 1,246 building permits in 2025, so new construction is active. Main roads are I-79, I-76, I-80, US 19 and US 422.

Preparing your filing

Start with the legal municipality and parcel details from your last tax bill. Have your attorney or closing agent draft the deed and count pages and names, so the fee is right. Add a Certificate of Residence if the document is a land contract or article of agreement, and a Statement of Value if you claim an exemption. Bring or mail payment to 124 West Diamond Street, Floor L, and call 724-284-5340 if the cover date or any fee is unclear. If you owe back taxes, call the Tax Claim Bureau at 724-284-5326 before any sale date.

On closing day, ask your closing agent to confirm that any mortgage release or satisfaction will be recorded, because an unreleased mortgage lingers in the index. If you're selling a house that came through an estate or a family transfer, expect the deed to need a Statement of Value, and allow a little extra time for that review.

Frequently asked questions

What is the base fee to record a deed in Butler County?

The base fee is $87.75 for a deed, mortgage or re-recorded deed that has four names, four pages and one parcel. Names over four cost $1 each, pages over four cost $2 each and extra parcels cost $0.50 each. The fee started on November 19, 2025.

Where is the Butler County Recorder of Deeds?

The office is in the Government Center, Floor L, at 124 West Diamond Street in Butler. Phone 724-284-5340. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1208, Butler, PA 16003.

Do I need a Certificate of Residence in Butler County?

Yes for an article of agreement or an installment land contract, which must carry one. The base fee for either document is $59.75 for four pages. Pages over four are $2 each and names over four are $1 each.

Who collects transfer tax on a Butler County sale?

The county Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording. The state rate is 1% of the value, and local taxes can add to that. Ask the office for the rate for your municipality and school district.

When is the Butler County upset tax sale?

The Upset Sale is held on the second Monday of each September. It covers properties that are two years delinquent. Unsold properties move to a Judicial Sale and then to the Repository List.

What the office handles

The Bellefonte office records the deeds, mortgages and related papers for every parcel in Centre County, and it acts as the county's agent for realty transfer tax. Its job is to record, protect, preserve and reproduce the legal documents tied to real estate here.

Official land records begin in 1800, the year the county was formed. The office also records notary commissions, oaths and military discharge papers, and it collects fees for the Affordable Housing Fund and the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts.

Location and hours

The Recorder of Deeds is in the Willowbank Office Building, 414 Holmes Street, Suite 1, Bellefonte, PA 16823. Call 814-355-6801. Doors are open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

  • Documents are taken as close to 5 p.m. as practical, and there are no Saturday or evening hours.
  • You can mail papers in, as long as every recording requirement is met and the right fee is enclosed.
  • A deed that still needs its UPI can go straight to the Assessment Office, which stamps it and forwards it to the recorder.
  • E-recording runs through Simplifile and CSC.

Return time is usually one to two days, though holidays, volume and staffing can stretch it. If nothing has come back after three weeks, contact whoever recorded the paper.

Recording fees

A deed or mortgage costs $71.25 for four pages and four names, plus $2 for each added page and $0.50 for each added name. The Commonwealth sets these fees through the General Assembly, and they can change.

Centre County recording fees
Document or serviceFee

Pay recording fees with cash, check or card. Cards add $3.99 or 2.95% of the transaction, whichever is higher.
