Transfer tax by municipality

The rate is 1% to the state and 1% local on the consideration or value, with three exceptions: State College Borough at 3%, Ferguson Township at 2.75% and Taylor Township at 1.5%. The state share goes to the Department of Revenue, and the local share splits between the municipality and the school district.

The office refuses a deed unless the tax due comes with it. Buyer and seller usually share the bill under the sales agreement. Still, if the amount paid is challenged later, the new owner is the one on the hook for any gap. You don't need separate checks for the state and local shares. Make every check payable to the Centre County Recorder of Deeds.

For a house near the University Park campus, the municipality changes the tax on the same price, so confirm whether the property is in the borough or a township before you set a net figure.

Exempt transfers and the Statement of Value

Exempt transfers include those between spouses, from parent to child, from grandparent to grandchild, and among brothers and sisters. A transfer between ex-spouses also qualifies. Most nonprofit corporations get no exemption. Anything out of the ordinary is a question for an attorney.

The Statement of Value is a state form giving the property's value or the reason no tax is due. Staff pass every one along to the Department of Revenue. You need one whenever the true value isn't on the deed, such as a $1 consideration, or when tax isn't paid at recording. An exemption claim not based on family relationship must give its reason, and a deed on land in more than one municipality must show the local tax split in dollars.

Getting a copy of a deed

Anyone can look at a deed or mortgage, because only military discharges are kept private. Ordering a copy costs $0.50 per page, and certifying it adds $1.50. Send the owner's full name, the property location, a rough purchase date and a self-addressed stamped envelope. If the original is lost, a certified copy takes its place.

The county also runs a subscription portal, WEBIA, covering the recorder, register of wills, tax claim and maps. Records from before 1989 sit in separate Deed, Mortgage and Miscellaneous books, and everything since 1989 is in Record Books, which helps when a title searcher asks for a book and page.

Staff won't search records for you or write a deed. After a death, a surviving spouse who held title as tenants by the entireties generally needn't record anything right away. The next deed or mortgage explains the death. Other forms of ownership can call for different steps, so see an attorney.

Common reasons for rejection

The county gives filers ten instructions, and most failures trace back to names, notary blocks or the UPI.

  • Names in the caption, signature block and acknowledgment must match exactly. Variants like John J. Doe and J Joseph Doe cause rejections.
  • The acknowledgment must show county, state, date, the person or officer appearing, and the notary's signature, seal and expiration date. It shouldn't predate the document date.
  • The written amount must match the numeric amount on deeds and mortgages.
  • Every deed needs a pre-authorized UPI from the Centre County Assessment Office before recording. Call 814-355-6721 with questions.
  • List the property's municipality, and every one if there are several.
  • Leave a one-inch by three-inch space for the recorder's stamp at the top of page one.
  • Include a self-addressed, postage-paid envelope big enough for the return.

Centre County housing context

Centre County is home to the State College metropolitan area, with Bellefonte as the seat and State College as the largest borough. About 157,393 people lived here in 2025, spread over roughly 1,109 square miles. Owner-occupied homes had a median value of $323,500 for 2020 to 2024, and just 61.8% of homes are owner-occupied. Median gross rent is $1,207. A seller in one township may face a different school district tax than a neighbor a few miles away. The county's Common Level Ratio was 6.10 as of July 1, 2026.

Preparing a sale for recording

Get the UPI early from the Assessment Office. It is a $10.00 stamp paid by separate check. Compare every name with the prior deed and look over the notary block. Settle how the transfer tax gets paid, then bring a single check to the Recorder of Deeds. If you can't be there at closing, e-record through Simplifile or CSC or mail the package with a return envelope. Recording protects the buyer, and it keeps tax bills from going to the old owner.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

Do Centre County buyers and sellers need separate transfer tax checks?

No. Separate checks for state and local transfer tax aren't necessary. All checks are payable to the Centre County Recorder of Deeds, and the office accepts cash or check for fees.

How much is the transfer tax in State College?

State College Borough is 3% of the consideration or value, compared with 1% state plus 1% local in most of the county. Ferguson Township is 2.75% and Taylor Township is 1.5%.

Can I record a deed without a UPI in Centre County?

No. Every deed needs a UPI issued by the Centre County Assessment Office, sold as a $10.00 stamp, before it can be recorded. A separate check payable to the County of Centre covers it.

Can the Recorder of Deeds change a deed that is already recorded?

No. Once recorded, a document can't be altered. A new deed showing the change has to be recorded, and a wrong name or description is usually fixed with a deed of correction prepared by an attorney.

Do I have to record a deed at all in Centre County?

A signed and delivered deed is valid, but recording protects the buyer. If it is left off the record, the former owner could still borrow against the property, and tax bills may keep going to the old owner.

Contacting the Monroe County recording office

The Recorder of Deeds is in Room 106 of the Administration Building at One Quaker Plaza in Stroudsburg. The main number is 570-517-3969, and the fax line is 570-517-3873. Doors open at 8:30 in the morning and close at 4:30 in the afternoon on weekdays, with major holidays off.

Walk-in recording and title searches are available, though appointments are strongly encouraged because space is limited. Packages can also arrive by post, or electronically through Simplifile, CSC and EPN. Record books begin in 1836, the year Monroe County was formed from parts of Northampton and Pike counties, and filings made since August 1995 sit on the Landex system.

Along with the recording fee, the office collects realty transfer tax for the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue and for every municipality and school district in the county. It also collects for the Monroe County Affordable Housing Agency, the Commonwealth Court Computer Automation fund, the Equal Access to Justice program and an archive fund for historical preservation of the land records.

The Recorder also runs a free Record Alert System, which sends a notice whenever a document is filed under the subscriber's name. An owner who wants to know about any filing against a property can sign up.

Deed filing fees

A deed or mortgage costs $87.75 under the fee bill that took effect November 17, 2025 and was revised the next day with no fee increase. The bill adds $2.00 for each page over four, $0.50 for each name over four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on a document.

Monroe County Recorder of Deeds fees, effective November 17, 2025
DocumentBase fee

Deed or mortgage$87.75
Easement, 30-year lease, sales agreement$59.75

Power of attorney, other agreements$18.50
Certified copy, added charge$3.00
Mailed copy, each page$1.00

Transfer tax is 1 percent state and 1 percent local. The fee bill also sets payment rules. Personal checks are turned away, the exact amount is required because the office makes no change and gives no refunds, and a rejected document adds a $2.00 charge. Include a postage-paid return envelope so originals can come back.

What a Monroe County deed must contain

The office wants an original that is signed, dated and acknowledged in front of a notary, showing the notary's seal, signature and expiration date. Fees and transfer taxes are due the moment the deed is presented.

  • A tax code number for the parcel.
  • A property description that names the municipality.
  • Payment of the transfer tax. If the tax is unpaid or the deed does not show true value, as with a $1.00 deed, a Statement of Value goes in as two copies and the office forwards it to the state.
  • A return envelope with postage already on it.

Staff will not draft a deed for anyone. Once recorded, a deed stays as written, so adding a spouse or fixing an error means recording a new deed or a deed of correction. Originals go back to the buyer, and mortgages go to the lender. On the lender side, Act 197 lets a satisfaction piece be recorded without the original mortgage or a certified copy of it.

Who pays transfer tax on a sale?

The state share and the municipal share are 1 percent apiece, applied to the property's value, which can differ from the sale price. Contracts often split the bill between seller and buyer. Even so, a deed is turned away unless the tax is paid when it is presented, and the new owner carries the risk if the amount is questioned later.

Family exemptions cover a husband and wife, parent to child, grandparent to grandchild, and brothers and sisters, plus deeds between former spouses. Non-profit corporations get no break. Deeds handed to government units and property that passes by inheritance are also exempt.

A state investigator can decide that a property was worth more than the value stated, or that a claimed exemption fails. The Department of Revenue then mails the owner a determination. Extra tax and interest are paid to the state, a matching municipal sum is paid at the recorder's office, and the deed is recorded again for regular fees.

Unpaid property tax and the Tax Claim Bureau

Delinquent real estate taxes go to the Monroe County Tax Claim Bureau, which handles 20 municipalities and four school districts and receives about 9,000 delinquent returns a year. It exists under Act 542 of 1947, the Pennsylvania Real Estate Tax Sale Law, with the aim of putting tax-delinquent properties back on the productive rolls.

The bureau is down the hall in Room 104 of the same building, at 570-517-3172, and works weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30. A seller with overdue taxes should request a lien certificate so the closing agent can see what must come out of the proceeds. Counter payments can be made with a money order, a cashier's check or a card, and repository sales run through Bid4Assets.

If you are behind on taxes, call the bureau before listing, because the balance has to be settled as part of any sale.

Steps for a Monroe County sale

Start with the tax side. Request the lien certificate if anything is owed. Next, confirm the municipality and the parcel's tax code number, since both go on the deed. At closing the deed is signed and acknowledged before a notary. Your closing agent then files it with the transfer tax and recording fee, either electronically or at Room 106, and the original goes back to the buyer. Because personal checks are refused and no change is given, the payment form and exact amount are worth confirming the day before.

If a family member is receiving the house, tell the closing agent so the exemption is claimed correctly on the deed or a Statement of Value.

The Pocono setting

Stroudsburg is the county seat of this Pocono county in northeast Pennsylvania, which had 168,327 people in 2020. The 2020 census listed 79,114 housing units, 21.3 percent of them vacant, and about three in four occupied homes (76.6 percent) had an owner living in them. Vacation and second-home use is part of the market here, so expect buyers from outside the county and have your tax code number and municipality ready when they ask. Public schools run through four districts: East Stroudsburg Area, Pleasant Valley, Pocono Mountain and Stroudsburg Area.

Frequently asked questions

What is the Monroe County deed recording fee?

A deed or mortgage starts at $87.75. The bill adds $2.00 for every page past four, $0.50 for every name past four, and $10.00 for each tax code number on the document.

Can I pay a Monroe County recording fee with a personal check?

No. Personal checks are not accepted, and the exact amount is required, with no change or refunds. Ask the office which payment forms it takes before sending a package.

Does Monroe County take e-recording?

Yes. Simplifile, CSC and EPN are the three e-recording routes, and paper still works by post or at the Stroudsburg counter.

Which Monroe County deeds are exempt from transfer tax?

Family deeds between spouses, down the line from parent or grandparent, or among brothers and sisters are exempt, and so are deeds between ex-spouses. Non-profit corporations are not exempt. For any other case, talk to an attorney.

Who collects overdue Monroe County property tax?

The Tax Claim Bureau, Room 104 at One Quaker Plaza in Stroudsburg. Its counter takes money orders, cashier's checks and cards, and the bureau can issue a lien certificate for a sale.

The parcel certification stamp

Before the Recorder of Deeds accepts a deed, it needs a tax parcel certification stamp from the Tax Assessment Office. The county requires that stamp on deeds, mortgages, easements, rights of way, land leases and several other instruments, and it has to be completed first.

The Tax Assessment Office charges its own fee for the stamp, $20 per instrument. Questions about the certification go to the assessment office at 570-628-1025. This step is separate from the recording fee and from realty transfer tax, so a seller or closing agent should expect three different amounts on a Schuylkill County deed.

The county also recommends e-recording, which folds the recorder and assessment steps into one submission. That saves postage and avoids the rejection charge described below.

How to pay the recorder

Not with a personal check. Since 2016 the office has refused personal and personal business checks. The list of what it does accept is short.

  • A check from a law firm
  • A certified bank check
  • A money order
  • Cash

Payment goes to "Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds." If a document is rejected for any reason and was sent by mail, UPS or FedEx, the office charges a $3 rejection and return fee, and the sender must include a self-addressed stamped envelope of adequate size for the return. E-recording avoids that charge entirely.

The office also lists what it will not do. It does not supply forms, help prepare legal documents, notarize anything, run real estate searches, certify that a property is free and clear or give legal advice. If you need a title search, that comes from a title company or attorney.

How do I get a copy of a Schuylkill County deed?

Mail or courier a written request that gives the exact book and page number and the year of the document. The office does not search for documents and does not do genealogy research, so a request without those details cannot be filled.

For each document under 40 pages the county charges $8.50 for an uncertified copy and $10.00 for a certified copy. Enclose a self-addressed envelope of adequate size with prepaid postage. The online land records database at uslandrecords.com is the better route when you only know the owner's name, but it needs a computer, internet access and a credit card to pay for printed pages.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Schuylkill County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax when a house sells

Pennsylvania takes 1 percent of the property's value as realty transfer tax, and seller and buyer share liability for it. County recorders collect it, often alongside a local transfer tax shared between the municipality and the school district.

The local portion depends on where the house sits in the county, from Pottsville to the smaller boroughs and townships. Get the combined percentage for your deed from the recorder or closing agent ahead of closing day. That way the settlement sheet agrees with what the office collects.

Several kinds of transfer are exempt: some between relatives, some to government bodies, and property passing by will or intestate succession. A house inherited in Schuylkill County therefore moves to the heirs without that tax, but a sale by the heirs afterward is a new transfer.

Schuylkill County recording rules and state transfer tax

The countywide reassessment

Schuylkill County's last countywide reassessment before this one dated to 1996. Property owners sued in 2018, arguing that assessments no longer met the uniformity requirement in the state constitution, and the county signed a consent decree on May 16, 2022 that committed it to a new countywide assessment.

A vendor, Vision Government Services, collected property data in the field and appraised every parcel with computer-assisted mass appraisal. Owners can appeal to the Schuylkill County Board of Assessment Appeals, and the new assessed values took effect January 1, 2026.

For someone selling, the practical point is that the tax bill a buyer will pay can differ from the bill you paid in earlier years. If your assessment changed, read the notice. Before quoting a buyer a tax figure, ask the Tax Assessment Office how the new value applies to your parcel.

Schuylkill County housing at a glance

Pottsville is both county seat and the one city in the county, which lies in the Coal Region of northeastern Pennsylvania. The July 2025 population estimate is 145,085, and the county has 67,679 housing units. Prices are modest. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $153,000, gross rent has a median of $876 and household income has a median of $68,313. Owners live in 76.1 percent of occupied homes, so most sales run from one owner-occupant to another.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Schuylkill County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to check before the deed is signed

Begin with the parcel stamp, because a deed without it cannot be recorded. Then confirm the payment method: if the closing agent hands you a personal check for the recording office, expect it to be refused.

Look at the paperwork next. A seller with a vacant or inherited house may be facing repairs, back taxes and an unclear title at the same time. Gather the prior deed, any mortgage satisfaction and the latest tax notices. If heirs share ownership, every owner of record has to sign.

Last, find out from the title company who files the deed. Electronic submission through the county's recommended route is quicker, and the recorder confirms the recording by book and page, which you should keep with your closing papers.

Recording steps for a cash sale

A cash sale has fewer moving parts, but the county's steps are the same.

  1. The closing agent gets the tax parcel certification stamp from the Tax Assessment Office, at $20 per instrument.
  2. The agent totals the recording fee, the state 1 percent transfer tax and the local share.
  3. The deed is submitted online, or mailed with a self-addressed stamped envelope and an accepted form of payment.
  4. A rejected mailed package costs $3 to return, so the paperwork is checked before it goes out.

If the house came through an estate, add the heirs' signatures and the estate paperwork to this list before anything is filed. The recorder will not supply forms or help prepare documents, so any gaps are fixed by the title company or an attorney, not at the counter. Once the deed is recorded, note its book and page. The office needs those two numbers if you ever request a copy.

Frequently asked questions

Does Schuylkill County accept personal checks for recording?

No. The recorder has refused personal and personal business checks since 2016. It accepts law firm checks, certified bank checks, money orders and cash, made payable to Schuylkill County Recorder of Deeds.

What is the parcel certification stamp?

It is a tax parcel ID certification the Tax Assessment Office applies before a deed or mortgage can be recorded. The assessment office charges $20 per instrument. Call 570-628-1025 with questions.

What happens if my document is rejected?

A mailed or courier submission that is rejected for any reason incurs a $3 rejection and return fee. You must also supply a self-addressed stamped envelope. E-recording avoids the fee.

How much does a copy of a recorded deed cost?

$8.50 for an uncertified copy and $10.00 for a certified copy, for documents under 40 pages. Send a written request with the book and page number, the year and a prepaid return envelope.

Is there transfer tax on an inherited house?

Title passing by will or intestate succession is exempt from Pennsylvania realty transfer tax. If the heirs then sell, that sale deed is taxed at the state rate of 1 percent plus any local tax, unless another exemption applies.

Lebanon County keeps its land records in Room 107 of the Municipal Building at 400 South 8th Street, Lebanon, PA 17042. Call 717-228-4447. The office is staffed Monday through Friday, opening at 8:30 in the morning and closing at 4:30 in the afternoon.

Everything that touches title to land in the county gets filed here: deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, easements, plans, UCC financing filings and notary bonds. A seller meets this office twice. The deed from the old owner to you was recorded here when you bought, and the deed you sign at closing goes onto the same record. If a mortgage is paid off from your sale proceeds, the lender's satisfaction piece also lands on the county record, usually a few weeks after the payoff.

Staff will help you find a record, but they won't tell you how to word a deed or whether a name should come off one. The office is a custodian of records and sends those questions to an attorney.

Recording fees

A standard deed or mortgage costs $91.75 to record under the fee schedule that took effect November 12, 2025. That base price covers up to four pages and four names, and it already contains the affordable housing fee, the records improvement fee, the parcel identifier fee and the court and access-to-justice surcharges, so those don't show up as separate line items.

Lebanon County recording fees, schedule effective November 12, 2025
DocumentBase feeEach page over 4Each name over 4
Deed$91.75$4.00$1.00
Mortgage$91.75$4.00$1.00
Satisfaction piece$84.75$2.00$0.50
Release of mortgage$81.75$2.00$0.50
Assignment of mortgage$81.75$2.00$0.50
Agreement of sale$79.75$2.00$0.50
Power of attorney (with parcel numbers)$38.50$2.00$0.50

A few smaller charges can matter on a sale:

  • A Statement of Value that has attachments adds $2.00 for each attachment page. The duplicate copy for the state carries no charge.
  • Sending a document by email to the office costs $5.00 plus $0.50 for each page.
  • A returned check costs $30.00.
  • Copies run $0.50 per page on sheets up to tabloid size, and oversized pages add $5.00.

The office takes cash or checks only. Write the check to the Recorder of Deeds for the exact amount, because fees and transfer taxes are due when the document is presented.

What a deed needs before it is recorded

The deed must show a Uniform Parcel Identifier, called a UPI, on page one, and the county Assessment Office must certify that number. The certification happens electronically inside the courthouse. If you don't have the number, call Assessment at 717-228-4425 or use the county property viewer to look the parcel up by address.

The recording instructions add several other requirements:

  • A signed certificate of residence for the grantee on every deed, and for the mortgagee on every mortgage or assignment.
  • Type no smaller than 10 point, and a legal acknowledgment before a notary.
  • A typed English translation attached to any document written in another language.
  • Page numbers or numbering that shows the filing order when several documents belong to one transaction.
  • Where a parcel straddles two or more municipalities or school districts, the percentage lying in each, so the local levy can be split.
  • A return envelope, addressed and stamped, big enough to carry the originals home.

A Statement of Value, the state's REV-183 form, is filed in duplicate with its attachments. It is required when the deed doesn't state the full price, when the transfer is a gift or has no consideration, when an exemption is claimed, and when the property was sold at a tax claim or sheriff sale. A statement isn't needed when full consideration is paid, when the transfer is between close family members, or when the grant is an easement to a public utility. Fill in every block, sign it, and date it with the settlement or acceptance date.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lebanon County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Realty transfer tax

The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of a property's value, paid at the counter with the filing fee. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue holds grantor and grantee jointly responsible. A local levy rides on top, divided between the school district and municipality that cover the house. Call the office or your settlement agent to learn the combined percentage for your street address.

Exemptions cover some family transfers, inheritance by will or intestacy, and government transfers. Anyone claiming one must lay out the basis on the REV-183. The Statement of Value also shows Lebanon County's common level ratio, 1.39 percent.

In a typical sale the settlement agent works out the tax and delivers a check. The purchase agreement says which side absorbs the cost.

Turnaround time and e-recording

Most filings are back with their owners the next business day, by pickup, mail or electronic return. Each document is received, reviewed and keyed in, sent to Assessment to certify the UPI, returned for recording, and then proofread. Documents are recorded in the order they arrive, so a heavy day can lengthen the wait.

Electronic recording is accepted through Simplifile, CSC and ePN, and confirmation can come back in minutes. A mailed filing needs a check for the exact amount plus the return envelope.

Landex, the county's records vendor, also runs record alerts tied to a parcel number. If you own a rental house or a home left empty after an inheritance, ask the Recorder of Deeds how to sign up.

Looking up deeds and mortgages

Documents recorded from 1925 to the present can be searched online through Landex. Anything older has to be viewed at the office in Room 107. Anyone may view the records, with one exception: military discharge papers (DD214 forms) are kept private. They can be recorded for free.

Phone help is limited, because the office isn't insured for title searching. Plan to do your own search online, or hire a title company if the chain of ownership is complicated. A deed describes the land and not the buildings on it, so adding a house to a lot doesn't produce a new deed.

Notary commissions are handled in the same office. The notary fee is $42.00, which includes the Prothonotary fee, paid by one check payable to the Recorder of Deeds.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lebanon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Lebanon County housing snapshot

Lebanon County has an estimated 146,380 residents for 2025, up from 143,257 in 2020. Whether a house sits in Lebanon city, a borough such as Palmyra, or a township changes which municipality and school district receive the local transfer tax, so confirm your municipality before you estimate closing costs.

Frequently asked questions

What is the base deed fee in Lebanon County?

Under the schedule effective November 12, 2025, the base fee is $91.75 and covers up to four pages and four names. Each extra page costs $4.00 and each extra name $1.00. The county accepts cash or check only.

Does Lebanon County require a parcel number on a deed?

Yes. The Uniform Parcel Identifier belongs on the first page and must be certified by the Assessment Office. Call 717-228-4425 to get the number for your property.

Can I record a Lebanon County deed by email or mail?

Mail works with an exact-amount check and a stamped envelope for the return. Email submission is accepted for $5.00 plus $0.50 per page, and electronic recording through Simplifile, CSC or ePN is also available.

How soon will my recorded deed come back?

Most documents are returned the next business day. The wait depends on how many documents were filed ahead of yours, since the office records in order of arrival.

Who owes transfer tax on a Lebanon County sale?

Seller and buyer both answer to the state for it, and the tax is payable at the counter at filing. The sales contract decides who bears the cost in practice, so check it with your closing agent.

Where to record a deed in Franklin County

Deeds are recorded by the Franklin County Register & Recorder at the Administration Building, 272 North Second Street, Chambersburg, PA 17201. The phone is 717-261-3872 and the fax is 717-709-7211.

One office wears several hats. Besides land records, deeds and mortgages, it handles probate for executors and administrators, records military discharges, and collects Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and inheritance tax for the Department of Revenue.

A deed signed at a Franklin County closing finishes its trip here. Once recorded, it becomes part of the land record that every later buyer, lender and title agent searches.

How to submit a deed

The county accepts deeds by e-recording through Simplifile, CSC or EPN, by mail, or in person at the Chambersburg office. Hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. The office is closed on weekends and county-observed holidays.

Searching is done remotely through Landex. For questions about that system, call 717-274-5890. Probate filings are by appointment only, but recording doesn't need one.

  • E-recording: Simplifile, CSC or EPN, with electronic rejection notices that explain the reason.
  • Mail or overnight delivery: rejected documents come back unrecorded with a written explanation.
  • In person: the clerk reviews the document at the counter before it is accepted.

Whichever route you use, the county scans the document and sends it to the Tax Assessment Office for UPI certification. It then returns to the recorder for recording, and the UPI stamp prints on the ending page. A document with a missing or wrong parcel number is returned with a note on what to fix.

Recording fees

A deed or a mortgage is $92.75 on the schedule posted for July 2026, and every document is priced at four pages and four names. The listed fees already include one UPI certification. Each extra certification adds $20.00.

Franklin County fees for common home-sale documents
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$92.75
Deed of distribution (Statement of Value required)$92.75
Mortgage$92.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$81.75
Assignment$81.75
Easement (Statement of Value required)$79.75
Power of attorney to sell real estate$38.50
Statement of Value$1.00

Beyond those, each page past four costs $2.00 and each name past four costs $0.50. Copies are $0.25 per page, copies of subdivisions $0.50, and certification of a document $1.50.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Franklin County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Realty transfer tax

A state tax of 1% and a local tax of the same amount are due at recording, so the combined rate is 2% of the price, or of the assessed value where no price applies.

Every deed must either state the true consideration or carry a Statement of Value. If a full or partial exemption is claimed, the Statement of Value is mandatory unless the deed itself notes the exemption, and it must be fully completed. Corrective deeds and any deed recorded more than 30 days after signing also need one.

  • A deed of distribution from an estate requires a Statement of Value.
  • A property in two or more taxing districts must show the value in each district on the deed so the local share lands in the right place.
  • Pennsylvania lists family transfers, transfers by will or intestacy, and transfers to government units among the exempt categories.

Grantor and grantee are jointly and severally liable, so an unpaid tax can reach either side of a Franklin County sale.

Selling a house that came through an estate

The same office that records the deed also opens the estate, so an heir can handle both in Chambersburg. Probating needs an appointment. The deed that moves title out of the estate is recorded as a deed of distribution with a Statement of Value attached.

Register of Wills fees step up with the size of the estate. Letters and probate run $30.00 for an estate up to $1,000 and $80.00 for one between $75,001 and $100,000, then $35.00 for each additional $100,000 or fraction. Probate also carries a $5.00 automation fee and a $41.25 JCP fee.

  • Short certificates are $5.00 each, and a lender or bank often asks for one.
  • An inheritance tax return or supplemental return is $20.00.
  • Certification of inheritance tax paid is $5.00.
  • An inventory and appraisement is $10.00.

Because the county collects Pennsylvania inheritance tax through this office, an heir who intends to sell the inherited house can finish the estate paperwork and the recording at one counter.

Other recordings around a sale

The deed is the main document, but a few others turn up around a sale. Releasing a loan is recorded as a satisfaction or release of mortgage at $81.75, and a partial release costs the same.

Leases are $38.50 unless they run 30 years, which needs a Statement of Value and costs $79.75. A right of way is $78.75, an installment sales agreement $79.75, and a memorandum $38.50. Farm owners may also record an Ag Security Map at $35.00, and plans on 8.5 by 14 paper are $35.00.

If you had a prior mortgage, confirm before closing that its satisfaction was recorded. A loan that was paid off but never released can still show up in a title search.

Free record alerts for your parcel

The Recorder of Deeds offers a free Landex Record Alert. It notifies an owner when a document carrying their parcel number is recorded or corrected. Sign-up is by email address or mobile number.

The service keys on the parcel number, which is 20 characters including dots and dashes and appears on a tax bill. The county calls the alert a courtesy tool. It doesn't replace your own diligence, paid monitoring or a lawyer. If you suspect fraud, contact local law enforcement quickly.

Signing up before you list is a cheap check. You can see any mortgage, easement or release recorded against the parcel while a sale is pending.

Franklin County at a glance

Franklin County has an estimated 160,652 residents as of July 2025, up 3.0% from the April 2020 base. The median owner-occupied home is worth $249,800 for 2020 to 2024, and owners occupy 73.5% of housing. Chambersburg sits at the center of the county.

Whoever sells a Franklin County house finishes at the Chambersburg office, so the deed paperwork above is the last item to confirm with the closing agent. A cash sale skips the lender's steps, but the recording requirements stay the same. Ask whether the deed will go out by e-recording or by mail, because that choice decides how fast you get the recorded copy back.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the UPI certification in Franklin County?

The first certification is built into the listed recording fee. Each additional UPI certification is $20.00, so a deed covering two parcels adds $20.00 to the posted price.

Can I e-record a deed in Franklin County?

Yes. The Register & Recorder accepts e-recording through Simplifile, CSC or EPN, plus mail and in-person submissions at the Chambersburg office.

What is the Statement of Value fee in Franklin County?

It is $1.00. You need one when a deed claims a transfer tax exemption, when a deed is corrective or recorded after 30 days, and for deeds of distribution.

When is the Franklin County recorder open?

Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office is closed on weekends and county-observed holidays. Probate filings need an appointment.

Who do I call about the Landex search system in Franklin County?

Call 717-274-5890 for Landex questions. The main line at 717-261-3872 handles recording, fees and probate appointments.

Where to record a deed in Fayette County

Deeds for Fayette County property are recorded at the Recorder of Deeds office in the courthouse at 61 E Main Street, Uniontown, PA 15401. The office phone is 724-430-1238 and the fax is 724-430-1458.

Records here go back to 1784. Before that the area belonged to Westmoreland County. The office also records mortgages, releases, satisfaction pieces, plans, powers of attorney, leases, notary bonds and military discharges. DD-214 forms are the one record that isn't public.

For a seller, the recorder is the last stop. The deed signed at the closing table becomes the public record of the new owner only once this office stamps it, assigns an instrument number plus a volume and page, and prints the recording time on every page.

Office and recording hours

The office is open weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., with the front counter shut from 12 to 1 each day. Recording follows the same pattern, so a deed that arrives during the lunch closure waits for the afternoon session.

  • Office hours: 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed 12 to 1.
  • Recording hours: 8 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4 p.m.

If you are delivering a closing package in person, arrive well before 4 p.m. and bring payment. All recording fees and transfer taxes are due at the time of recording.

What a deed must show to be accepted

A deed needs a typed parcel number, a proper notary acknowledgment and correct tax paperwork, or it comes back unrecorded. The county's recording requirements page lays out the rules, and most rejections come from small gaps in them.

  • A PIN (the tax assessment parcel number) must be typed on the first page. The Tax Assessment Office issues a UPI number for it before the document is recorded.
  • The acknowledgment must name the county, state and date, and the person or corporate officer appearing. It needs the notary's signature and commission expiration date. The acknowledgment date can't come before the date of the document. An embossed seal is now optional.
  • The deed must name the municipality, county and state where the land sits.
  • The written dollar amount must match the numerals on every deed and mortgage.
  • Grantee, mortgagee and assignee need a mailing address with ZIP code.
  • Any document that points back to an earlier mortgage must cite its book and page numbers, not a document number alone.
  • A re-recorded document has to explain why it is being recorded again.

Typing or writing on a notary stamp violates Pennsylvania notary law, the county says, so a smudged or altered stamp is a common reason for a bounce. Every document also needs a printed name so it can be returned to the right attorney or title company, along with a self-addressed stamped envelope unless the office will hold it for pickup.

Recording fees

The total is the base fee for the document type plus add-ons. Call 724-430-1238 and the office will quote the current deed figure. These are the add-ons that apply to a typical home sale.

Fayette County Recorder of Deeds add-on fees
Add-onAmount
UPI fee, per PIN number$20.00
Each page over 4$2.00
Each name over 4 (indexing)$0.50
Extra marginal notation$2.00
Copies in the office, per page$0.50
Copies by mail, per page$1.00
Certified copy$3.00 plus the copy cost

The UPI charge is per parcel, which matters on rural sales. A farm assembled from three tax parcels needs three PIN numbers certified, and each one carries the UPI fee.

Paying realty transfer tax

Recording fees and realty transfer tax can go in one check made out to Fayette County Recorder of Deeds. The county fee schedule describes the transfer tax as 1% state plus 1% local.

The deed has to state the price paid, or it must carry a Statement of Value that explains why no tax is due. An original goes into the document as a page and a duplicate goes to the state. Questions about the tax can be emailed to the Department of Revenue realty transfer tax division at ra-bitrealtytransfertax@pa.gov.

When a property lies in more than one local taxing district, the deed must show whole-number percentages for the division of the local share. Buyer and seller are both liable for the tax, and the recorder passes the 1% state share to the Department of Revenue.

Searching Fayette County land records

Index searches for most documents from 1950 to the present are free through the US Land Records site, though images are pay-per-access. Documents recorded before January 1, 2001 are also kept in books in the office, and public search stations in the Uniontown courthouse show the rest.

The recorder indexes by name, with the legal description and municipality, not by street address. For an address or parcel lookup, use the Tax Assessment property search or the Mapping Room at 724-430-1350, extension 229.

  • Archive Viewer indexes cover deeds and mortgages from 1950 to 1974, plans from 1791 to 1988 and agreements from 1854 to 1949.
  • Liens and judgments aren't filed here. The Prothonotary on the first floor of the courthouse handles them at 724-430-1272.
  • Subdivision plans are recorded in this office. Zoning questions go to Planning, Zoning and Community Development on the fourth floor at 724-430-1210.

Steps from closing to recorded deed

Here is the usual path. The deed is signed and notarized at closing. The closing agent gets the PIN certified through the Tax Assessment Office and types it on the first page. The package then goes to the Uniontown office with one check for fees and transfer tax, a printed return name and a self-addressed stamped envelope. Staff stamp it, assign the instrument number and record it.

If you are the seller, ask the closing agent when the package will be delivered. A deed that sits in an office drawer is not yet public record, and a rejected one has to be fixed and sent again.

Selling a house in Fayette County

Fayette County has an estimated 123,021 residents in 2025, down 4.5% from the April 2020 base. Owners occupy 72.4% of homes, and the median owner-occupied value for 2020 to 2024 is $143,200. Median gross rent is $793, which matters if you are weighing a rental against a sale.

Uniontown, where the courthouse stands, anchors the county. A seller who wants a quick closing mainly needs a clean deed, a certified parcel number and a buyer whose title agent knows how the Uniontown office works. A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting steps, but the deed still has to pass the same recording checks described above.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the UPI fee in Fayette County?

The posted schedule shows $20.00 for each PIN number certified. A deed that covers two tax parcels therefore adds $40.00 to the recording bill.

Can I record a deed in Fayette County without a parcel number?

No. The county requires a PIN typed on the first page, and the Tax Assessment Office issues the UPI number before recording. A deed without it comes back unrecorded.

Can one check cover the recording fee and transfer tax in Fayette County?

Yes. The county allows fees and realty transfer tax in a single check payable to Fayette County Recorder of Deeds, as long as the amount is exact.

Does the Fayette County recorder search for liens?

No. Liens and judgments go through the Prothonotary's office in the courthouse at 724-430-1272. The recorder shows mortgages and whether they were satisfied.

Where do I get a copy of my recorded deed in Fayette County?

Visit the Uniontown office, where copies are $0.50 per page, or find the document through the US Land Records index. A certified copy costs $0.50 per page plus $3.00 for the certification.

Office location and hours

The Recorder of Deeds is on the first floor of the Cambria County Courthouse, 200 South Center Street, Ebensburg, PA 15931. Call (814) 472-1473. Staff work 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. on weekdays, but recording stops at 3:30 p.m. sharp. The office also answers questions by phone.

After recording, staff scan the document and hand it right back. Pay with cash or a check made out to Recorder of Deeds, and call ahead if you want a quote on recording fees or copies. Military discharge papers are recorded and copied free.

UPI approval for deeds

Since August 1, 2016, the county Assessment Office has had to approve a Uniform Parcel Identifier certification before many documents can be recorded. That covers deeds, decrees of distribution, awards of real estate, mortgages, rights of way, easements, leases, condemnations, declarations of taking, consents, assignments of leases and rents, sewage and water permits, highway occupancy permits, statements of adverse possession and boundary line agreements. The Recorder refuses these papers without the approval.

The Assessment Office is at 200 South Center Street, phone (814) 472-1451. A UPI staff member sits in the Recorder's office, but approval isn't available from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m. each day. Closers are urged to email documents ahead for pre-approval, using the UPI address on the county page.

  • Send the deed for UPI review before the closing date, not on the day.
  • Keep the parcel description identical to the prior deed.
  • Don't book a closing slot that hinges on approval between 1:00 and 2:00 p.m.

E-recording and transfer tax

The office takes e-recording for certain document types through Simplifile, Indecomm Global Services, CSC Global and ePN, and the recorder's page gives a phone number for each vendor. Paper originals can still be carried to the counter.

The Recorder also collects Pennsylvania realty transfer tax and passes it along. The state charges 1% of the value of the real estate, and local governments may add their own share, so ask the office for the combined rate in your municipality and school district. Some transfers are exempt, including certain family transfers and property passed by will or intestacy.

The state's Department of Revenue can hold buyer and seller both liable. Decide in the purchase agreement who pays, and confirm that your closing agent has the funds in an accepted form.

Tax-delinquent houses

Since April 1, 2025, a $250.00 fee is added to the costs of every property sold at an upset, judicial, private or repository sale, under Cambria County Ordinance 5 of 2024. Private sales are capped at 50 properties, and each bidder can list up to four per sale. For the 2025 tax year and later, delinquent school taxes in Cambria Township, Ebensburg Borough and Jackson Township, the Central Cambria School District, are collected by Portnoff Law Associates at (866) 211-9466.

A seller who owes back taxes should order a certification from the Tax Claim office, which takes orders online. Ask what is owed for each tax year before you set a closing date.

Assessments and homestead filings

The Cambria County Assessment Office keeps property records and values real estate for taxation. It sits in the courthouse at 200 South Center Street, with phone (814) 472-1451 and hours of 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. on weekdays. Millage and tax collection belong to other bodies. The county is a fourth-class county under the General County Assessment Law.

The same office runs the Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion program under Acts 50 and 1, and the Clean and Green preferential assessment program under Act 319. It posts an appeal form, appeal board rules, millage rates and a homestead application, along with appeal hearing schedules. If you plan to appeal before listing, read the board rules first.

  • Assessment Office: values property and takes appeals.
  • Tax Claim office: collects delinquent taxes and holds tax sales.
  • Recorder of Deeds: records the deed and collects transfer tax.

Cambria County housing context

Cambria is an older industrial county, and home prices run far below those in the state's suburban counties. It covers 694 square miles, with Ebensburg as the seat and Johnstown as the largest city. Population was 133,472 in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 128,968. For 2020 to 2024 the median home value was $121,000, median gross rent was $739 and the owner rate was 76.4%. About 26.2% of residents are 65 or older. Main roads are US 22, US 219 and US 422, plus PA 36, PA 56 and PA 53.

Getting your deed to the counter

Order matters here. First get UPI approval from the Assessment Office, ideally by email ahead of the closing. Then confirm the total with the Recorder's office by phone, adding the $15.00 and $1.00 charges to the base fee. Bring cash or a check payable to Recorder of Deeds, or send the package through an e-recording vendor. Arrive well before 3:30 p.m. Before a sale, also ask the Tax Claim office for a certification so no delinquent tax surprises the closing.

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Cambria County Recorder of Deeds stop recording?

Recording stops at 3:30 p.m. on weekdays, even though the office stays open until 4:00 p.m. The office opens at 9:00 a.m. Monday through Friday. Plan the deed to arrive well before the cutoff.

Does Cambria County charge an extra fee on deeds?

Yes. A $15.00 fee applies to all deeds and mortgages under Act 152 of 2016, in place since March 1, 2017. Since December 1, 2025 an added $1.00 applies to deeds, mortgages, easements and many other documents.

Where can I search Cambria County deeds online?

Records from 1986 to now are on the county's Tyler web portal, linked from the recorder's page. The 1924 to 1985 index is on SearchIQS. Records before 1924 are available only in the office, and printing costs $0.50 per page.

Does a deed in Cambria County need approval before recording?

Yes. Since August 1, 2016 the Assessment Office has to approve the UPI for deeds, mortgages, easements, leases and similar documents. Approval isn't offered from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m., so send the document in advance.

What extra fee does Cambria County add to tax sale costs?

A $250.00 fee is added to the costs of every property sold at an upset, judicial, private or repository sale since April 1, 2025. The charge comes from Cambria County Ordinance 5 of 2024. Call the Tax Claim office at (814) 472-1445 for details.

Office location and hours

Blair County's Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds work out of one office in the courthouse at 423 Allegheny Street, Suite 145, Hollidaysburg, PA 16648. The phone is (814) 693-3095. Doors are open Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., closed on legal holidays, and staff stay through lunch.

Land records here start in 1846, the year the county was carved out of Huntingdon and Bedford counties. Recorded documents are public and anyone can view them during business hours. The one exception is military discharge papers, which are impounded. You can also search remotely through Landex. A free Record Alert service will text or email you when something is recorded under up to five names you sign up.

Recording fees

A deed costs $87.75, and a mortgage costs the same. That price covers up to four names and four pages. Each extra name adds $0.50 and each extra page adds $2.00. Make checks payable to Blair County Recorder of Deeds. The office takes no credit cards.

DocumentRecording fee

Recording a military discharge, and certified copies of it, is free. For any document without a listed price, the Recorder sets the fee.

Paperwork a deed needs

Three rules catch a lot of filers. A deed that claims an exemption from realty transfer tax needs two statements of value. Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a signed certificate of residence with the exact address of the grantee, mortgagee or assignee. And blanket assignments, releases and satisfactions are turned away.

  • Include a self-addressed, stamped envelope, sized right for the return.
  • Name the correct municipality and mark it as a city, township or borough.
  • Awards of real estate and decrees of distribution go in with a statement of value.
  • A lease of 30 years or more is $59.75 and needs a statement of value. Shorter leases are $18.50.

Before you pick a net figure, ask the Recorder at (814) 693-3095, or your closing agent, which transfer tax rate applies in your municipality and school district.

What time to turn in a deed

Get your documents in by 3:15 p.m. Anything submitted after that may not be processed the same day. The recording desk itself stays open until 3:45 p.m., but if you need a same-day record for a closing, the earlier cutoff is the one to plan around.

You can skip the trip with e-recording. The office accepts filings through Simplifile, CSC at eRecording.com and ePN, and the county pitches it as a way to save time, postage and checks. Mail and counter drop-off work too, provided the return envelope is in the package.

The office posts a holiday calendar. For the rest of 2026 it shows closures on Thanksgiving, the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day, so schedule a closing near those dates with that in mind.

Housing market snapshot

Blair County covers 527 square miles around Altoona, with Hollidaysburg as the county seat. Population was estimated at 119,541 in 2025, a 2.7% slide since 2020. The county counts 56,086 housing units and 50,558 households, with 72.4% of homes lived in by their owners. The median value of an owner-occupied home for 2020 to 2024 was $161,100, and median gross rent was $885. Builders pulled just 86 permits in 2025, so a resale rarely competes with new homes. Roughly 24.5% of residents are 65 or older. Buyers touring an older house tend to scrutinize the roof and furnace.

Other documents the office records

Deeds and mortgages are only part of what gets filed here. Agreements, affidavits, bills of sale, powers of attorney, ordinances, waivers and sewage permits are $18.50 each. Articles of agreement, installment sales agreements, declarations of taking and notices of condemnation are $59.75. An order of court is $20.50.

  • Subdivision plans cost $30.00 for page one, then $10.00 per added page.
  • Surveys and plans cost $10.00 for page one, then $5.00 per added page.
  • Highway plans cost $18.00 for page one, then $3.00 per added page.
  • UCC financing statements: $100.00.
  • Notary public bond, oath and commission: $38.50.

A satisfaction by order of court is $64.75, the same as an ordinary satisfaction piece. If you hold a paid-off mortgage that was never released, the satisfaction is the filing that clears it from the index before you sell.

Office rules for visitors

No photography is allowed in the office, and that covers phones, so bring paper and a pen when you look up a record. Staff give general information by phone but won't search records or offer legal advice. For anything deeper, hire a title examiner or an attorney.

Plan your visit around the cutoff times and document rules above. Bring a check, since cards are refused, and a stamped, self-addressed envelope for any mailed or dropped-off filing. A family transfer that claims a tax exemption needs two statements of value, so it takes more prep than an ordinary arm's length sale.

Getting a copy of your deed

Landex has records online. Or walk in during business hours and staff will locate the reference and photocopy it for you. Counter copies run 25 cents a page. If you ask by mail, email or fax, give the full name, the property location and the year of purchase. Those cost $1.00 per page, and you supply a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. Certifying a copy adds $2.00.

A certified copy can stand in for a lost or destroyed deed. A recorded document can't be altered after the fact. To add, drop or change a name, record a new deed. Office staff can't prepare deeds, so an attorney drafts it. When a spouse dies and the couple held title as tenants by the entireties, the name normally can stay on until the house is sold or mortgaged. The next deed then records the date of death.

Recording a deed, step by step

An attorney or your closing agent drafts the deed. Clip on the signed certificate of residence, plus both statements of value if you claim an exemption. Cut a check for the fee and enclose a return envelope with postage so the original finds its way back to the buyer. Pick how it travels: e-recording vendor, post, or the counter before 3:15 p.m. If a payoff is part of the sale, confirm with your closing agent that the release or satisfaction gets filed, because that wipes the old lien from the index.

Where a Lycoming County deed is recorded

Deeds for property anywhere in Lycoming County are recorded by the Register and Recorder in Williamsport, the county seat. Land records go back to 1795, and every deed from 1795 to today can be viewed online through the searchiqs.com/palyc portal.

The deed is the last paper in a sale. Your buyer's title company or attorney usually carries the signed deed to the recorder after closing, and the recording date is when the public record shows the new owner. Corrections work differently than you might expect: a name cannot be added, removed or changed on an existing deed. A new deed has to be drafted and recorded, and the office points owners to a real estate attorney or title company for that.

Lycoming is the largest Pennsylvania county by land area, about 1,229 square miles, and a house in Jersey Shore, Montoursville or Hughesville is recorded at the same Williamsport counter as one on a city street.

The Uniform Parcel Identifier step

Every instrument that affects real estate needs a Uniform Parcel Identifier, called a UPI, before the Recorder will accept it. That covers deeds, easements, rights of way, mortgages, mortgage assignments, releases, satisfactions and leases, and a 2017 ordinance amendment extended the rule to every instrument involving a specific interest in real estate.

The Land Records Office in the Department of Planning and Community Development assigns or verifies the UPI. It is on the third floor of the Third Street Plaza at 33 West Third Street in Williamsport. The price is $10.00 per UPI, collected when the document is recorded, and a single-UPI document has that charge folded into the base recording fee.

  • Bring or mail the original document to Land Records, or email a draft to upi@lyco.org or fax it to 570-320-2135 for review before closing.
  • Turnaround is roughly 5 to 10 minutes at the counter and no more than one business day.
  • Staff stamp the UPI in the upper left corner of the first page so the Recorder can collect the right fees.
  • One document can list several lots and still need just one UPI.
  • For questions, call 570-320-2130. Weekday hours are 8:30 in the morning to 4:30 in the afternoon.

If you are splitting off part of a parcel, the new piece is labeled as part of the original UPI, so start the paperwork before the closing date.

Charges on a deed filing

The Register and Recorder publishes a fee sheet and updates it from time to time. Get the latest sheet before closing day so your check matches. The base recording fee covers a set number of pages and names, the UPI charge is $10.00 for each parcel identifier, and realty transfer tax is paid on top.

Charges that attach to a Lycoming County deed recording
ChargeWho sets itAmount or rule
Base recording feeLycoming County Register and RecorderListed on the office's current fee sheet
UPI certificationLycoming County Land Records$10.00 per UPI
Commonwealth realty transfer taxPennsylvania Department of Revenue1 percent of value
Local transfer taxMunicipality and school districtShared by the district and municipality, rate varies
Name or ownership changeRecorderRequires a new recorded deed
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lycoming County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Realty transfer tax on a sale

The commonwealth levies 1 percent of the property's value, and under state law the grantor and the grantee each answer for it. The Williamsport office collects it with the local share and passes the state portion up to Harrisburg.

The recorder's page lists the school districts used for transfer tax purposes, which is the quickest way to see how local tax is split. There are eleven:

  • Canton, East Lycoming and Jersey Shore
  • Loyalsock, Montgomery and Montoursville
  • Muncy, South Williamsport and Williamsport
  • Southern Tioga and Wellsboro, which reach into neighboring Tioga County

A few transfers escape the tax, among them some gifts inside a family, deeds to public bodies and estates passing at death. If you think one of those fits, tell the closing agent early, since the deed must carry supporting language.

Appealing your assessment

If you think the assessment is too high, you can file a yearly appeal from July 1 to September 1, which applies to the following tax year, or file within 40 days after a change of value notice arrives. Each parcel needs its own form. The filing fee is $15.00 for residential property and $50.00 for everything else, including commercial, industrial and Clean and Green.

The appeal has to argue market value. Tax bills and your ability to pay cannot be appealed, and the law presumes the assessment is correct until you show otherwise. The board will not split a property into land and buildings, so the appeal covers total value.

  • Useful evidence: a certified appraisal from the last three years, sales of similar homes within the past three years, photos of a run-down interior and, for rural lots, perc test results.
  • An annual appeal never changes the current year, so keep paying on time.
  • On a change-of-value appeal, pay with a letter saying the tax is paid in protest.
  • A ruling that still looks wrong can go to the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days.

Ask the Assessment Office which value will drive the next tax bill, since that is the number a buyer inherits.

Getting the filing right the first time

Most delays come from the parcel identifier, not the deed text. Send a draft to Land Records a few days ahead and ask for the UPI to be stamped on page one. Then confirm the school district and municipality for the property so the transfer tax split is right, check the current fee sheet for the recording amount, and make the check payable as the office instructs. If the sale is a gift or an inheritance, say so on the deed so the exemption language is there when the recorder reviews it.

After recording, keep the recorded copy with your closing papers. It is the proof of when ownership changed, and a corrected name later means a fresh deed and a fresh round of fees.

Selling in Lycoming County

Lycoming County sits in north central Pennsylvania on the West Branch Susquehanna River. The 2020 census counted 114,188 residents, and owners lived in 67.2 percent of occupied homes. Williamsport is the seat and the only city. The next largest places are South Williamsport, Montoursville, Jersey Shore and Muncy. Lycoming, Loyalsock and Muncy creeks drain the county, so describe flood or creek exposure accurately to buyers if your house sits near one. Cold winters also put roofs and heating systems to a real test, and buyers will ask about both.

Frequently asked questions

Does the Lycoming County recorder fix a misspelled name on an old deed?

Not on the old deed itself. A recorded deed stays as written, and a new deed must be prepared and recorded to add, remove or change a name. A title company or real estate attorney can draft it.

How much is the UPI charge in Lycoming County?

It is $10.00 for each UPI, paid when the document is recorded. A document with one UPI has that charge included in its base fee, and extra UPIs on the same document cost more.

Can I check Lycoming County deeds from home?

Yes. Deeds from 1795 to the present can be viewed online at searchiqs.com/palyc, and the same records can be searched at the recorder's office in Williamsport during business hours.

What deadline applies to a Lycoming County assessment appeal?

Yearly appeals go in between July 1 and September 1 and apply to the next tax year. After a change of value notice, the window is 40 days counted from the notice date.

Who covers the realty transfer tax on a Lycoming County sale?

The grantor and grantee each answer for the 1 percent state tax, with local tax added on top. The sales contract normally sets how the two split it, and the recorder collects it at filing.

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Northumberland County?

Where to record a deed in Northumberland County

Deeds are recorded by the Register and Recorder at 201 Market Street, first floor, in Sunbury. The phone is 570-988-4143. On Mondays the office is open from 9:00 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., and Tuesday through Friday it runs 9:00 a.m. to 4:15 p.m. It closes every day from noon to 1:00 p.m., so a package that arrives at 12:15 p.m. waits until 1:00.

One office holds two jobs. It records land documents, and it also acts as register of wills for estates and issues marriage licenses. Heirs who sell an inherited house use both functions: first to open the estate, later to record the deed out of it. Probate visits are by appointment, booked at 570-988-4985.

Recording charges

Filing a deed costs $86.25 on the current schedule, whether it is taxable, nontaxable or a quit claim. That price assumes four pages, four names and a single tract.

Northumberland County recording charges
DocumentCharge
Deed of any kind$86.25
Mortgage$86.25
Satisfaction piece$64.75
Lease of 30 years or more$71.25
Right of way agreement$59.75
Affidavit affecting real estate$18.50
Statement of Value$2.00
UCC financing statement$100.00

Extras are small. Each page after the fourth adds $2.00, and each added name or added tract adds fifty cents (no tract charge on a mortgage). A marginal notation is $2.00.

A wrong fee gets the document rejected, and a payment that is too high counts as wrong. Add it up before writing the check.

How transfer tax is paid on a sale

A taxable deed owes the state's 1 percent, a local 1 percent and the recording fee. Separate checks are not required, so one check can cover all three amounts.

The grantor and grantee share liability for the state portion. The state also exempts some deeds, such as particular family transfers, deeds to a government body and inherited property.

An exempt deed still travels with a Statement of Value, priced at $2.00 here, and the title agent or attorney should state the reason for the exemption on the form.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Northumberland County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What paperwork does the recorder require?

The county's requirements are short, so each item matters.

  • The document submitted must be an original.
  • If the recorded deed must come back by mail, enclose a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself.
  • No blanket assignments or satisfaction pieces.
  • The exact recording fee is required or the document is refused.

Electronic filing covers deeds, mortgages, assignments, satisfactions, mortgage releases, UCC filings and powers of attorney. Filers sign up with one of two vendors, CSC E-Recording Solutions or Simplifile.

Selling an inherited house

An heir cannot sign a deed until someone has authority to act for the estate. In this county that authority comes from letters issued by the Register and Recorder, and the fee rises with the size of the estate.

  • Letters in an estate under $1,000 cost $142.75.
  • An estate between $50,001 and $100,000 costs $267.75.
  • Each additional $100,000, or fraction of it, adds $100.00.
  • Letters used for litigation only cost $102.75.

Those prices include the filing of the inventory and the inheritance tax return. The same office charges $50.00 for a certified copy of an instrument and $10.00 for a short certificate, which a title company may ask for. Call the office before the visit, since probate meetings run by appointment.

Heirs sometimes need smaller filings too, and the estate's representative usually learns about them only after the first visit. A disclaimer costs $15.00, a renunciation is $10.00 per name, a receipt and release in the register of wills is $10.00 per name, and a creditor's claim is $75.00. Whoever is handling the estate should add these to the budget before the house is listed.

Local housing market

Sunbury is the county seat and the biggest city, and Shamokin is the other city. The 2025 population estimate is 89,920. Housing costs are low: the latest five-year survey shows a $162,400 median home value, $60,583 in median household income and 75.5 percent owner occupancy. Every town in the county files with the Sunbury office.

Recording fees do not shrink with the price. An $86.25 deed fee is the same on a $90,000 house as on a $900,000 one, so on a low-priced sale it takes a bigger bite and belongs in the closing estimate as its own line.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Northumberland County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Clearing an old mortgage at sale

The lender files a satisfaction piece or a release of mortgage with the recorder, and each costs $64.75 to record. A partial release costs the same. An assignment of a mortgage from one lender to another is $61.75.

The county refuses blanket satisfaction pieces, so each one has to name the specific mortgage it clears. If a paid-off mortgage still shows in the public record, ask the title company to track it down. Ask the lender how long it takes to file, so the record is clear for the buyer.

Step by step: getting the deed recorded

The order below keeps a sale from stalling at the counter. Sellers rarely handle this alone, since the closing agent usually files, but knowing the steps helps you ask the right questions.

  1. The title agent or attorney prepares the original deed and the Statement of Value. A taxable deed carries the state 1 percent and the local 1 percent, and an exempt deed carries the stated reason for the exemption.
  2. Someone totals the charges: $86.25 for the deed, $2.00 for the Statement of Value, plus any extra pages, names or tracts.
  3. The package goes in either by mail, with a stamped return envelope addressed to the filer, or through CSC E-Recording Solutions or Simplifile.
  4. The county records the deed and returns it.

If a mortgage is being paid off at the same closing, the lender's satisfaction piece is a separate filing at $64.75. Sellers who skip a lender payoff and sell for cash still need the deed filed, but they have fewer documents to track.

Closing checklist

Work through this list before the deed leaves the title office.

  • Work out the exact fee from the schedule, including extra pages and names.
  • Bring a stamped, self-addressed return envelope.
  • Check the hours, including the noon closing.
  • Decide ahead whether the closing agent will file electronically through CSC or Simplifile.
  • For an inherited home, schedule the probate appointment well before the closing.

A cash sale does not remove any of these steps, since the deed is still recorded here. It does cut out lender requirements, so the paperwork is usually the deed, the Statement of Value and the fee.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What will a deed cost to file in Sunbury?

$86.25 for a deed of four pages, four names and one tract. Each extra page adds $2 and each extra name adds 50 cents.

Do I write one check or several for a taxable deed?

One check can cover the state tax, the local tax and the recording fee. Northumberland does not require separate checks.

Can a deed be recorded electronically?

Yes. CSC E-Recording Solutions and Simplifile handle electronic deeds, mortgages, assignments, satisfactions, releases, UCC filings and powers of attorney for the county.

When can I visit the Sunbury recorder?

The office opens at 9:00 a.m. It stays open until 4:45 p.m. on Mondays and 4:15 p.m. Tuesday through Friday, and it closes from noon to 1:00 p.m. every day.

What happens if I send the wrong fee?

The document comes back unrecorded, and a payment that is too high counts as wrong. Calculate the fee from the current schedule before mailing.

content:
Adams County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Pennsylvania
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Adams County, PA Recorder of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Adams County, PA Recorder of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Adams County, PA Recorder of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Adams County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Adams County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Adams County?
We buy Adams County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
