Where deeds are recorded in Adams County

Head to the Adams County Courthouse, 117 Baltimore Street, Room 102, Gettysburg, where the Recorder of Deeds keeps the land records. Call 717-337-9826 between 8:00 a.m. and 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday. County holidays are closed days.

Accepting new filings ends at 4:00 p.m., thirty minutes ahead of closing time, so a package arriving at 4:20 sits until the next business day. The same counter handles realty transfer tax on behalf of the Department of Revenue, then splits the money among the state, the municipality and the school district.

Think of this office as the finish line of your sale. After you sign at closing, the deed is filed here, and the filing date is when the buyer shows up as owner in the public record.

Recording fees

Under the fee bill in force since December 1, 2025, one deed or mortgage is $71.25 to record, good for four pages and four names. Extras are charged on top.

Filing typeRecording fee
Deed or mortgage$71.25
Each page over 4 (deed or mortgage)$4.00
Each name over 4 (deed or mortgage)$1.00
Satisfaction piece or mortgage release$61.75
Power of attorney$18.50

Assignments of mortgage also cost $61.75, easements and rights of way $59.75, and copies $0.25 a page. A document type missing from the list gets a fee set by the Recorder. Fees are due when you record.

You may pay with cash, a check or a card; cards carry a vendor charge. Checks cannot be broken into change. If you overpay by $10 or less, the extra stays as an overpayment noted on your receipt; a larger overage means writing a new check.

Realty transfer tax at recording

Bring a checkbook. Transfer tax cannot be paid in cash and is collected as the deed is recorded. The county’s fee bill describes a 1% state tax and an equal local tax, and asks for three checks, made out to the state, to the township or borough, and to the recorder for the fee.

The buyer and seller are jointly liable. A handful of transfers are excused, among them some family transfers and property passed down by will or intestacy.

  • File a Statement of Value whenever the tax is not paid in full, and that includes a family exemption claim.
  • For land in two or more municipalities, the deed should show how the value divides so each local share is routed properly.
  • Transfers from grandparent to grandchild and between siblings appear among the recognized exemptions.
  • No deed or mortgage is recorded without a signed Certificate of Residence.

The Statement of Value is a Revenue form, and this office charges nothing to file it. For help with it, ask Revenue.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Adams County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Document requirements

Filings have to involve real estate, show original signatures and be notarized correctly. The document date may not fall after the notary’s acknowledgment date.

Compared with neighboring counties, Adams is relaxed in a few ways. It does not use the Uniform Parcel Identifier system, which means no UPI fee, and a parcel number or street address is not required. There are no margin rules, and letter or legal paper both work.

  • Put in a stamped, self-addressed envelope. The finished document is mailed back about two weeks after it is recorded.
  • An assignment of mortgage must cite where the original mortgage is recorded, by book and page.
  • Subdivision plans are 18 by 24 inches, signed off by the municipality and the county planning commission, and recorded within 90 days of approval.
  • Remote online notarization works only during a declared emergency.

Ways to submit a document

Options are a visit in person, the secure drop box by the courthouse entrance, or delivery by USPS, FedEx or UPS. An appointment is preferred though not mandatory; arrange one by phone or at registerrecorder@adamscountypa.gov.

Search terminals for the public sit in the courthouse lobby, along with a copier that works with a button from the Register and Recorder or the Prothonotary. The recording office has no terminal of its own, and taking photos of screens, books or microfilm is prohibited.

The office offers a free fraud alert called PropertyCheck, which emails or texts an owner when anything is recorded against the property. Owners who keep other land here can sign up. Also ask your title company whether the closing package can go in electronically instead of by courier.

The Adams County market in brief

Roughly 107,594 people lived here as of July 2025, a 3.6% rise since 2020. Gettysburg is the center of the county, with the national military park on three sides. Close to 78.9% of homes are occupied by their owners, and a typical owner-occupied home is valued at $268,500, which is why most local sales are owner to owner. Median household income is $84,092.

After the deed is on record, a new owner can contact the county’s Tax Services office.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Adams County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Closing-day checklist

Run through this list so the deed is accepted the first time.

  • A signed, notarized deed showing the notary’s venue and expiration date and a stamp you can read.
  • Three checks drawn on the right accounts, for state tax, local tax and recording fee, with amounts that match the consideration stated in the deed.
  • A completed Certificate of Residence, plus a Statement of Value if any tax is excused.
  • A stamped return envelope addressed to the buyer or the title agent.
  • Delivery before 4:00 p.m. on a weekday that is not a county holiday.

Settle ahead of time who walks the package into the courthouse and who receives the recorded original afterward.

How a cash sale fits in

Paying cash leaves the recording steps alone: the deed is still signed, notarized, taxed and filed in this office. What disappears is the buyer’s lender, along with loan underwriting and the wait that comes with it. If you still owe on a mortgage, a satisfaction piece gets recorded after payoff, and its fee appears in the table above. Ask the title agent to confirm that the release is filed so the public record shows clear title.

A simple order of events for sellers

Most Adams County sales run in a predictable order. The title agent prepares the deed and the tax forms, you sign before a notary, and the package goes to Room 102 with three checks. After recording, the deed is mailed back to the address on your envelope. If you are selling an inherited house, ask early which exemption, if any, applies, since a Statement of Value must accompany any claim. Sellers who live out of the area can sign with a notary near them and let the title agent handle delivery.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Questions to put to your title agent

A few plain questions save a trip to Gettysburg. Who is buying the three checks and from which accounts? Does the stated price on the deed match the amount the tax is figured on? Is anyone claiming an exemption, and if so, is the Statement of Value ready? Will the agent record electronically or drive the paperwork in before the afternoon cutoff? And where should the returned original go, to you, to the buyer or to the lender? Sellers who are out of town can ask the agent to confirm each answer by email so there is a written trail. Keep the receipt from the recorder with your closing papers, since it shows the exact fees paid and the date the filing was accepted.

Waiting for the recorded deed

Once the package is accepted, nothing more is needed from you except patience. Mail return runs slow, so if the buyer or the title agent needs proof sooner, ask the agent for the stamped receipt that shows the recording date. If a month goes by without the deed arriving, phone the recorder and give the date you filed and the names on the deed.

Frequently asked questions

What is the base recording fee for a deed in Adams County?

A deed or mortgage costs $71.25 under the schedule effective December 1, 2025, plus $4.00 for each page after the fourth and $1.00 for each name after the fourth. Transfer tax is paid separately, by check.

When does Adams County stop accepting documents each day?

The cutoff is 4:00 p.m. on business days, although the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. For a special circumstance, call or email before you come.

Is cash accepted for transfer tax at the Adams County courthouse?

No. Realty transfer tax must be paid by check, with separate checks for the state tax, the local tax and the recording fee. The recording fee itself can be paid in cash or by card, with a vendor fee on cards.

Must a deed carry a parcel number to be recorded here?

No. The county does not use the UPI system, and a parcel number or property address is not required on a document. A Certificate of Residence is required, though.

Where should a signed deed be delivered or mailed?

Take it to the Recorder of Deeds at the Adams County Courthouse, 117 Baltimore Street, Room 102, Gettysburg, PA 17325, or use the drop box at the entrance. Enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope; return mail takes about two weeks.

What the recorder's office does

The Recorder of Deeds is an elected county office that keeps Carbon County's land records, from deeds and mortgages to easements and rights of way. When a house sells in Jim Thorpe, Lehighton, Palmerton or any other Carbon County town, the deed has to be recorded here before the public record shows the new owner.

Every document goes through three steps: indexing into the public retrieval system, scanning, and a check of the index entries. One copy sits on the county's public system, Landex, and two archive copies are kept on secure servers at separate locations. The office also collects realty transfer tax and the court-related fees that go to the state, plus the Affordable Housing Program fee that supports income-based housing in the county.

Recording fees

A deed or mortgage costs $102.75 under the fee sheet effective November 17, 2025. That covers four pages, four names and one parcel number.

Carbon County recording fees, effective November 17, 2025
DocumentRecording fee
Deed$102.75
Mortgage$102.75
Assignment, release or satisfaction of mortgage$74.75
Agreement of sale$74.75
Easement or right of way$74.75
Mortgage modification or subordination$33.50
Power of attorney$18.50

Longer documents cost more. Deeds and mortgages add $4.00 for each page past four, other documents add $2.00 per page past four, every name beyond four adds $0.50, and each extra parcel number adds $15.00. Pay the exact amount in cash, personal check, business check or money order. A wrong amount comes back with a $5.00 rejection fee, though the county keeps an overpayment of $10.00 or less.

Realty transfer tax

The office collects 2% of the total consideration or the fair market value, and the money is divided among the state, local school districts and municipalities. A Pennsylvania Statement of Value, form REV-183, is required whenever you aren't paying tax on full market value.

  • All trusts require a Statement of Value.
  • Easements need one unless the grantee is a public utility.
  • A transfer out of an estate needs one unless full tax is being paid.
  • Submit the form in duplicate. Its pages don't count toward the page total.
  • A family transfer, such as a parent to children, must be typed on the deed if no tax is being paid.

Use the Common Level Ratio factor for the year your document is dated. For factors older than five years, call the office at 570-325-2651.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Carbon County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Where to file and the daily cutoff

Carbon County takes recordings by mail, in person and through the e-recording partners CSC and Simplifile. The office number is 570-325-2651. Recording closes at 3:30 p.m., so a closing that wraps up late in the day may not record until the next business day.

Documents must relate to real estate, be in English or carry a translation, and bear original, properly notarized signatures. A mailed filing needs a self-addressed stamped envelope, and a holder of an office mailbox is asked to pick up recorded papers at least weekly. Remote online notarization is accepted when the certificate says the notarial act used communication technology.

Why a deed gets rejected

The county's recording requirements run to 21 items, and the same few mistakes come up again and again.

  • The document date must match or precede the acknowledgment date.
  • Grantor names, signatures and acknowledgments must match exactly, and the names should match the prior deed's grantee.
  • Reference documents must show the book and page of the earlier recorded paper.
  • State the municipality, whether township or borough, above the legal description. For land in several localities, show the percentage split for local transfer tax on the Statement of Value.
  • Deeds, mortgages, easements, releases and assignments need a signed mailing address certification, because that address tells the Assessment Office where to send property tax bills.
  • Notary blocks need the right venue, a legible stamp and a current commission expiration date.

Searching and monitoring records online

Records are published through Landex. Landex Webstore gives the public remote access to documents from 1988 forward, and a separate Landex Remote service serves title searchers. Anyone can sign up for a Landex Record Alert on a name or a tax parcel number and get a notice whenever a new document is recorded against it.

An alert is a cheap way for a seller to confirm that a satisfaction of mortgage was recorded after payoff, or for an heir to watch for filings against an inherited house. Staff can also help trace a property back through earlier owners and purchase prices, and help replace a lost document.

  • A re-recorded document needs a new acknowledgment and new signatures.
  • When several documents are filed together, label them, such as POA, deed and mortgage, so they record in the right order.
  • Sales agreements must list the full address of both buyer and seller.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Carbon County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Releases and satisfactions before you sell

If you have a mortgage, the lender's satisfaction has to be recorded so the title is clear for the next owner. A satisfaction applies when the whole loan is paid off. A release, sometimes called a partial release, applies when part of the property or one name comes off the mortgage while the loan stays active on the rest.

Each satisfaction or release can reference only one mortgage, and blanket documents are refused. Trust transfers have their own rule. Since October 1, 2024, deeds into a trust can't be e-recorded, so they must be brought in or mailed. For tax parcel numbers on agreements, easements, leases and rights of way, call the county GIS department at 570-325-8519 first.

Before you send your paperwork

Run through a short list. Confirm the grantor and grantee names match the prior deed, and that the acknowledgment date is the same or later than the document date. Get your parcel number from the Assessment Office at 570-325-5254. Count pages and parcels so you can send the exact fee, since a wrong amount means a rejection fee and a delay. If the closing is late in the day, file electronically through CSC or Simplifile so it is in before 3:30 p.m., unless the deed goes into a trust, which must come by hand or mail.

Carbon County housing context

Carbon County was split off from Northampton County in 1843. Jim Thorpe is the seat and Palmerton is the largest borough. I-80 and the Northeast Extension of the Pennsylvania Turnpike (I-476) cross the county. It has 65,868 residents in 2025 on about 381 square miles, with 34,816 housing units. For 2020 to 2024 the median home value was $211,400, owner-occupancy was 76.4% and median gross rent was $994. About 24.3% of residents are 65 or older.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

What time does the Carbon County Recorder of Deeds stop recording?

The cutoff for recording is 3:30 p.m. Documents arriving after that time wait for the next business day, so plan closings with that in mind.

How much is the realty transfer tax in Carbon County?

The office collects 2% of the total consideration or the fair market value of the property. That money is distributed to the state, the local school district and the municipality.

Can a deed into a trust be e-recorded in Carbon County?

No. Since October 1, 2024, the office accepts deeds into a trust only in person or by mail. Other documents can still be e-recorded through CSC or Simplifile.

Do I need a UPI to record a Carbon County deed?

Yes. All real estate documents need a Uniform Parcel Identifier before recording. Call the Assessment Office at 570-325-5254 to get one, and add $15.00 for each parcel beyond the first.

What happens if I pay the wrong recording fee in Carbon County?

The document is returned and a $5.00 rejection fee is charged per document. The one exception is an overpayment of $10.00 or less, which the county keeps.

Cash Home Buyers in Pennsylvania
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Pike County, PA Recorder of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Pike County, PA Recorder of Deeds sale

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

What the Pike County Recorder of Deeds does

The office records and indexes real estate documents for Pike County, such as deeds, mortgages and mortgage satisfactions. The same counter also collects realty transfer tax on behalf of the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue, so the tax and the recording fee are paid together.

Find it at 506 Broad Street in Milford. Staff are there weekdays from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, and the phone is 570-296-3508. Checks go to "Pike County Recorder of Deeds." A returned document carries a $10 return fee.

Recording comes last in a sale and decides whether the buyer's name shows up in the public index. A deed that sits in a drawer, or one that is rejected, leaves the seller on record as the owner, with consequences for property tax bills, liability and any lien searches that follow.

How to record a deed

You can deliver the deed to the Milford office or send it through an electronic recording vendor. Two vendors serve title companies and law offices every day.

  • Simplifile, phone 800-460-5657
  • CSC, phone 866-652-0111
  • Walk it in or mail it to 506 Broad Street, Milford, PA 18337, with a check for the fee and, if the deed carries transfer tax, a payment for that

The fee schedule changes from time to time, so ask the office for the current deed fee before you write a check. A check in the wrong amount is one of the reasons a package comes back.

When a title company or attorney closes your sale, they normally prepare the deed, calculate the tax and file it. After closing, request the recording confirmation or book and page reference and keep it with your sale papers.

Why deeds get returned

The recorder keeps a short checklist of defects. Most are clerical, and every one can be fixed before the deed leaves your hands.

  • The acknowledgment date falls before the date on the caption.
  • The acknowledgment leaves out the county, state, date, the names and titles of the people appearing, or the notary's signature, seal and expiration date. The office treats that acknowledgment as defective.
  • The deed leaves out the township, county or state where the property sits.
  • The amount written in words differs from the amount in numbers.
  • A document that refers back to an earlier mortgage omits that mortgage's book and page.
  • A set of papers for one transaction is not numbered in the order they should be recorded.
  • Property crossing two municipalities does not show the split of local transfer tax in dollars.
  • The deed lacks the grantee's address, or the grantee address is unsigned.
  • A foreign language document arrives without a written English translation.

If you are selling by yourself without a closing attorney, read this list against your deed line by line. The re-recording costs from a wrong document order fall on whoever submitted it.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Pike County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Transfer tax on a Pike County sale

The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent of the value being transferred. Seller and buyer are jointly responsible, and the recorder takes it in along with any local tax.

Local transfer tax is the part that varies. Municipalities and school districts may add their own share, and Pike County deeds can cross municipal lines, which is why the recorder asks for the local split in dollars. Get the combined rate for your township or borough from the recorder before you sign a settlement sheet.

Some transfers pay nothing. The exemption list covers certain family transfers, transfers to governmental units and property that passes through an estate. If an heir later deeds the inherited house to a buyer, that second deed is an ordinary taxed sale.

Pike County recording quick reference
TopicRule
Office hoursWeekdays, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm
Return fee$10 on any returned document
Checks payable toPike County Recorder of Deeds
State transfer tax1 percent of value
LiabilityBuyer and seller jointly

Pike County housing at a glance

Pike County sits along the Delaware River at Pennsylvania's northeastern edge, with Milford as its seat and Matamoras as the largest borough. Many sales are in lake communities such as Saw Creek, Hemlock Farms, Pocono Woodland Lakes and Pine Ridge. The mid 2025 population is 62,808, up 7.3 percent from 2020, and the county has 40,861 homes.

  • Owner-occupied share of occupied homes: 87.0 percent
  • Typical owned home: $272,600 in value
  • Typical household income: $81,323
  • Typical gross rent: $1,378 a month

With owners living in 87 percent of occupied homes, a typical Pike County sale is an owner selling to another buyer rather than a landlord exiting a rental.

Fraud alerts on your deed

The recorder offers a fraud alert service through the county's online land records. Sign in at the Uslandrecords site, pick Pennsylvania and Pike County, register, and open the Alerts menu to get notice whenever a document is recorded under a name you pick. Setting up alerts does not need a credit card. Viewing or downloading images does.

An alert helps before and after a sale. Before closing, an alert under your own name shows whether anything unexpected gets recorded against your property. After closing, it confirms that your sale deed reached the index. Copies of recorded deeds are available by contacting the office or through the Property Record Search.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Pike County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What should an heir or landlord do before selling?

Start with the title. When an owner has died, someone must be shown to have authority to sign for the estate. That is a matter for the Register of Wills and an attorney. The Recorder of Deeds only records what is presented.

Next, check for open mortgages. A mortgage that was paid off years ago may still look open in the index until its satisfaction is recorded, and the recorder's office files satisfactions as part of its normal work. A title company will want that cleared before closing.

Finally, think about timing. Tax bills, rent and repairs keep running while a deed waits for signatures. Someone who wants a quick closing can ask a buyer to take the house as it is. Even then, the deed is recorded the same way.

Closing-day steps in order

  1. Before closing, confirm with the office or your title company the current deed fee and the local transfer tax rate for your township or borough.
  2. Check the deed against the defect list above, especially the acknowledgment, the grantee address and the match between words and numbers.
  3. Sign the deed before a notary, and check that the notary's seal and expiration date are filled in.
  4. The deed is filed either at 506 Broad Street or through Simplifile or CSC, with one payment for the fee and another for transfer tax.
  5. After recording, get the confirmation or the book and page reference and file it with your papers.

A sale for cash with no lender follows these same steps, though there is usually no mortgage satisfaction to track at the end.

Frequently asked questions

Which office takes a deed for filing in Pike County?

The Recorder of Deeds at 506 Broad Street in Milford, or an electronic vendor. Simplifile and CSC handle online filing, and the counter keeps weekday hours.

What is the return fee on a rejected deed?

$10. The Pike County recorder charges that service fee on every returned document, so checking the acknowledgment and the amounts before you submit saves money and time.

Who is on the hook for transfer tax at a Pike County closing?

Both parties are liable together under state rules, though the sale contract usually assigns the cost. The state's share is 1 percent, and local taxes can add to it. The recorder can tell you the local amount.

Does inheriting a Pike County house trigger transfer tax?

No, title that passes through an estate is exempt. Selling afterward is a separate transfer, taxed like any other sale unless a different exemption fits.

How do I obtain a copy of a recorded Pike County deed?

Call the Recorder of Deeds at 570-296-3508 or use the Property Record Search on the county's land records site. Viewing or downloading images online requires registering a credit card.

Where Mercer County deeds are recorded

The same counter takes deeds, mortgages, leases, powers of attorney, easements, subdivision plans and notary bonds. For a house sale the order is simple: the deed is signed at closing, a Uniform Parcel Identifier is certified, and the closing agent files the deed with the transfer tax and the fee. Recordings can be checked online through the Land Records Search on the county website, with the index and images going back to 1972.

Sellers in Sharon, Grove City, Greenville, Hermitage or Farrell all record through this one office. School district names matter on a deed because local transfer tax can be shared with the district. The county is served by Commodore Perry, Farrell Area, Greenville Area, Grove City Area, Hermitage, Jamestown Area, Lakeview, Mercer Area, Reynolds, Sharon City, Sharpsville Area, West Middlesex Area and Wilmington Area, so the property description should place the parcel in the right municipality and district.

The 2026 UPI ordinance

Mercer County certifies a Uniform Parcel Identifier for every document that affects title before it can be recorded. The commissioners passed Ordinance No. 2026-001 on November 20, 2025, and it took effect on January 5, 2026.

The UPI is the county tax parcel number already assigned to the property. The Tax Assessment Office certifies it. A document mailed or e-recorded to the Recorder is forwarded there first, so the identifier is settled before the deed reaches the Recorder's desk.

  • The charge is $20.00 for each UPI certification, paid separately to Mercer County Tax Assessment, not to the Recorder.
  • Including the parent parcel number costs nothing extra.
  • When only part of a property is being conveyed, two UPI numbers are needed: one for the new piece and one for the parent parcel.
  • Deeds, quitclaim deeds, mortgages, releases, easements, leases, court decrees and powers of attorney to sell are all covered.
  • Questions and pre-approval requests go to upi@mercercountypa.gov.

To keep your closing on schedule, send the draft deed to the Assessment Office well before the signing date.

Recording fees

A deed costs $71.25 under the fee bill revised June 15, 2026. That base fee includes four pages, four names and one parcel. The county adds $2.00 for each extra page and $0.50 for each extra parcel or name.

Mercer County Recorder of Deeds fee bill, revised June 15, 2026
Document or itemFee
Deed, including corrective deed and decree of distribution$71.25
Mortgage, including amendments and subordinations$71.25
Mortgage assignment, release, satisfaction$59.75
Easement or right of way agreement$71.25
Power of attorney$18.50
Realty transfer tax Statement of Value$2.00 extra
Copies made by staff$0.50 per page
Return of a rejected document$5.00 first time, $10 second, $20 after

The Statement of Value is not part of the four-page base fee. Bring the original plus one copy.

Payment is by cash or check only, and each check needs the account holder's current address and phone number. Enclose a stamped return envelope so the recorded deed goes back to the right buyer.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Mercer County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Realty transfer tax by town

The baseline is 1 percent to the Commonwealth plus 1 percent local. Five places charge a different local rate, and the recorder collects the whole amount when the deed is filed.

  • Hermitage: 2.5 percent local
  • Sharon: 2.5 percent local
  • Farrell: 2 percent local
  • Greenville: 2 percent local
  • Sheakleyville: 1 percent local, effective May 1, 2019

A deed that covers land in more than one municipality has to state how the transfer tax is divided or what percentage goes to each. The fee bill prints a common level ratio factor of 9.52 for July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027. Under state revenue rules, grantor and grantee both stand behind the tax. Some family transfers, deeds to government bodies and inherited property are exempt from the state tax.

Document standards

The office rejects paper that does not meet its standards, and a rejected document costs the return fee shown in the table. Check your deed against this list before closing.

  • Original documents only, with an acknowledgment date that does not come before the date of the document.
  • A 2-inch blank margin at the top of every page for the Recorder's stamp.
  • The municipality, county and state of the property written on deeds and mortgages.
  • A signed certificate of residence on deeds, mortgages, articles of agreement and assignments.
  • No highlighting, and text legible enough to index and copy.
  • When several documents belong to one transaction, a note on each showing the order of recording.

The county also requires either the transfer tax or a fully completed Statement of Value on the current Pennsylvania form.

Steps to get a Mercer County deed recorded

In a normal sale the steps run in a fixed order. First the draft deed goes to the Tax Assessment Office so the UPI can be certified and its $20.00 fee paid. Next the deed is signed and acknowledged at closing, and the acknowledgment date must not come before the date of the document. The closing agent then files it at Suite 109 or by e-recording, with the transfer tax and the recording fee, a Statement of Value if one is needed, and a stamped return envelope. Last, the recorded deed is mailed back and the title appears in the online index.

If anything on the document fails the standards above, it comes back with a rejection fee and your closing date can slip, so most agents review it a few days ahead.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Mercer County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

How the reassessment affects a sale

The last countywide reassessment finished in 1971. Its replacement was pushed back a year, so new assessed values now take effect for the 2028 tax year instead of 2027. In 2027 each owner will receive a Final Value Mailer showing land, improvements and the total.

A reassessment is designed not to raise total tax revenue. The county, municipalities and school districts are to bill the same total after the change, so millage drops where values rise. As a seller, you can tell a buyer that the value is likely to be reset soon and that the bill may move in either direction.

Once the mailer arrives, you can appeal to the Board of Assessment Appeals, and formal appeals must be finished by October 31 of the appeal year. For the current tax picture on a parcel, call the Assessment Office at 724-662-7551 or use the county's GIS parcel viewer, which shows the county, municipal and school bills separately.

Mercer County at a glance

Mercer County is in northwest Pennsylvania along the Ohio line, and Hermitage is its largest city. Interstates 79, 80 and 376 and US routes 19 and 62 cross the county. Parcel, school district and municipality decide your transfer tax, so confirm all three before you quote a net figure to a buyer.

Frequently asked questions

How much is the Mercer County UPI certification fee?

It is $20.00 for each UPI certification, paid to Mercer County Tax Assessment rather than to the Recorder. Naming the parent parcel on a document carries no extra fee.

What is the base price of a Mercer County deed filing?

A deed starts at $71.25, which pays for four pages, four names and one parcel. Each added page runs $2.00, each added name or parcel $0.50, and the Statement of Value tacks on $2.00.

Can Mercer County recording fees go on a credit card?

No. The office takes cash or checks only. A check should show the account holder's current address and phone number.

Why is Hermitage transfer tax higher than the rest of Mercer County?

Hermitage and Sharon carry 2.5 percent local tax, while Farrell and Greenville charge 2 percent. Other places use the usual 1 percent local share on top of the 1 percent state tax.

When do new Mercer County property values take effect?

The reassessment was moved to the 2028 tax year. Owners will get a Final Value Mailer in 2027 explaining the new values and how to appeal.

Where deeds are recorded

Take Clearfield County deeds to the Register and Recorder's Office on the courthouse's first level; the phone is 814-765-2641, extension 5012. Visitors can use six public workstations to look up what has been filed.

Its Recorder of Deeds division handles real estate paperwork along with notary bonds and commissions, UCC filings and military discharges, and it issues copies and certified copies.

For you as the seller, this is where the sale becomes official: recording a signed deed puts the new owner's title on the public record.

UPI stamp before recording

Before any deed is recorded, the county's Uniform Parcel Identifier office has to stamp it. The fee is $10 per parcel. Questions go to 814-765-2641, extension 2042. Deeds can be pre-approved for the UPI before the day of recording.

Sellers often assume recording is a single stop. It is two. Title agents typically send the deed over a day or two ahead, collect the stamp, and only then file with the recorder along with payment. Closing without a title company? Ask the county how pre-approval works before you pick a date.

The recorder's own deed checklist says the same thing: no UPI stamp from the Assessment Office, no recording.

Recording fees

Recording a deed or a mortgage runs $79.75. Names past four cost 50 cents each, and each page over four adds $2. For anything not listed, the Recorder of Deeds sets the fee.

When a Statement of Value is needed

A Statement of Value comes into play when the deed omits the full price, when the home is given away, when you claim a tax exemption, or when a tax claim sale or sheriff's sale was involved. Inheritance by will does too. Sign and date it before filing.

The one exception is a transfer exempt only because the parties are close family: grandparent, parent, child, brother or sister.

The state's realty transfer tax is 1 percent, paid at the recorder's window and often joined by a local tax. Buyer and seller share liability. Certain family transfers, inheritances by will or intestacy, and farms are exempt.

  • The deed carries the buyer's signed certificate of address.
  • It names the municipality and county where the property sits.
  • Land that crosses municipal or school district lines needs the percentage in each, so the local tax is split properly.
  • The acknowledgment date cannot be earlier than the date on the document.

Searching records before you list

Two search products are open to the public. Landex Remote is the full tool, with the same search criteria as the software in the courthouse, and it suits someone who searches often. Landex Webstore is the basic version for occasional use. It can search several counties at once and narrow results by county, instrument type and municipality. Viewing images requires a credit card payment. For help with the online products, call 717-274-5890.

Look up your own last recorded deed, plus any open mortgage, easement or right of way. Whatever turns up will also appear in the buyer's title search, so surprises are cheaper to handle now. A paid-off mortgage that was never released of record needs a satisfaction piece from the lender.

Rules that get documents rejected

Documents come back unrecorded when the notary block is defective: no county or state, no date, no name of the signer or corporate officer, or no notary signature, seal or expiration date. The office will not take blanket assignments, releases or satisfactions.

  • A corrective or re-recorded document explains why and gets a fresh acknowledgment.
  • When one transaction has several documents, number them in recording order.
  • Foreign language documents need a written English translation.
  • Mailed packages need a stamped, addressed return envelope large enough to hold the document.

For electronic recording, the vendors are Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and CSC at 866-652-0111. A title company already set up with either one can skip the courier. Owners can also join the county's free Landex Record Alert, which sends an email or text if anyone tries to record a deed under your name or parcel number. Housing in Clearfield County

About 78,100 people lived here as of July 2025, a drop of 3.1 percent from the 2020 base. The county has 38,429 housing units, and 78.5 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. A typical owned home is worth $137,000, rent runs $791 a month, and household income is $62,152. DuBois is the biggest city; the county seat is Clearfield borough.

Packet checklist for Clearfield County

Gather these before anyone heads to the courthouse, and you will rarely get a package bounced.

  • The original deed, signed in ink and notarized with the notary's seal and expiration date showing.
  • Proof the UPI office has stamped it, at $10 for each parcel.
  • Buyer's address certificate and a clear municipality and county description.
  • A Statement of Value if the sale is a gift, an estate transfer or an exempt one.
  • One check for the recording fee and another for the realty transfer tax, payable to the Recorder of Deeds.

If anything is wrong, the office returns the package, and a corrective deed means paying to record again.

Steps for a seller at the recorder

Here is the usual order. You sign the deed in front of a notary at closing. The title agent or attorney arranges the UPI stamp, attaches the buyer's certificate of address, and writes checks for the recording fee and transfer tax. After that, the package reaches the recorder by courier, by mail with a return envelope, or electronically through a vendor.

Handling the sale on your own? Deliver the original signed deed with its UPI stamp, a Statement of Value if one applies, and checks made out to the Recorder of Deeds. Phone 814-765-2641, extension 5012 beforehand to learn the total for your page count.

Even a fast cash closing passes through the same two stops, the UPI office and then the recorder, so leave room for both.

Frequently asked questions

What is the filing charge for a Clearfield County deed?

The base fee is $79.75 for a deed or mortgage. Extra names beyond four are 50 cents each and extra pages beyond four are $2 each. The posted schedule carries a March 27, 2020 date, so phone 814-765-2641, extension 5012 for the current total.

What is the UPI fee in Clearfield County?

The UPI stamp costs $10 per parcel and has to be on the deed first. Ask about pre-approval on 814-765-2641, extension 2042.

Is e-recording offered in Clearfield County?

Yes, through Simplifile (800-460-5657) or CSC (866-652-0111). Your title company will usually start the submission.

When is a Statement of Value required in Clearfield County?

File it if the deed leaves out the full price, if the house is a gift, if you claim an exemption, after a tax claim or sheriff sale, or when property passes by will. A transfer exempt only because of close family ties skips the form.

Who pays Pennsylvania realty transfer tax?

Buyer and seller are jointly liable for the 1 percent state tax. Your sales contract decides who actually pays what share. The recorder collects it when the deed goes in.

Which Somerset County office takes my deed?

Deeds go to the Somerset County Recorder of Deeds, which works out of the County Annex Office Building at 300 North Center Avenue, Suite 400, Somerset, PA 15501. The phone number is (814) 445-1547. The county courthouse sits separately at 111 East Union Street, so a seller who is dropping off paperwork should head to the annex.

The county describes the office as the keeper of records about real property. More than fifty kinds of documents are filed there, among them deeds, mortgages, easements, powers of attorney, leases, agreements of sale, military discharges, subdivision plans and old mine maps. About 12,000 new documents are recorded each year.

What will the Somerset recorder charge on a deed?

The county's fee schedule took effect on November 14, 2025, under Act 45 of 2025. Its stated minimum covers the state fee and the recording fee for one instrument of up to four pages and four names. Any part of a page counts as a whole page, with no exceptions, so a document that spills a few lines onto a fifth sheet is billed for five.

The recorder posts a separate price list for additional pages and a fee sheet for each type of document. Ask the recorder's office for the current total on your deed before closing, since the number depends on page count, names and the type of instrument. The county also asks that the instructions on its fee notice be read closely, so that every filer pays by the same rules.

  • Count pages first, and treat a partial page as a full one.
  • Count every name that has to be indexed.
  • Confirm the fee for any extra document, such as a release or an easement, that comes with the deed.
  • Ask whether the transfer tax is paid separately from the recording fee.

How is transfer tax settled on a Somerset County sale?

The state levies 1 percent of the transferred value, and both the person handing over the deed and the person receiving it answer for the bill. The county recorder collects it, forwards the state's cut and deals with any local piece owed to the municipality or school district. Exemptions exist for some family transfers and for property that passes under a will or by intestacy.

Somerset County's recorder page links to the Department of Revenue's Common Level Ratio page. If your deed involves a gift, an inheritance or a sale well below market, ask the recorder's staff which transfer tax paperwork applies.

What should a Somerset County seller know about the county?

Somerset County is a large, thinly settled county in southwestern Pennsylvania. It was carved out of Bedford County on April 17, 1795, and spreads over 1,074 square miles of land, and has Mount Davis, the highest natural point in the state at 3,213 feet, in its southern part. Average temperatures in Somerset borough from 24.5 degrees in January to 67.1 in July, a spread that tells a seller to expect a real winter on the roof, gutters and heating system.

Somerset borough is the county seat. By 2010 head count, the biggest municipalities were Somerset Township (12,122), Conemaugh Township (7,452), Somerset borough (6,277) and Windber borough (4,683). The county is known for the Flight 93 National Memorial in Stonycreek Township near Shanksville, and for one of the oldest Amish communities in the country, founded in 1772.

How can I check records and get alerts from the Somerset County recorder?

The recorder's page offers Landex, an online records service with remote access instructions, plus Record Alert and Notary Alert sign-ups. A Record Alert is useful for homeowners who want to know when anything is filed against their name or property, so a surprise filing does not sit unnoticed.

  • Recorded plat maps are available through the recorder's page.
  • The county GIS parcel viewer draws on Tax Assessment Office and Recorder of Deeds records, and the county warns that it is not for exact measurement.
  • Plans for wind turbines and towers have their own recording rules, including a minimum sheet size of 18 by 24 inches.

How is Somerset County laid out and who lives there?

Somerset County runs along Pennsylvania's southern edge and borders Garrett and Allegany Counties in Maryland, along with Fayette, Westmoreland, Cambria and Bedford Counties in Pennsylvania. Cambria County was split from it in 1804, and its boundaries have held since. Forbes Road, cut through the area in 1758 during the campaign against Fort Duquesne, was one of the early western routes, and settlers from New Jersey reached the Turkeyfoot area around 1770.

Towns beyond the county seat include Windber, Meyersdale, Berlin, Boswell, Central City and Confluence. 29,344 households with 2.34 people on average, and 93.0% of residents had not moved in the previous year. A bachelor's degree is held by 17.9% of adults, and the typical rent is $753.

  • 1,647 employer establishments employed 18,678 people in 2023.
  • Retail sales totaled about $1.04 billion in 2022.
  • Builders took out 57 permits in 2025, so most buyers choose among existing houses.
  • The mean commute is 24.9 minutes, and 82.0% of households have broadband.

What should I prepare before a Somerset County closing?

Gather the existing deed, the latest tax bill, any mortgage payoff statement and a legible copy of the survey or plat if you have one. Recorded plat maps are available from the recorder's page, and the county parcel viewer helps you confirm the lot lines against the tax map number.

On deed day, count the pages and the names, make sure the notary block is complete, and ask whether your title company will record electronically or in person. A document with a missing acknowledgment costs more time than a lower price ever saves. If a relative died owning the house, the personal representative's authority has to be clear before anyone signs.

What if I want to sell a Somerset County house quickly?

Recording is the last step, so the sale itself comes first. A seller in a hurry can consider a direct cash purchase, which avoids showings, repair requests and financing delays. Expect a lower price than a polished listing, and weigh that against the commission and repairs a listing would cost.

Before any closing, pull your deed, get a payoff letter for any mortgage, and ask the recorder's office whether anything recorded against the parcel needs to be released. A paid-off mortgage with no recorded release is the kind of loose end to find before closing day.

Frequently asked questions

How do I reach the Somerset recorder in person?

It is at the County Annex Office Building, 300 North Center Avenue, Suite 400, in Somerset. The phone is (814) 445-1547. The courthouse is a separate building at 111 East Union Street.

What does the Somerset minimum recording fee cover?

The minimum covers the state fee and recording fee for one instrument with up to four pages and four names, under the schedule effective November 14, 2025. Call the recorder for the current dollar total for your document.

Is a part of a page billed as a whole page?

Yes. The county's fee notice says any fraction of a page is counted as one page, with no exceptions. Check the page count before you submit so the fee is right the first time.

Can I get an alert when a document is recorded on my property?

Yes. The county links to Landex Record Alert and Notary Alert sign-ups. You must register yourself, because the recorder's office cannot sign people up.

Who pays the state transfer tax on a Somerset sale?

Both sides are liable for the 1 percent state tax. Your sales agreement decides how buyer and seller divide the cost.

Where to record a deed in Indiana County

Indiana County deeds are recorded at the Register & Recorders Office in the county courthouse, 825 Philadelphia Street, Indiana, PA 15701. The phone is 724-465-3860 and the fax is 724-465-3863. The office is open Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. and closed on county holidays.

One office combines the Recorder of Deeds, the Register of Wills and the Clerk of Orphans' Court. It takes deeds, mortgages, satisfactions and other land documents in person, by mail or by e-recording through CSC or Simplifile. Every sale of an Indiana County house ends with the deed going through this counter or its electronic equivalent.

Recording rules and the 13-point checklist

The office publishes a 13-point recording checklist and says the list may not cover every policy. Reading it before closing prevents a returned package.

  • The acknowledgment date can't come before the date on the document. It must show county, state, date, the name and title of the person appearing, and the notary's signature and expiration date.
  • The municipality, county and state must be stated. For parcels in Blacklick, Canoe or Young Townships, the school district must be named too.
  • The UPI parcel number must appear on every real estate document.
  • Numerals must match the written amount on deeds and mortgages.
  • Mortgages must cite a book and page or instrument number that refers back to the original.
  • Deeds and mortgages need a certified grantee or mortgagee address, and the Certificate of Residence must be signed.
  • A deed with land in more than one municipality must state the percentage split of transfer taxes.
  • When several documents make up one transaction, mark the order of recording, for example deed first and then mortgage. Re-recording costs from the wrong order fall on whoever submitted them.

The office doesn't currently accept e-notarizations. An e-recording that makes staff print extra pages, such as a trust copy filed with a deed or the original deed attached to a corrective one, must be sent on paper or it is rejected. A returned document carries a $5 rejection fee.

Recording fees

A deed or mortgage is $91.75 on the document listing the office posted for November 1, 2025, which raised its JCS document fees by $1. Call to confirm the current figure. The fee schedule effective December 1, 2025 sits on the Register & Recorders page.

Checks and transfer tax

Indiana County asks for three separate checks made out to Recorder of Deeds, each for an exact amount: one for recording fees, one for the 1% municipal transfer tax and one for the state transfer tax. The printed fee sheet says the same thing by asking for two additional checks on a deed with transfer tax, one for 1% local and one for 1% state.

The deed must either come with a Statement of Value or state its exemption, for example a transfer between family members. One Statement of Value counts as a page of the document, and a second completed copy goes to the Department of Revenue.

The 1% state rate applies to the value of the real estate, and grantor and grantee are both liable. Exemptions cover certain family transfers, transfers to government units and property that passes by will or intestate succession.

Scams aimed at owners

The Register & Recorders Office warns that scammers have tried to sell property in the county. It urges owners to sign up for its free Property Alert, which notifies them of fraudulent recordings. It also advises watching for drivers who collect information from vacant properties while claiming to work for utility companies.

A second warning covers text messages saying delinquent taxes must be paid or a property will be sold. The county calls these fraudulent. The tax claim office doesn't text or call owners, and all its notices are written and mailed. Questions go to 724-465-3810.

If you've left a house empty while preparing to list, the alert lets you see every document recorded against the parcel.

Selling an inherited house

The Register of Wills asks anyone opening an estate to make an appointment first, by emailing the office to calculate costs and receive forms. For probate the office wants a copy of the petition, the death certificate, the will and any renunciations, plus the number of short certificates desired, so it can quote a total.

  • Inheritance tax payments can be mailed, and the postmark date counts as the payment date.
  • Short certificates are the papers a bank asks for.
  • The same courthouse office records the deed that follows, so heirs can finish both steps in Indiana.

The county won't change a deed once it is recorded, so any correction to a name needs a new, corrective deed. The posted fee for a corrective deed is $91.75, the same as a regular deed, and one that needs a copy of the original attached must be filed on paper if it is e-recorded.

Heirs who plan to sell should phone 724-465-3860 first, since probate here runs by appointment.

From closing table to recorded deed

Here is how a typical sale moves through the courthouse. The deed is signed and notarized at closing. The closing agent adds the UPI parcel number, checks that numerals match the written amount, and prepares the Statement of Value or the exemption language. If a mortgage is part of the deal, the order of recording is marked on each document.

Next come the three checks and, if you want the recorded original back, a stamped, self-addressed return envelope. The package goes to the courthouse, or the title company e-records it through CSC or Simplifile. Staff review it against the checklist. If everything fits, the deed is recorded and indexed. If not, it is returned with the $5 rejection fee, and the fix and resubmission fall to whoever sent it.

As the seller, you can ask your closing agent which route they use and when the package will arrive. A paper deed that is mailed takes longer than an e-recorded one.

Indiana County housing snapshot

Indiana County has an estimated 82,878 residents as of July 2025, nearly flat from the April 2020 base. The median owner-occupied value is $152,800 and the owner-occupied rate is 72.1% for 2020 to 2024. Monthly owner costs are $1,266 with a mortgage and $540 without, and median gross rent is $800.

A farm or acreage sale here may involve more than one parcel, and each parcel needs its own UPI number on the deed.

Frequently asked questions

Does Indiana County accept e-recording?

Yes, through CSC and Simplifile. The office doesn't currently accept e-notarizations, and an e-recording that needs extra pages printed must be submitted on paper.

What is the rejection fee in Indiana County?

A returned document carries a $5 rejection fee. Checking the recording checklist first avoids it.

Which Indiana County townships need a school district on the deed?

Blacklick, Canoe and Young Townships. The school district must be stated for parcels in those townships.

How many checks does Indiana County want for a deed with transfer tax?

Three, each payable to Recorder of Deeds: one for recording fees, one for the 1% municipal transfer tax and one for the state transfer tax.

How do I confirm the current deed fee in Indiana County?

Call 724-465-3860 or use the fee calculator on the county page. The November 2025 listing shows $91.75 for a deed, and the office asks callers to confirm.

Recording a deed in Armstrong County

The Register and Recorder handles deeds, from Suite 102 of the courthouse at 500 E. Market Street, Kittanning. One office holds three jobs: Recorder of Deeds, Register of Wills and Clerk of Orphans’ Court. The main number is (724) 548-3280.

Transactions are taken from 8:00 a.m. to 3:45 p.m., while records research runs until 4:15 p.m. Payment is by cash or check only. Cards of any kind are refused.

On the recorder’s side, the office keeps real estate records safe and files land documents, military discharges, notary bonds and commissions, and powers of attorney that deal with real estate.

Electronic and paper filing

A deed can be recorded electronically or on paper. Four e-recording vendors are listed: Simplifile, CSC Recording, ePN and Indecomm. A title company already using one of them can send a deed without a courier.

Staff check each document against a fixed list before accepting it.

  • The document date has to fall on or before the acknowledgment date.
  • Deeds and mortgages need a legal description that names the municipality, county and state.
  • A tax map number is required. It is not the same as a parcel number, and the Mapping Department, at (724) 548-3234, can supply it.
  • The acknowledgment needs the notary’s signature, a readable stamp and the expiration date.
  • A Certificate of Residence must be completed and signed.
  • Documents with shaded areas are not recorded.

Fees are not refunded, so the amount has to be right the first time. When several documents belong to one transaction, each page must show the intended recording order, and any re-recording expense caused by wrong order falls on whoever submitted them.

Transfer tax

The tax is 1% for the state and another 1% for the local governments and school district. Each is paid on a separate check, with a third check for the filing fee. All three are written to the Recorder of Deeds.

A Statement of Value, filed in duplicate, is needed in three situations: the full price is missing from the deed, the deed is a gift or has no consideration, or an exemption is claimed. It is also needed for rights of way and easements. A transfer that is wholly exempt on family grounds does not require one, provided the relationship is written on the deed. The office forwards one copy to the Department of Revenue.

A deed that names a price of $1.00 triggers the form, because the real value is not shown. When land spans more than one municipality, the deed must state each one’s percentage so the local tax divides correctly.

The state can revisit a sale later. If an investigator decides the property was worth more than stated, or that an exemption was invalid, the Department of Revenue sends a determination directly to the parties, collects the extra tax and interest itself, and issues a receipt for the recorder to file.

Fees and office facts

The recorder’s fee schedule is posted as a PDF on the county’s Register and Recorder page. Ask the office for the current sheet before closing.

Armstrong County recorder, other charges
ServiceCharge
Copies of recorded documents$0.50 per page
Large copy of a plan of lots, 11 by 17$3.00 per page
Military discharge filingNo fee

The Common Level Ratio changes each July 1, so ask the office which factor applies to the date on your deed.

Record searches are by first and last name or by book and page. The office cannot search by tax map number or street address, and its staff do not give legal advice. If you need a title history, hire a title company or an attorney.

Protection against deed fraud

The recorder runs a free Record Alert System through Landex, the recording vendor. Anyone who signs up gets an email whenever a document is recorded under their name, and businesses can sign up as well.

The same Landex site holds the county’s records for people who search often. A paid remote subscription suits frequent users and a pay-per-document web store suits occasional ones. Landex sets those charges, not the county. Owners who inherit or sell land here can use the alert to catch an unexpected deed or mortgage.

Armstrong County housing

Kittanning is the county seat, and the Allegheny River runs through the county. Population is 63,698 as of July 2025, with 32,314 housing units. About 78.8% of homes are owner-occupied, and the median value of an owner-occupied home is $157,300. Median household income is $65,008. With so many owner-occupied houses, most buyers choose among existing homes.

Documents to bring on closing day

Before anyone drives to Kittanning, make sure the packet has a notarized deed with a legal description, the tax map number, a signed Certificate of Residence, and three checks: state tax, local tax and filing fee. Add a Statement of Value in duplicate if the deed has no price, is a gift, or claims an exemption. Cash is accepted, but checks are easier to trace if a question comes up later.

Step by step for a seller

Most Armstrong County sellers never stand at the counter, but it helps to know the order. The title agent drafts the deed from your existing one, so keep a copy of how you took title. You sign before a notary at closing. The agent then adds the legal description, the tax map number and the Certificate of Residence, writes the three checks, and files the packet by e-recording or in person. Once the office accepts it, the buyer is on record as owner. If something is rejected, the office will say why, and the fix is usually a missing signature, a shaded area or a wrong date, so a second trip is rare when the list above is followed.

Sellers who inherited a house should ask whether the transfer is wholly exempt on family grounds. If it is, the relationship has to be written on the deed in plain words, or the office will expect a Statement of Value.

What a cash sale does not change

Selling for cash does not skip the recorder. The deed is still checked, taxed and filed here. What a cash deal removes is the buyer’s loan approval, which is often the slowest piece of a closing. If a mortgage is being paid off from your proceeds, ask the title company to confirm that the release is recorded afterward.

Frequently asked questions

Where is the Armstrong County Recorder of Deeds office?

It is inside the Register and Recorder’s office, Suite 102 of the Armstrong County Courthouse at 500 E. Market Street, Kittanning, PA 16201. The telephone is (724) 548-3280.

Can I pay with a credit card at the Armstrong County recorder?

No. The office accepts cash or check only. Plan checks ahead for the state tax, the local tax and the filing fee.

Is e-recording available for Armstrong County deeds?

Yes. Simplifile, CSC Recording, ePN and Indecomm are the listed vendors, so title companies using any of them can submit a deed electronically.

What is a tax map number and why does a deed need one?

It identifies the property in the county’s mapping system and has to appear on deeds and mortgages. It is not the parcel number. The Mapping Department at (724) 548-3234 can provide it.

Do I need a Statement of Value to record a deed?

You need one if the deed omits the full price, is a gift, or claims an exemption, and it must be filed in duplicate. A transfer wholly exempt because of family ties does not need one when the relationship appears on the deed.

Who records deeds in Lawrence County

The Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds is a combined office serving the county seat of New Castle. The Recorder's main duty is recording, protecting, preserving and reproducing legal documents that relate to real estate.

The same office collects county recording fees, the Real Estate Transfer Tax owed to the state, local municipalities and school districts, and the fees that state law sends to the Administrative Office of Pennsylvania Courts. For anyone selling a house in Lawrence County, one counter takes the tax and the fee and files the deed.

Ask the office for its current hours and its last time to accept a deed on a given day, since your title company's schedule depends on it.

Searching Lawrence County land records

Records reach back to the founding of the county in 1849, and all real estate records are open to the public. Older books are searched in the office, while more recent years can be searched online.

The online service runs on CountyFusion and lets you search, view and print documents dating to about 1970. The county also offers a quick land-records search from its cloud search page, and a free property alert service launched in October 2022 that warns an owner when a document is recorded against their property.

  • Use the online index to pull the previous deed and copy the legal description exactly.
  • Check that the name on the old deed matches the name of the person signing the new one.
  • Look for old mortgages that still show as open, and ask the lender for a satisfaction if one was paid off.

Electronic recording

Lawrence County accepts e-recording, which the office describes as simple, fast and money-saving. It names four vendors on its website: Simplifile, CSC, Indecomm and EPN. Closing agents who already use one of these can send the deed in without a courier.

Paper still works. A deed can be carried in or mailed to the Recorder, but you need the exact total in the right form, so call the office for a figure before you write a check. The Recorder's page also carries notices about a state-mandated fee increase and a separate increase in the parcel ID fee, so don't rely on an old fee sheet.

Recording fees

Recording charges on a Lawrence County fee sheet
ChargeAmount

Treat these numbers as a guide and get the real total from the Recorder, because the add-ons change with the page count and the number of parcels.

The county's Assessment Office assigns parcel IDs and provides a form to request a new one. A deed that covers more than one parcel costs more to record.

Transfer tax on a sale

Pennsylvania imposes a 1 percent state tax on the value of the transfer, and the Department of Revenue holds both grantor and grantee liable. The county fee sheet shows the local share as another 1 percent, for a combined 2 percent.

The Recorder sends the state's part to Harrisburg and the rest to the municipality and school district. Certain family transfers, transfers to government, and property that passes by will or intestacy are exempt, but a Statement of Value is still filed to show why.

  • A sale to an outside buyer is an ordinary transfer, so an estate selling a house should plan for the tax in its settlement figures.
  • If title first passes to an heir, the Register of Wills side of the same office can say what paperwork it wants.

What the Assessment Office handles

It values the county's roughly 56,000 parcels, which cover 367 square miles across 27 municipalities. One of them is the city of New Castle, with 8 wards, and the others are nine boroughs and sixteen townships. Ellwood City's second ward lies partly in Beaver County.

The office also runs the Act 72 Homestead and Farmstead Exclusion and the Clean and Green program, and it keeps the county's GIS tax maps. Its forms page lists a sales verification form, a change of address form, and a property owner contact form tied to Act 29 of 2026.

The Assessment Board meets monthly. If you sell a homestead property, ask the office how the sale affects the exclusion, and update your mailing address with its change of address form.

Lawrence County has 83,911 residents in the July 2025 estimate, down 2.5% since April 2020, and 39,704 housing units. Owners live in 75.8% of homes for 2020 to 2024, and the median owner-occupied home is worth $147,200. Median gross rent is $831.

Steps from signing to recorded deed

Start with the old deed. Pull it from the online index, copy the legal description exactly, and confirm the seller's name matches. Next, list each parcel by its ID from the Assessment Office. The deed is then signed and notarized at closing.

The closing agent adds a Statement of Value if tax is excused or the price isn't stated, and totals the recording fee, the $20.00 per parcel charge and the transfer tax. The package goes in electronically through one of the four vendors or on paper to the New Castle office. The Recorder files the deed, sends the tax to the state, municipality and school district, and the new owner enters the public record.

Afterward, check that any paid-off mortgage shows a satisfaction. An open mortgage on the record can slow the next buyer's title search, so ask your lender to file it.

What to bring to record a Lawrence County deed

Pull these together before the closing date.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the full legal description.
  • The parcel ID for each parcel being conveyed.
  • A Statement of Value if tax is excused or the price is not stated.
  • Payment for the recording fee, the parcel ID charge and the transfer tax, in the form the office accepts.
  • A return address for the recorded deed.

If a title company is handling the sale, confirm that they file electronically through one of the four vendors and ask when the recorded copy will arrive. A cash buyer skips the lender's steps, but this list stays the same.

Yes. The Recorder of Deeds lists four e-recording vendors on the county site: Simplifile, CSC, Indecomm and EPN. A closing agent with an account at one of them can submit the deed without a trip to New Castle.

How far back can I search Lawrence County deeds online?

The online system covers documents from about 1970 forward. County records start with the formation of the county in 1849, and the older volumes are searched in the office.

How much is transfer tax on a Lawrence County home sale?

The combined rate on the county fee sheet is 2 percent, made up of 1 percent state tax and 1 percent local tax. Exempt transfers, such as some family transfers, file a Statement of Value instead.

Is there a way to be warned if someone records a document on my property?

Yes. The county offers a free property alert service, launched in October 2022, as fraud protection. Ask the Recorder's office how to sign up.

What office issues parcel IDs in Lawrence County?

The county Assessment Office. It posts a Request for a New Parcel ID Number form, and it can tell you which parcels a deed must name. Every parcel on a deed adds to the recording cost.

Where do you record a deed in Wayne County, PA?

At the Recorder of Deeds office in the Wayne County Courthouse Annex, 925 Court Street, Honesdale, PA 18431. The phone is 570-253-5970, extension 4040. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and nothing is accepted for recording after 4:00 p.m.

Wayne County calls the office the custodian of the records and indexes for land transfers. It keeps deeds, mortgages, subdivision plans, rights-of-way and easements, and it also records the commissions and oaths of county officials, district justices and notaries, plus military discharges. A house sale in Wayne County ends here: after closing, the signed deed is recorded in Honesdale, and the new owner appears in the public record from that point.

The county asks one thing of readers up front. Staff cannot give legal advice or attorney referrals, so questions about how to word a deed belong with a lawyer, and the Wayne County Bar Association keeps a member list.

What new Uniform Parcel Identifier rule started in Wayne County in November 2026?

UPI certification began on November 2, 2026, at $20.00 per UPI number. The county posted the start date and the fee at the top of its recorder page, and its tax sale page notes that the Wayne County UPI Ordinance was adopted, with a $20.00 fee for each Uniform Parcel Identifier beginning that date.

For a seller, the practical effect is simple. A deed for a parcel now involves a certification step, and a sale that covers more than one parcel pays the $20.00 once per UPI number. Ask the recorder's office for the UPI notice, and have your closing agent or attorney confirm when the certification has to be completed.

The same date changed another number. The county's tax sale page says the deed recording fee became $94.75 as of November 2, 2026. That figure appears in the context of a tax sale deed, so ask the office to confirm the charge for an ordinary private sale deed.

What charges does Wayne County name on its recorder and tax sale pages?

Wayne County posts a fee schedule as a spreadsheet and a PDF, and the figures below are the ones stated on the county's web pages themselves.

Wayne County fees stated on county web pages
ItemAmountApplies to
UPI certification$20.00 per UPI numberDocuments recorded from November 2, 2026
E-recording helper pages$0.50 per pagePages attached to the REV-183 Statement of Value, from January 1, 2026
Deed recording fee, tax sale deed$94.75From November 2, 2026
Deed preparation fee, tax sale$25Added to a repository sale purchase
Bidder pre-registration$25, non-refundableTax sale bidders

For a plain deed, the county's page does not print one total, so call 570-253-5970, extension 4040, or open the fee schedule on the county's Recorder of Deeds page. The schedule is dated November 2026, and it lists fees by document type.

How can a Wayne County deed be e-recorded?

Through one of two vendors: CSC at 866-652-0111 or Simplifile at 800-460-5657. Most land-related documents can be sent that way without a trip to Honesdale.

Two kinds of document cannot be e-recorded and must be delivered on paper: subdivision plans, and deeds that are taxable in more than one jurisdiction. The second exception comes up when a parcel lies in more than one municipality: the deed then has to state the percentage in each so the local transfer tax divides correctly.

  • E-recorded transactions with a REV-183 Statement of Value attach helper pages, and those pages cost $0.50 each.
  • Paper filings go to the courthouse annex before the 4:00 p.m. cutoff.
  • Faxed or emailed copies are not accepted for recording.

What does the Wayne County recorder require on a deed?

The county publishes a checklist, and it is stricter than many sellers expect. An acknowledgment must show the county, state, date, the people or corporate officers appearing, and the notary's signature, stamp and expiration date. If any of those is missing, the acknowledgment is treated as defective.

  • The written amount of consideration has to match the number on the deed.
  • Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a signed certification of the grantee's address with zip code.
  • Transfer taxes or a completed Statement of Value must accompany every deed.
  • Black ink and white or manila paper only, since the office scans everything.
  • Documents may not exceed 8 1/2 by 14 inches, and maps may not exceed 24 by 36 inches.
  • Recorded papers come back by mail only if you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope.

What is Wayne County like for a house sale?

It is a rural, lake-and-hill county in the Poconos with a small population. The Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 51,703 people on about 726 square miles of land, which works out to roughly 70 people per square mile. The county was formed in 1798 from part of Northampton County, and Honesdale is both the seat and the largest borough.

QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 shows 80.5 percent owner-occupancy, a median owner-occupied home value of $242,100, median gross rent of $1,038 and median household income of $62,381. Residents aged 65 or older make up 27.2 percent of the population, which is high, and 32,637 housing units serve only 20,877 households.

The county's boroughs are Bethany, Hawley, Honesdale, Prompton, Starrucca and Waymart. Terrain varies from rugged ground along the New York border to a wide central plain, and the Delaware River separates the county from New York. Winters are cold, with Honesdale averaging about 22.8 degrees in January, so heating systems and roofs draw attention at inspection. Six school districts serve the county: Forest City Regional, North Pocono, Susquehanna Community, Wallenpaupack Area, Wayne Highlands and Western Wayne.

What should a Wayne County seller know about assessments and unpaid taxes?

The Assessment Office maintains property records and prepares the tax rolls, and it does not set millage rates or collect taxes. It sits at 925 Court Street in Honesdale, phone 570-253-5970, extension 4010, open 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The county has 28 municipalities and 6 school districts, all of which draw on those rolls.

Back taxes go to the Tax Claim Bureau, extension 4000, at the same address. It runs sales under the Real Estate Tax Sale Law, and unsold properties go on a repository list. Repository sales are held quarterly in February, May, August and November, and the owner can pay up to the day of the sale. Buyers at a repository sale pay costs, a $25 deed preparation fee and 2 percent transfer tax, and Act 33 requires every bidder to pre-register.

If a back-tax balance sits on the house you want to sell, ask the Tax Claim Bureau for a payoff figure before closing.

Frequently asked questions

What are the Wayne County Recorder of Deeds hours?

The office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., but it takes no documents for recording after 4:00 p.m. It is in the Courthouse Annex at 925 Court Street in Honesdale, and the phone is 570-253-5970, extension 4040.

Is there a new fee for parcel identifiers in Wayne County?

Yes. Uniform Parcel Identifier certification began on November 2, 2026, and costs $20.00 per UPI number. The county's recorder page links a UPI notice that explains the process.

Can I e-record a Wayne County deed?

Yes, with exceptions. Use CSC (866-652-0111) or Simplifile (800-460-5657). Subdivision plans and deeds taxable in multiple jurisdictions cannot be e-recorded and must go in on paper.

Does Wayne County mail back a recorded deed?

Only if you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope when you submit it. Without one, the Recorder's Office does not mail recorded documents.

Where do I see who owns a Wayne County parcel?

Search recorded documents on Landex, which the county uses for online records. Index searching is free, and you pay only when you buy copies of documents to download or print.
