Where to record a deed

Columbia County deeds go to the Register and Recorder's Office at 35 West Main Street, Bloomsburg, PA 17815. Call 570-389-5632. That office also handles wills and estates, but a home sale only touches the Recorder of Deeds side.

The office posts three documents on its website: a fee schedule, a realty transfer tax policy and a list of recording requirements. Landex online access is available for searching records. Whoever assembles your closing package, whether a title agent or your own agent, should read all three, since a deed that breaks one rule comes back for correction.

Bloomsburg is the county seat, and it is where couriers and title agents bring Columbia County closing paperwork.

Recording fees

The schedule effective November 17, 2025 puts a deed or mortgage at $87.75. Each of those fees already folds in a $3.00 Recorder Improvement Fund charge and a $2.00 County Improvement Fund charge, and amounts marked with two asterisks include the state surcharges added under Act 45.

Columbia County recording fees by document type
DocumentRecording fee
Deed, corrective deed, deed of distribution$87.75
Mortgage, re-recorded deed or mortgage$87.75
Satisfaction or release of mortgage$59.75
Assignment of mortgage, easement, right of way$59.75
Power of attorney, affidavit, lease$18.50
UCC filing$100.00
Name search$20.00
Copies, per page (8.5 x 11 or 8.5 x 14)$0.50

Deeds and mortgages pick up extras: $1.00 for every name past four, $1.00 for each tract after the first, and $4.00 for every page past four. Other instruments charge 50 cents, 50 cents and $2.00 for the same things. A military discharge is recorded free. If the office mails a document back for fixes, it adds a $2.00 service charge.

Checks you need at closing

Plan on three payments. The fee schedule calls for two separate checks for realty transfer tax, each equal to 1 percent of the sale price or fair market value, with the recording fee paid on top.

Pennsylvania's tax is 1 percent at the state level, collected by the county recorder along with an optional local tax. Buyer and seller are jointly liable. The recorder sends the state portion to the Department of Revenue, and local governments may divide their portion between school districts and municipalities. If land lies in more than one municipality, the deed must state what percentage of the tax belongs to each.

When the full tax is not being paid, a Statement of Value form goes in place of the check. Fill it out completely, and write out any claimed exemption along with the reason. The price has to read the same in words and in numbers.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Columbia County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

What the recorder requires on a deed

The county's checklist is labeled a partial list of twenty items. These are the ones most likely to decide whether a house deed gets accepted.

  • Signatures and initials must be original, with blue ink preferred.
  • The document needs a date, and the acknowledgment cannot be dated earlier.
  • The acknowledgment has to be a formal one, not "sworn and subscribed," and include state, county, date, name, notary signature, stamp and expiration date.
  • A deed carries the buyer's Certificate of Residence or exact address, signed in original ink.
  • Anyone signing under a/k/a names signs each one, and each appears in the acknowledgment.
  • Foreign language documents come with an English translation.
  • Pages can be up to 8.5 by 14 inches, except maps. No margin rules apply because the office attaches a cover sheet to every document.

Mail-in packages need a stamped, self-addressed return envelope big enough for the contents. Maps must be signed and acknowledged by the owners. Subdivision plans need county or municipal approval and must be recorded within 90 days of it. The office does not take mylar.

Corrections and other services

A name search is $20.00, and copies are $0.50 a page on 8.5 by 11 or 8.5 by 14 paper or $1.00 on 11 by 17. Certifying Recorder of Deeds documents costs $1.50.

Errors can be fixed, though the process is strict. Re-recording a deed takes the original document with its original recording cover sheet, a written reason, and a new acknowledgment. When the original notary is unavailable, the parties sign again in front of a different one. Mortgages follow similar address rules: the lender's Certificate of Residence or exact address goes on a mortgage, and the assignee's goes on an assignment.

A corporation, partnership or other entity signs through an authorized officer. That person's title and company name appear under the signature and again in the acknowledgment.

Housing in Columbia County

The county had an estimated 66,193 people in July 2025, up 2.3 percent from the 2020 base. Bloomsburg (14,855 in 2010) and Berwick (10,477) are the two largest communities. The county covers 483 square miles along the Susquehanna River in central Pennsylvania, with farmland and state game lands across much of it.

There were 30,065 housing units, and 69.5 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The median owner-occupied value is $206,200, median gross rent is $943 and median household income is $64,644. The county issued 111 building permits in 2025, which points to a market with steady activity.

When you price your home, a title agent or local agent can tell you how your borough compares. Bloomsburg, Berwick, Catawissa, Millville, Benton and Orangeville are the main places buyers search.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Columbia County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Seller checklist

Begin with the title company or attorney running your closing and ask who will deliver the deed to Main Street in Bloomsburg.

  • Confirm the November 17, 2025 fee total for your deed's page and name count.
  • Write two transfer tax checks of 1 percent each, plus a check for the recording fee.
  • Check that the notary block names the correct county and shows an unexpired commission.
  • Attach the buyer's Certificate of Residence, signed in ink.
  • Enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope if the package is mailed.

Inherited houses may be exempt. Property passing by will or intestate succession is exempt from the transfer tax, and the county requires a Statement of Value to document the exemption.

A deed that is rejected delays the buyer's title, so build in a day or two for corrections. Phone 570-389-5632 with questions before you send anything. If the sale is a cash deal with a quick closing, the same recording rules apply, so have the notary block and the buyer's address certificate ready ahead of time instead of fixing them after the signing, since a notary has to be present again for any new acknowledgment.

Frequently asked questions

What is Columbia County's base charge for a deed?

A deed or mortgage is $87.75 under the schedule effective November 17, 2025. Names, tracts and pages past the limits add $1.00, $1.00 and $4.00 each.

Does Columbia County want one check or several?

Two checks for transfer tax, each for 1 percent of the sale price or fair market value, and a third for the recording fee. The county's fee schedule requires the two separate tax checks.

Does Columbia County require a Certificate of Residence on a deed?

Yes. Each deed carries the buyer's Certificate of Residence or exact address, signed in original ink.

Can I mail a deed to the Columbia County recorder?

Yes, if the package meets every recording requirement and includes a stamped, self-addressed envelope large enough for the return. Send it to 35 West Main Street, Bloomsburg, or call 570-389-5632.

How soon must a Columbia County subdivision plan be recorded?

Within 90 days of its approval date. The plan needs county or municipal approval, and mylar is not accepted.

Where to record a deed in Huntingdon County

Deeds are recorded by the Huntingdon County Register & Recorder. The Register & Recorders Office covers three jobs: the Register of Wills, the Recorder of Deeds and the Clerk of the Orphans' Court.

Call (814) 643-2740 and choose option 2 for fee schedules, deeds, wills and marriage licenses. Recorded documents here run from 1787 to the present. Deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, releases, subdivision plans, agreements and easements, highway maps and secured transactions all live in this office.

A seller meets the office at the end of a sale, when the signed deed is recorded and the new owner enters the public index.

UPI numbers

A UPI is the Uniform Parcel Identifier. Huntingdon County has required one on real estate documents since October 1, 2014 under county Ordinance 2014-2. It is the same number that appears as the tax parcel number on a tax bill and in the County Assessment Office.

The Assessment Department, through its Mapping Department, compares the document against county records and accepts or rejects it based on the accuracy of that number. The county says the check keeps recorded documents accurate and helps later real estate searches.

  • The UPI must be the first line on the document, below the top margin.
  • The top margin must be at least 2 inches.
  • The certification fee is $20 for each UPI number certified, paid with the other recording fees to the Recorder of Deeds.

A deed that covers a house and a separate lot can carry two parcel numbers, and each certified number adds $20 to the recording bill.

How UPI certification works

Walk-in customers take documents to the Mapping Department at 233 Penn Street, Huntingdon, PA 16652, between 8:30 a.m. and 4:30 p.m. on weekdays except holidays. A submission made after 4:15 p.m. is processed the next business day.

Mail-in and e-file customers send documents to the Recorder of Deeds, which processes them in the order received. The Mapping Department collects mail-in documents daily and returns them to the recorder within one business day.

The split affects timing. A closing agent who walks a deed in at 4:20 p.m. has missed the same-day window. A package submitted electronically goes through the recorder first and needs no trip to Penn Street. Ask the Register & Recorders Office which route fits your closing schedule.

Recording fees and transfer tax

The base recording fee for a deed or mortgage comes from the county fee schedule, and the office quotes it by phone at (814) 643-2740, option 2. One add-on is fixed: $20 per UPI number certified.

What to ask the office to total before closing
ChargeHow it is set
Base recording feeCounty fee schedule, quoted by phone
UPI certification$20 for each UPI number certified
Per-page chargeQuoted by the office
Realty transfer taxState rate of 1% of value, plus a local tax

Ask for the full total before closing, with the UPI line for each parcel. Whoever runs the closing sends these amounts with the deed, and the figures belong on the settlement statement.

Transfer tax is the larger cost. The Pennsylvania Department of Revenue sets the state rate at 1% of the value of the real estate. County recorders collect it, usually along with an additional local tax. Grantor and grantee are both liable, and the recorder passes the state's 1% along to the Department.

Some transfers are exempt, including certain transfers between family members, transfers to government units, deeds to burial sites, and property that passes by will or intestate succession.

Seller checklist before the deed is signed

Start with the parcel number. Check the latest tax bill, or ask the County Assessment Office, so the number typed on the first line of the deed matches the records the Mapping Department will compare it with.

  • Confirm the margin: at least 2 inches at the top of the first page, with the UPI number on the first line below it.
  • Decide how the deed will travel. In person it goes to the Mapping Department first. Mail and e-file documents go to the recorder, who passes them along for certification.
  • List every parcel being conveyed, because each UPI number certified is $20.
  • Ask the Register & Recorders Office for the total recording fee before the closing date.
  • If the transfer claims an exemption from realty transfer tax, ask the Department of Revenue or the closing attorney which paperwork supports it.

Subdivision plans are recorded in this office too. If you divided off a lot, check that the plan was recorded, because a deed that references a lot needs a recorded description to point to.

From signed deed to recorded deed

The path is short but unforgiving about details. The deed is signed and notarized at closing, and the closing agent confirms the parcel number against the tax bill. The UPI goes on the first line, with the top margin of at least 2 inches kept clear.

Next, the package is certified. In person, that means the Mapping Department before 4:15 p.m. if you want same-day service. By mail or e-file, the Recorder of Deeds receives it first and the Mapping Department collects it the same day, returning it within one business day.

Finally the recorder charges the fees, records the deed and adds the new owner to the index. If the number is wrong or the margin is short, the document is rejected, and you correct it and resubmit. A cash buyer and seller can close quickly, but the UPI step is the same for every sale, so build a day or two of slack into the schedule.

Military discharge papers

Military discharge records are recorded in the Recorder of Deeds office, but they are secure records closed to the public. A DD-214 is given only to the person named on it, who must show proper identification.

Anyone else asking for the information is directed to the county's military affairs officer at (814) 643-1360. If you need the document for a loan or a benefit tied to your sale, bring identification to the recorder's office in person.

Huntingdon County housing snapshot

Huntingdon County has an estimated 43,001 residents in 2025, down 2.4% from the April 2020 base, and 79.2% of homes are owner-occupied. The county has 21,148 housing units. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $183,200 for 2020 to 2024, and median gross rent is $810.

Most of the county is rural, and a Huntingdon County deed often describes land in more than one tax parcel. Each parcel needs its own UPI certification, so ask early what the deed and recording will cost.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I record a deed in Huntingdon County?

Record it with the Register & Recorders Office at (814) 643-2740, option 2. UPI certification for walk-ins happens at the Mapping Department, 233 Penn Street in Huntingdon.

How much is UPI certification in Huntingdon County?

It is $20 per UPI number certified. You pay it to the Recorder of Deeds with the other recording fees.

What is the cutoff for same-day UPI certification in Huntingdon County?

A walk-in submission to the Mapping Department after 4:15 p.m. is processed the next business day. Walk-in hours run 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays.

How far back do Huntingdon County recorded documents go?

Documents in the Recorder of Deeds office date from 1787 to the present day.

Who can get a military discharge record in Huntingdon County?

Only the person named on it, with proper identification. Others contact the county's military affairs officer at (814) 643-1360.

Where do I take a deed in Lewisburg?

You will find the office inside the Union County Courthouse, 103 South Second Street, Lewisburg, PA 17837. Call (570) 524-8762 with questions. It shares space with the Register of Wills, and the same elected office covers both jobs. The counter is open from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, though the county notes that document recording concludes at 4:15 p.m.

That fifteen minute gap trips up closings. A deed brought in at 4:20 is not recorded that day, so a title agent or seller who needs same-day recording should plan to arrive well before the cutoff.

What does the Union County recorder do?

Its job is to record paperwork tied to land and buildings: deeds, mortgages, releases, easements and rights of way, subdivisions and restrictions. It also records notary and county officer information and military service discharges. Records from January 1, 1962 to the present can be searched online, and anything earlier is on microfilm.

The recorder also collects the real estate transfer tax for the state, the townships, the boroughs and the school districts. That makes it the last stop in a sale: the buyer and seller sign at closing, then the deed is recorded here and the taxes are paid at the same time.

What are the recording rules for a deed in Union County?

The county publishes a short list of recording requirements, and a document that misses one comes back unrecorded. Mailed documents that cannot be recorded are returned with a letter of explanation and a $3.00 charge.

  • The acknowledgment must show the county, state, date, the people or corporate officers who appeared, and the notary's signature, seal and expiration date.
  • The notary stamp must be clear, and the stamp, seal and signature must not overlap one another.
  • Every deed, mortgage and mortgage assignment needs a signed certificate of address for the grantee, mortgagee or assignee.
  • A re-recorded document needs fresh acknowledgments and a note on why it is being filed again.
  • A Statement of Value, when one is required, must be filed in duplicate, fully completed, signed and dated.
  • Each recorded document and each transfer tax payment gets its own check, payable to Union County Recorder of Deeds.
  • Blanket documents are refused, and checks must be for the exact amount because no refunds are given.
  • Return by mail needs a stamped, self-addressed envelope supplied at the time of recording.

What will Union County charge to record my deed?

The county posts a recorder's fee schedule on its website, and the amount depends on the type of document, its page count and the number of names. Ask the office at (570) 524-8762 for the current total on your deed before you write the check, since checks must match the fee exactly.

On top of that, the state takes 1 percent of the property's value as transfer tax, with buyer and seller sharing the legal duty to pay. The recorder sends the state portion onward, and local governments may divide their own tax between municipalities and school districts. Some family transfers and property passing by will or intestacy are exempt.

What does a Union County seller need to know about the county?

Union County is one of the smallest counties in Pennsylvania, the fourth smallest by area, at 316 square miles of land. It was created on March 22, 1813 from part of Northumberland County. Mifflinburg was the first county seat, New Berlin took over in 1815, and Lewisburg has held the role since 1855.

It is also far more densely settled than Somerset or Venango County, with 135.1 residents per square mile in 2020 against 69.0 and 74.8 there. The county has four boroughs, Hartleton, Lewisburg, Mifflinburg and New Berlin, and its main roads include Interstate 80, US 15 and PA 45. In 2010 Lewisburg had 5,792 residents and Mifflinburg 3,540.

How is Union County laid out and who lives there?

Union County sits in central Pennsylvania and borders Lycoming, Northumberland, Snyder, Mifflin, Centre and Clinton Counties. R. B. Winter State Park and Sand Bridge State Park lie within its borders, and the overlook at Shikellamy State Park is in the county as well. Average temperatures in Lewisburg from 27.2 degrees in January to 72.7 in July.

14,546 households averaging 2.30 people. Residents move more often than in the other two counties, since only 79.3% stayed in the same house over the prior year, and 26.5% of adults have a bachelor's degree. The average commute is a short 17.9 minutes, and 11.0% speak another language at home.

Why does Union County recording go smoothly for some sales and not others?

Rejected recordings usually trace back to the acknowledgment or the checks. The county's own list shows how specific the office is: a legible notary stamp, a seal that does not overlap the signature, a certificate of address and exact payment. Two sellers closing on the same day can have different outcomes simply because one deed had a clean notary block and the other did not.

If a house is being sold by an estate, the Register of Wills sits in the same office and handles probate and inheritance tax, with checks for inheritance tax payable to Union County Register of Wills, Agent. A seller settling an estate can often resolve both matters on one visit to the courthouse in Lewisburg.

What should a seller bring to the Union County recorder?

Most sales are recorded by the title company, but a seller who handles the paperwork should assemble the signed and notarized deed, the certificate of address for the buyer, a Statement of Value when the tax is not paid in full, separate checks for the recording fee and for each tax payment, and a stamped return envelope. Having every item on this list in one folder is what keeps a closing from slipping a day.

  • Deed with a complete, legible notary block.
  • Signed certificate of address for the grantee.
  • Checks written to Union County Recorder of Deeds, one per document and per tax.
  • Statement of Value in duplicate, if it applies.

A seller who wants to skip showings and repairs can ask for a direct cash purchase on a timeline of their own choosing, and the recording steps above are the same either way.

Frequently asked questions

When does the Union County recorder stop taking documents?

Recording ends at 4:15 p.m., even though the office stays open for fifteen minutes longer. Anything that arrives after 4:15 waits for the next business day.

Will the Union County office accept a deed by mail?

Yes, as long as you enclose a stamped, self-addressed envelope and the right checks. A document that cannot be recorded is returned with a letter of explanation and a $3.00 fee.

How far back do Union County online records go?

Records from January 1, 1962 to the present can be searched online. Earlier records were placed on microfilm and are available through the office.

Can one check cover everything?

No. The recording requirements call for separate checks for each recorded document and for each realty transfer tax payment, all in the correct amount.

Which Union County office collects the transfer tax?

The Recorder of Deeds collects it for the state, townships, boroughs and school districts. The state rate is 1 percent, and local shares are added by the municipalities and districts.

Where deeds are recorded

How you pay matters as much as how much. The office stopped accepting credit and debit cards on June 1, 2025, so a closing package should arrive with a check for the recording fee and a check for the transfer tax. If the title company handles recording, ask which of its checks covers each charge.

  • Ask whether the office can take the package by mail and whether a return envelope is needed.
  • Keep the recording receipt. It shows the date the new owner entered the record.

Realty transfer tax

The state tax is one percent of what the property is worth, collected at recording by the county recorder. Under state rules the grantor and the grantee are both held jointly and severally liable, so a missed payment can be pursued against either party.

Counties usually collect an additional local realty transfer tax at the same time. The recorder forwards the 1 percent state share to the Department of Revenue, and local governments may split their share between the school district and the municipality. Ask the recorder which local rate applies to the borough or township where the house stands.

Some transfers are exempt from the tax.

  • Certain transfers among family members.
  • Transfers to governmental units and between religious organizations.
  • Transfers to shareholders or partners, and to or from nonprofit industrial development agencies.
  • Deeds to burial sites and farms, and property passed by will or intestate succession.

If you claim an exemption, ask the recorder what paperwork the office wants with the deed.

Searching land records

Many records can be searched online around the clock through the Infocon County Access System, a subscription service the county points people to. Searching in person is free during public hours, and the office keeps land records from 1840 forward.

A search helps a seller in a few ways. It shows whether an older mortgage was ever satisfied of record, whether a prior deed in the chain was recorded, and what the legal description said when the current owner bought. An heir who inherited a Clarion County house can check how the previous owner took title. Birth and death certificates after 1906 aren't kept here. They're filed with the state's vital records office, and the county page links to VitalChek for ordering.

Military discharge papers and adoption records are the exceptions to public access, so an owner who needs a discharge on file should ask the office how to request it.

Clarion County housing context

Clarion County covers 610 square miles in Northwestern Pennsylvania, with 601 of them land. The seat is the borough of Clarion, which had 3,931 residents in 2020. The county had 36,680 residents in July 2025, 1.5 percent fewer than after the 2020 count.

What happens after recording

Once the clerk records the deed, the buyer's name is in the public record, and the recording date becomes the date the new owner entered it. Keep the receipt with your closing papers. If you later need to prove who held title, or show a lender or title agent how you acquired the house, you can look the deed up in person for free during public hours or search online by subscription.

If something looks wrong on the recorded page, the office can't offer legal advice, so bring the question to your attorney or closing agent. A search of the record is also a good way to check that your old mortgage was satisfied of record and that every deed in the chain was recorded, which a buyer's title agent will check as well.

Checklist before closing

A short list prevents a delay at the recorder's counter.

  • Phone (814) 226-4000 to confirm the current fee schedule and any recording requirements for the deed.
  • Make sure the deed names the municipality where the property sits, since the local transfer tax follows that location.
  • Prepare checks for the recording fee and for state and local transfer tax. The office stopped taking cards on June 1, 2025.
  • If a family exemption or another exemption applies, ask what form the office needs filed with the deed.
  • Decide who will deliver the package and who receives the recorded original.

A quick sale for an heir or an owner behind on payments follows the same recording steps. The deed is still signed, still recorded in Clarion, and the transfer tax is still figured on the sale price. Allow time for the title agent to collect both checks, and confirm the amounts with the recorder's office the day before the closing.

Frequently asked questions

Where do I take a deed in Clarion County?

Go to the Register and Recorder's Office in the Clarion County Courthouse, Suite 24, 421 Main Street, Clarion, PA 16214. The phone number is (814) 226-4000, and the public may inspect records on weekdays between 8:30 and 4:30.

Will the Clarion County office take a debit card?

No. The office stopped accepting credit and debit card payments on June 1, 2025, so bring a check for the recording fee and for the transfer tax.

What does Pennsylvania charge when a house changes hands?

The state tax is one percent of what the property is worth, and buyer and seller are both liable. Counties usually collect a local tax of their own at recording, so the total is higher than 1 percent.

How old are the land records held in Clarion?

Land records run back to 1840, and the office also holds a few deeds from Venango and Armstrong counties dating to 1800. Many of the records can be searched online through a subscription service.

Does Clarion County require an attorney at the recorder's counter?

The office gives no legal advice, so a lawyer or the closing agent should prepare the deed and answer questions about exemptions. The office records the document once it meets requirements and the fees are paid.

Which Venango County office takes my deed?

The Register and Recorder office handles deeds from the county courthouse, 1168 Liberty Street, Franklin, PA 16323, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 831. It opens on weekdays at 8:30 in the morning, closes at 4:30 in the afternoon and shuts for legal holidays.

The same elected office also serves as Register of Wills and Clerk of Orphans' Court, so probate filings, marriage licenses and real estate recordings all run through one courthouse counter. A seller dealing with an inherited house will often visit for both reasons.

Can Venango County deeds be recorded electronically?

Yes. The county says electronic filing of real estate documents is handled by CSC eRecording Solutions, reachable at 866-652-0111. Title companies and attorneys commonly use e-recording because it skips the courthouse trip and the mail time, and it fits well when buyer and seller sign in different places.

The Register and Recorder's page does not print the recording fees in the text of the page. It tells filers to contact the office for fees or a fee schedule, and the county also posts a Recorder of Deeds fee schedule dated November 2025 in its document library. Call the office for the exact total on your deed before you send payment.

How is transfer tax handled in a Venango County sale?

The recorder collects it when the deed is filed. The state's cut is 1 percent of the value, and the person conveying and the person receiving the property both answer for it. Local governments can add a tax of their own and split it between school districts and municipalities.

  • Exempt transfers include some family gifts, transfers to government bodies and property passed by will or intestacy.
  • Of what the state collects, 15 percent is set aside for the Keystone Recreation, Park and Conservation Fund and most of the remainder reaches the General Fund.
  • The sales contract sets who pays in practice, so read that clause before you sign.

Venango County has two cities, Franklin and Oil City, plus boroughs and townships, and the local share depends on where the parcel sits. Ask the recorder which municipality and school district your parcel falls in before you work out your net proceeds.

Why does oil history matter for a Venango County house?

Venango County was created in 1800 and organized in 1805, and its name comes from a Native American word for otter. The county is tied to the start of the oil industry. On August 28, 1859, George Bissell and Edwin L. Drake used the first successful drilling rig near Titusville, and the well sat less than a mile inside the Venango County line. Oil boom towns followed, among them Franklin, Oil City and the now vanished Pithole City.

The industry also shaped the land. French Creek, which runs 117 miles, joins the Allegheny River near Franklin, and Riverfront Park in Franklin sits at that meeting point. A seller with an older house in the two cities should expect a buyer's inspector to look hard at the foundation, wiring and plumbing.

What do the Venango County housing numbers show?

Venango County has been losing residents for decades. Its population peaked at 65,328 in 1950 and stood at 50,454 in 2020. The Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate is 49,346, down 2.2% from the 2020 base. By 2018 estimates, Oil City (9,897), Cranberry Township (6,789), Franklin (6,231) and Sugar Creek borough (5,008) were the largest places.

How is Venango County laid out and who lives there?

The county covers 683 square miles, 674 of them land, in northwestern Pennsylvania. It borders Crawford, Warren, Forest, Clarion, Butler and Mercer Counties. The Drake Well Museum stands in Cherrytree Township, and the area around Oil City and Franklin is known as the Oil Region.

A settled, older population. Households average 2.28 people, 90.5% of residents did not move in the past year, and 27.2% are 65 or older. How has the Venango County population changed over time?

The county grew fast during the oil boom, from 25,043 residents in 1860 to 47,925 in 1870. After a dip to 43,670 in 1880 it climbed past 56,000 by 1910 and peaked at 65,328 in 1950. Since then each census has counted fewer people, ending at 59,381 in 1990, 54,984 in 2010 and 50,454 in 2020.

One early oil figure is worth knowing: Henry Huttleston Rogers started his first refinery venture, the Wamsutta Oil Refinery, in 1861 at McClintocksville in Cornplanter Township, before he joined Standard Oil. Stories like that explain why so many Venango County properties have old deeds, old easements and mineral questions, and why a title search matters on a long-held parcel. Ask your title company to look for recorded easements, rights of way and releases ahead of closing.

Which Venango County communities do sellers come from?

The county has two cities, Franklin, which is the seat, and Oil City, the largest place. Boroughs include Sugar Creek, Pleasantville, Polk, Emlenton, Rouseville, Clintonville, Cooperstown, Barkeyville and Utica. Cranberry and Cornplanter are the two most populous townships, and Hasson Heights, Woodland Heights and Seneca are census-designated places.

Because each of these has its own municipal government, a parcel's zoning, permit rules and local tax shares depend on the address. Before listing, call the borough, city or township office that covers your house and ask what an inspector or buyer is likely to raise. The recorder's staff can tell you which municipality and school district a parcel belongs to when the deed is filed.

How do I look up real estate tax rates in Venango County?

The county publishes a Real Estate Tax Millages page with a PDF for every year from 2005 through 2026. Check the latest sheet for your municipality and school district, since the millage that applies to a house depends on where it sits. Ask the county's Tax Assessment Office, also in the courthouse complex, about the assessed value behind that bill.

Buyers will ask for the figures, so keep your last tax bill handy when you talk to a title company. A seller who would rather skip repairs can consider a direct as-is cash purchase, since fixing an older home can cost more than the market returns.

Weekdays from 8:30 a.m. until 4:30 p.m., closed on legal holidays, in the courthouse at 1168 Liberty Street in Franklin.

Yes. The county names CSC eRecording Solutions as the processor of electronic real estate filings, at 866-652-0111. Your title company or attorney can usually set this up.

The county posts a Recorder of Deeds fee schedule from November 2025 in its document library, and the Register and Recorder's page tells you to contact the office for fees. Call before you send a check.

Who handles probate for a Venango County house?

The Register of Wills handles probate and collects inheritance tax for the Commonwealth. In Venango County that office is combined with the Recorder and the Clerk of Orphans' Court.

What transfer tax rate applies in Venango County?

The state's piece is 1 percent of the value. A municipality and school district may add shares, so ask the recorder for the combined rate on your parcel.

Crawford County recording office

One office, the Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, does both jobs. It is open weekdays from 8:30 to 4:30, and the phone is 814-373-2537. Land records filed here include deeds, mortgages, mortgage satisfactions and releases, agreements such as oil and gas leases, UCC filings, notary publics and powers of attorney.

You can search records online back to 1954, and land records go back to 1800. For entries from 1954 through 1974, check the index books in the office. Written requests for copies cost $0.50 a page.

Owners can enroll in a free property fraud monitor built into the Landex software, which flags new filings recorded against the property.

What recording costs

Under the November 17, 2025 schedule, filing either a deed or a mortgage costs $74.75. Four pages and four indexed names are included; beyond that, add $0.50 per name and $2.00 per page.

Smaller items round out the list. A notary commission is $33.50, a declaration of taking is $10.00 plus $1.00 for each added page, a highway map is $16.50 plus $3.00 for each added page, and a UCC filing is $100.00. Faxed copies are $1.00 a page, a plan map copy is $10.00, and certifying a document is $1.50. A marginal notation is $2.00; it links a new document to an earlier one in the computer index and does not mark up the earlier document itself.

A payment that runs over by $5.00 or less is accepted and shown on the receipt as an overpayment. Mailing it in? Add a return envelope with at least $1.00 of postage, or a self-addressed stamped one. A fee calculator for the main recording documents is on the county website.

Parcel numbers and transfer tax

Any document the county ordinance covers must carry a Uniform Parcel Identifier number to be recorded. Each parcel numbered costs $20.00, due at recording and payable on one check together with the recording fee.

Your deed's parcel needs that number before the recorder takes the deed, so ask for it before closing day. No number yet? Ring 814-373-2537 and ask how to get the parcel numbered.

One change surprises some sellers: there is no separate check for the realty transfer tax anymore, so it can travel with the other payments. The state levies 1 percent of the value, buyer and seller share liability, and local governments frequently add their own.

How a Crawford County recording works, step by step

A typical sale unfolds in this order. The title agent or attorney drafts the deed and secures the UPI number for the parcel. At the closing table you sign with a notary present, and the buyer's address is added. The agent then adds up the recording fee, UPI fee, any Statement of Value charge and transfer tax, and submits everything on paper or through an e-recording company.

After acceptance the document is indexed and the buyer appears in the searchable records. Selling without a title company? Phone 814-373-2537 to confirm the total, then carry a check for the full sum, because a wrong amount can hold the package up.

Keep copies of the signed deed and the receipt for your own records, since the recorded copy can be ordered later at $0.50 a page. Timing matters as well. The counter closes at 4:30, so plan your drop-off with some margin on a closing day.

  • Indecomm Global Services, at 877-272-5250.

E-recorded Statement of Value forms carry a small added charge. Any document attached to the form costs $0.50 per page, and the system calculates the amount automatically.

Selling a house held by an estate

The Register of Wills sits in the same office, so an heir can open the estate and later record the deed in one place. This office probates estates, collects Pennsylvania inheritance tax and takes the resident inheritance tax returns. Opening an estate takes a death certificate and a $7.00 filing fee.

  • Every estate on file is public record, and estate records from 1991 to the present are online.
  • Probated estates go back to 1800, including most of the old original wills and supporting papers.
  • Will indexes cover 1800 to 1974 and 1975 to 2000.
  • Copies mailed or faxed on written request are $0.50 a page plus fees.

Once the estate has authority to sell, the sale follows the normal recording steps, including the UPI number and a Statement of Value when the transfer is not a paid sale.

The county's estimated population was 81,792 in July 2025, down 2.6 percent from the 2020 base. Meadville is the county seat and the largest city, with Titusville the other city. There are 42,385 housing units, and 74.7 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The median value of an owned home is $153,200, the median monthly rent is $802, and median household income is $60,476. The county issued 99 building permits in 2025.

The 2020 census counted 42,063 housing units, and 19.3 percent of them were vacant. That is a lot of empty housing, so expect buyers to compare your listing with plenty of other choices. Lakeside areas around Pymatuning Reservoir and Conneaut Lake bring a seasonal market of their own.

Seller checklist for closing

A tidy package keeps the deed from bouncing.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the buyer's address.
  • The UPI number for the parcel and $20.00 to cover the fee.
  • A check for the recording fee from the November 17, 2025 schedule, with state and local transfer tax.
  • A Statement of Value if tax is excused or not paid in full.

Recording comes last, but the tax and fee amounts depend on the sale price, so ask the title agent to work out the totals in advance. A cash sale skips the lender's paperwork, yet the deed still needs the same parcel number, notary block and payment before it can go on record.

What is the filing charge for a Crawford County deed?

A deed is $74.75 under the schedule effective November 17, 2025, covering four pages and four names. Extra names are $0.50 each and extra pages $2.00 each.

What is the UPI fee in Crawford County?

It is $20.00 for each parcel that receives a number, paid when the document is recorded. The fee can go on the same check as the recording fee.

Does Crawford County want a check just for transfer tax?

No. The office no longer requires separate checks for the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax.

Can a Crawford County deed be recorded electronically?

Yes. Simplifile, EPN, CSC and Indecomm Global Services are the listed electronic recording companies.

Recorder of Deeds records are online from 1954 to the present, and land records exist back to 1800. For 1954 to 1974, check the index books in the office.

Where Elk County deeds are recorded

Ridgway is the county seat, and St. Marys is the largest city. If you live in St. Marys or Johnsonburg and mail a deed to Ridgway, allow time for delivery. Title companies usually skip the mail by using e-recording, and the office names Simplifile and CSC as its current partners.

The office records, protects and reproduces legal documents for Elk County real estate. It also collects realty transfer tax on behalf of the Commonwealth, the school districts and the municipalities. Records since 1843 are open to the public, except military discharges.

Recording fees

A standard deed costs $92.75 to record on the schedule that took effect December 1, 2025. The price covers four names, four pages and one parcel, and the schedule lists fees apart from state and local realty transfer tax.

Credit and debit cards work through AllPaid for transactions that do not involve realty transfer tax or inheritance tax. AllPaid adds a convenience fee of 2.5% of the transaction, with a $3.99 minimum.

Deed requirements

Title agents and do-it-yourself sellers both run into a short list of rules. Check your document against it before you send it.

  • Leave a 1-inch top margin on every page, because the office stamps recording data automatically.
  • Put the tax parcel identifier (UPI) on any instrument that affects land.
  • State the true consideration on every deed.
  • Pay state realty transfer tax with its own check or electronic payment.
  • Attach an original signed Statement of Value (REV-183) plus a copy if you claim an exemption from tax, unless the deed itself gives the reason.

If the property lies in more than one taxing jurisdiction, the person recording must give the percentage in each. Fees and taxes are due at recording, so the closing agent should bring payment with the package.

Realty transfer tax

The recorder collects state and local realty transfer tax at recording. The state share goes on its own check, separate from the other fees.

Elk County's municipalities and school districts set their own local share, so the rate depends on where the house is. Ask the Recorder of Deeds for the combined rate for your township, borough or the city of St. Marys before you set a net-proceeds figure. The municipal list includes Benezette, Fox, Highland, Horton, Jay, Jones, Millstone, Ridgway and Spring Creek townships, along with Johnsonburg and Ridgway boroughs and St. Marys.

Heirs selling an inherited house deal with the same office, which issues letters and keeps wills. That helps when a deed cannot be signed until someone has authority to act for the estate.

Searching deeds online

Deeds from 1864 to the present can be searched online. Anything older has to be searched at the office. Guests can view records with some information redacted. An account with a credit card lets you save or print an unredacted copy at 50 cents per page, the same price as in the office.

Older books lettered A through Z need four zeros ahead of the letter in the search tool, for example 0000B. A live chat link to the software vendor is on the search page if the tool misbehaves.

Estate paperwork before a sale

The Register of Wills fee schedule effective December 1, 2025 shows what an estate pays before a house can be sold. Letters testamentary or of administration start at $76.25 for an estate not exceeding $1,000 and rise with the value of the estate. That fee includes the $41.25 judicial computer and access to justice surcharge.

  • Probate of a will only: $15.00 for the first page, $2.00 for each added page
  • Short certificates: $5.00 each
  • Certified copy of a will: $10.00 for the first 10 pages
  • Inheritance tax return filing: $15.00
  • Certification of inheritance tax paid, issuing: $15.00

Ask the Register of Wills which filings your estate needs. A buyer's title company will want letters in hand before it closes on a deed signed by an executor or administrator.

Elk County housing

The county's population was estimated at 29,926 in July 2025, down 3.4% from the 2020 base. It has 16,968 housing units, and 79.5% of occupied homes are owner-occupied. The median home value for 2020 to 2024 is $133,600, and median gross rent is $719.

The assessment office has used a 50% ratio since the countywide reassessment of 2005, which took effect in 2006. Its example of total county, municipal and school mills is 16.15 for 2025 and 18.40 for 2026. Assessed value is therefore about half of market value, so do not compare your assessment directly with a sale price.

Steps for a seller

The usual sequence starts at closing, where you sign the deed before a notary. The title agent or attorney adds the UPI, states the true consideration, prepares the Statement of Value if one applies, and writes one check for recording fees and a separate one for state transfer tax. The package then goes to Ridgway by e-recording through Simplifile or CSC, or by courier or mail.

When you sell without a title company, call the office first and ask for the current fee and the local tax rate for your municipality. A cash sale needs the same deed, fees and tax, so allow the same lead time.

Keep your receipt and ask for a copy of the recorded deed. You can find the new record in the online search later, and if the search tool misbehaves, the chat link mentioned above reaches the software vendor. Questions about a rejected package go to the Ridgway office, where the staff can tell you which of the deed rules was missed and what the corrected package needs before it is brought back.

Frequently asked questions

How much does it cost to record a deed in Elk County?

A deed costs $92.75 under the December 1, 2025 schedule, with four names, four pages and one parcel included. Extra pages are $2.00 each and extra names or parcels are $0.50 each.

Where is the Elk County Recorder of Deeds?

It is at 250 Main Street, Ridgway, PA 15853, in the office shared with the Register of Wills and Clerk of Orphans' Court. Mail goes to P.O. Box 314, Ridgway, PA 15853.

Does Elk County accept e-recording?

Yes. Simplifile and CSC are the current e-recording partners. Title companies usually submit seller deeds this way.

Can I pay Elk County recording fees by credit card?

Yes, for transactions that do not involve realty transfer tax or inheritance tax. AllPaid charges a convenience fee of 2.5% of the transaction, with a $3.99 minimum.

How far back do Elk County online deed records go?

Online deed search covers 1864 to the present. Deeds recorded before 1864 must be searched in the office.

title: Wyoming County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax
content:
Wyoming County, PA Recorder of Deeds: Recording a Deed, Fees and Transfer Tax

Cash Home Buyers in Pennsylvania
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Wyoming County, PA Recorder of Deeds: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Wyoming County, PA Recorder of Deeds sale
  • Turn the Wyoming County, PA Recorder of Deeds offer down and you owe us nothing

Selling in Wyoming County? Get a Cash Offer

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326

Selling in Wyoming County?

Who records deeds in Wyoming County, PA?

In Wyoming County a single elected officeholder serves as both Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds, working from the courthouse in the county seat, Tunkhannock. Every deed and mortgage on a county parcel is filed there, alongside estate paperwork.

Counter service runs weekdays from 8:30 to 4:00, with the last filing taken at 3:45 in the afternoon. Call (570) 996-2361 with questions. Only cash and checks are taken. Electronic recording, electronic filing and e-signatures are all unavailable, so whoever closes your sale must hand-deliver or mail the paper deed bearing original signatures.

The recorder's land records start in 1842, when the county was created out of Luzerne County. Papers filed before February 2007 are cited by book and page, while later ones use an instrument number. Either reference will bring up the deed by which you took title, using the online deed search on the county website.

What are the recording fees at the Wyoming County courthouse?

Filing a deed costs $64.75 at base, according to the county's schedule dated December 1, 2025. That amount is good for four pages and four names. A fifth page and beyond adds $2.00 apiece, and extra names beyond four add $0.50 apiece.

Charges for the other papers that tend to accompany a sale appear below. The recorder's website also announced a $20 flat lien search fee and a $30 base fee for maps starting November 1, 2026, and said the full schedule would be revised then, so request the current sheet before writing your check.

Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds base fees, schedule effective December 1, 2025 (source: county fee schedule)
DocumentBase fee
Deed$64.75
Mortgage$64.75
Satisfaction of mortgage$61.75
Release or assignment of mortgage$59.75
Easement$59.75
Affidavit or power of attorney$18.50
Military discharge (DD-214)No charge

Pay the exact sum. Anything over by $5.00 or less stays with the county, a larger overpayment gets the document sent back, and there are no refunds. Checks go to the order of the Wyoming County Recorder of Deeds.

How much is realty transfer tax on a Wyoming County sale?

Expect 2 percent in total, according to the county recorder: one point goes to the state and one point to local government. Harrisburg's Department of Revenue confirms the 1 percent state piece and says recorders gather it along with local tax.

Take a $215,400 price, the same as the county's Census median home value. The tax would come to $4,308. No deed is accepted until the tax is in hand. Here a single check can cover a taxable transaction, with no separate check for the tax.

Gifts inside the family can be exempt: the recorder's FAQ names husband and wife, parent and child, grandparent and grandchild, and siblings. It also suggests talking to an attorney before counting on that. Whenever an exemption is claimed, or the price paid differs from the one printed on the deed, a Statement of Value form must go in with two copies.

What must a deed look like to be recorded in Wyoming County?

Pages that break the formatting or notary rules come back unrecorded, so have the deed checked before it leaves your hands. The published list includes:

  • Ink signatures with a notary acknowledgment that is not dated before the deed. Photocopies are refused.
  • Font size 9 or bigger, half an inch of clear space at the top of each page, black and white only, and no staples.
  • The property's municipality, county and state written out, and a price in words that agrees with the price in figures.
  • A signed certification of address attached to each deed and mortgage.
  • A stamped return envelope, addressed to you and big enough for the original.

No parcel or PIN number is needed on a Wyoming County deed. Two cases add paperwork. A parcel spanning several municipalities calls for a Statement of Value giving the whole-number share of local tax for each. A taxable sale in Windham Township calls for one too, so the school district is correct.

To fix an earlier deed, a corrective or confirmatory deed has to carry a Statement of Value, say why it is being corrected, and attach the old deed. The recorder also points out that it does not vouch for what a document says. Staff confirm only that the rules are met and the fees and taxes are paid.

How soon do I get the deed back, and where can I see records?

A recorded original typically returns by mail about a week later, workload permitting, since staff proof, scan, index and verify each one. Names on a recorded deed cannot be added, dropped or altered by the office. Only a newly drafted deed can do that.

The courthouse computers and the county's online deed search both let you look through the records. Certified copies run $5.00 through eight pages and $0.50 for each page beyond. Staff look up documents by full name only. To trace an owner from a parcel number or street address, turn to the county GIS site or phone the assessment office.

Liens are split between offices. This one records mortgages and UCC filings. Other liens and judgments sit with the Prothonotary, the Clerk of Courts or Orphans' Court, so a seller worried about judgments needs to search those too.

What kind of place is Wyoming County for a house sale?

Rural Wyoming County covers roughly 397 square miles of land in the northeastern corner of the state. The Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 25,790 people, a drop of 1.1 percent since 2020. Five boroughs (Tunkhannock, Factoryville, Nicholson, Meshoppen and Laceyville) sit among the townships, and 95.3 percent of people live in areas the 2020 census classed as rural.

The Susquehanna's North Branch cuts through the county and the ground is hilly, with Mehoopany, Tunkhannock, Knob and Bowman's mountains filling some of it. US 6, US 11 and PA 29 are among the through roads. Tunkhannock averages about 25 degrees in January and 71 in July, so an inspector will look hard at roofs, plumbing and heating.

  • Housing units counted in 2025: 12,989.
  • Share of homes lived in by their owners: 77.9 percent, 2020 to 2024.
  • Middle-of-the-market value for those homes: $215,400.
  • Typical gross rent: $943 a month.
  • Household income at the midpoint: $72,460, with 24.3 percent of people aged 65 or over.

These numbers are. When many owners are older, houses often pass through estates, and the Register of Wills half of this same office handles letters and the inheritance tax forms for them.

Frequently asked questions

Does Wyoming County accept e-recording for deeds?

No. The Recorder of Deeds states that it does not accept e-recording, e-filing or e-signatures. Deliver the paper deed in person or by mail, with original notary signatures and a self-addressed stamped return envelope.

What is the realty transfer tax rate in Wyoming County?

It is 2 percent of the price, split 1 percent state and 1 percent local, according to the county's fee schedule and FAQ. The deed is not accepted until the tax is paid, and the office takes one check for one taxable transaction.

Do I need a parcel number to record my deed in Wyoming County?

No. The recorder says it does not require or certify PIN numbers. It does require the municipality, county and state on the document, and a Statement of Value when land lies in several municipalities or in Windham Township.

How much does the Wyoming County recorder charge for a mortgage satisfaction?

A satisfaction piece is $61.75 on the schedule effective December 1, 2025, which covers four pages and four names. A mortgage release or assignment is $59.75. Lenders usually file the satisfaction, and the recorder cannot do it for you.

Where do I find who owns a property in Wyoming County?

Use the county GIS website or call the assessment office, which can look up ownership by parcel number or address. The recorder can only search by full name, and the online deed search shows recorded documents back to 1842.

Where deeds are recorded in Bedford County

Land documents of every kind, from deeds and mortgages to leases, surveys, financing statements and rights of way, are filed with the Recorder of Deeds side of the combined Register and Recorder office. It occupies Room 106 on the first floor of the Bedford County Courthouse at 200 S Juliana St, Bedford, PA 15522. The phone is (814) 623-4836 and the email is randr@bedfordcountypa.org.

The files reach back to 1771, the year the county was created. Seven public workstations are available for title searchers, lenders and genealogists to browse on their own; employees will not do the searching for you.

Closing agents can e-file through Simplifile and CSC, which is why most sellers never see the counter. FraudSleuth, a free office service, lets owners check that every recording against their property was authorized.

Hours and same-day cutoff

Weekday counter hours are 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., with closures on designated county holidays. For recording, though, the window is 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and the same-day cutoff is 4:00 p.m.

The early cutoff catches people out. If the closing is tight, have the title company submit the deed long before 4:00 p.m. instead of hand-carrying paper in late in the day.

  • Mail goes to Recorder of Deeds Division, Bedford County Courthouse, 200 S Juliana St, Room 106, Bedford, PA 15522.
  • Every mailed filing needs a self-addressed stamped envelope for return of the documents.

Recording fees

The fee bill effective November 20, 2025 sets a deed at $59.75. State and county taxes the schedule folds in are part of that number, which is calculated for a document of up to four names and four pages. Past that, add $0.50 per name and $2.00 per page.

Bedford County recording fees, effective November 20, 2025
DocumentFee
Deed$59.75
Mortgage$59.75

Pay the exact amount. Refunds are not possible. An overage of $5.00 or less stays with the office, and a bigger one sends the document back. A single check may cover no more than five documents.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Bedford County house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Realty transfer tax

Two layers of tax apply, each at 1% of the consideration, one state and one local, and both are due as the deed is recorded. Together that is 2%, on top of the recording fee. Payment may be by check, money order, cash, or credit or debit card. Make checks out to the Register Recorder as named on the fee bill.

A single check can cover both the tax and the recording fee. Land that lies in several municipalities or school districts needs a statement on the deed, in whole numbers, of how the local tax divides among them.

  • Deeds must show the true consideration or carry a completed Statement of Value.
  • Deeds, mortgages and assignments all need a signed Certificate of Residence.
  • The county web page links a Common Level Ratio sheet and the realty transfer tax forms.

Bedford County housing

The county seat is Bedford, in ridge and valley country. The 2025 population estimate of 47,480 is close to the 2020 figure of 47,567. There are 23,836 housing units and 19,750 households. Owners occupy 77.5% of homes, valued at a median of $179,000, while median gross rent is $784. New construction is scarce, so most buyers shop existing houses.

Other documents and their prices

Beyond deeds and mortgages, the fee bill lists many real estate and miscellaneous instruments. Most affidavits, agreements, covenants, declarations, notices, restrictions and orders are $18.50. Amendments, cancellations, modifications, subordinations and terminations run $20.50, and leases of 30 years or longer, installment sales agreements, memorandums and oil and gas leases are $59.75.

Maps and plans are priced separately. A plat under 24 inches is $9.00 and one over 24 inches is $13.00. State highway and mining plans are $16.50 for the first page, with additional pages at $3.00. UCC financing statements and their ancillary filings are $100.00 each.

  • Notary public bond and commission: $39.50, which includes the commission tax and writ tax.
  • Notary name change or address change: $18.50.
  • Clean and Green filing: $18.50.
  • Partial release: $61.75.

For a home seller the practical lines are the deed, the mortgage satisfaction and any easement. If a title search turns up an old right of way or an unreleased mortgage, those are the instruments your closing agent will ask the office to record or clear.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bedford County houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Checklist before the deed goes in

Begin with the items that get a deed rejected when absent. Every deed, mortgage and assignment needs a Certificate of Residence completed and signed, and the deed must state the true consideration or come with a fully completed Statement of Value. Fees must be exact, so confirm the number with the office or your closing agent instead of rounding up.

Then decide who supplies the 2% tax and the recording fee, whether a title company runs the closing or you do it privately. Payment comes first; a deed cannot be recorded now and paid for later.

  • Confirm the grantee name and mailing address spelling.
  • Ask which municipality and school district the parcel falls in.
  • Call (814) 623-4836 with questions about the fee bill.
  • Keep a recorded copy for your records after closing.

If the title search finds a problem

Old paperwork sometimes surfaces during a sale: a mortgage that was paid off but never released, or a right of way nobody remembers. Neither one has to stop the closing. Your title agent will ask the recorder to file the missing release or to record the easement properly, and the fee comes out of the settlement figures. The sooner you hand over your own copies of old deeds and payoff letters, the faster these loose ends get tied up. Do not assume the buyer will overlook them, because a lender or inspector often will not.

Getting a copy of a recorded document

Records can be viewed online through the Recorder of Deeds Records Online link on the county page, or at the public workstations in Room 106. Photocopies are $0.25 a page at the counter, pages larger than 11 by 17 inches are $2.00, and a certified copy is $1.00 plus $0.25 for each page.

The office does not take part in title searches and cannot offer legal advice, so ask an attorney what a document means. Originals go back to whoever presented them, unless the filer directs otherwise, and mailed documents must come with a postage-paid return envelope. Military discharge papers are confidential and available only to the service member or a service organization. Recording a DD-214 and any certified copies are free.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a cash sale fits the recording process

A cash buyer still needs the deed recorded, taxed at 2% and filed with a Certificate of Residence. What changes is that no lender is waiting on paperwork, so the title company can often send the deed in as soon as signatures are done. If you still have a mortgage, make sure a satisfaction piece is recorded after payoff, at the fee shown above, so the record shows the loan as paid.

Frequently asked questions

What is the recording fee for a deed in Bedford County?

It is $59.75 for a deed with up to four names and four pages, under the fee bill effective November 20, 2025. Each added name is $0.50 and each added page is $2.00.

Is the transfer tax included in the Bedford County deed fee?

The fee bill says its listed fees include state and county taxes. The realty transfer tax itself is 1% state and 1% local of the consideration, collected at recording, so ask the office how your deed's total is calculated.

Can I record a Bedford County deed electronically?

Yes. The office accepts e-recording through Simplifile and CSC, along with mail and in-person filing. Most sellers leave this to the title company.

When does same-day recording stop in Bedford County?

Same-day recording stops at 4:00 p.m. even though the office stays open until 4:30 p.m. Call (814) 623-4836 if a closing is running late.

Does the Bedford County office return my original deed?

Yes. Originals go back to the person who presented them unless the office is told otherwise, and mailed documents need a postage-paid return envelope.
